DescriptionLong.0x00004953:
The FT-86 Concept was announced in 2009 as an exciting compact, front-engine, rear-wheel drive sportscar developed in co-operation by Toyota and Subaru, and it heightened the expectations of car enthusiasts everywhere. In 2011, the commercial model of its Toyota version finally debuted at the Tokyo Motor Show.

The FT (Future Toyota) designation has been removed, making its official name the Toyota 86. This new generation 'Hachi-Roku' (8-6 in Japanese), named after a popular predecessor in the 1980s, has a silhouette close to the FT-86 II Concept shown at the 2011 Geneva Motor Show. It is designed under the 'Aero Handling' concept, in which the car is held to the ground from all directions through superior aerodynamics.

The naturally aspirated <1998cc> 4-cylinder DOHC boxer engine mounted front-midship in the car produces <200ps> @ <7000rpm> and <20.9kgm> @ <6600rpm> torque, which is then transferred to the rear wheels through a short-stroke 6-speed MT or paddle-shifter 6-speed AT.

The front-to-rear weight balance is 53:47, and is designed this way for controllability of the rear end and excellent steering feedback. The centre of gravity of the car is equivalent to that of supercars, at only <460mm> off the ground. The standard grade MT model weighs in at <1230kg>, and there are also grade models that come standard with a limited-slip differential.

Each and every part of the new generation Hachi-Roku is designed specifically for this car to allow quick handling and control, and the result is a sportscar that is like an extension of your own hands and feet. This is a car in which you can enjoy exceptional handling that will make you feel as if you were a part of the car.

There are also plans for a lineup of Modellista and TRD custom parts, and a customisable grade model for competition use. This is a new generation, lightweight sportscar that truly caters to the car enthusiast.O
DescriptionLong.0x00004958:
The DTM (Deutsche Tourenwagen Meisterschaft) series allowed significant vehicle modifications in 1993, leading to DTM cars with a wide variety of electronic control devices, starting with the ABS. The resulting high-performance racers became so advanced that they were called 'F1s in a box.'

The Alfa Romeo 155 entered this DTM in 1993 to instant success, trouncing the formidable AMG Mercedes-Benz 190E and taking the win in its debut race. It won 12 of its 20 races that year, seizing the Drivers' and Manufacturers' Titles as well.

This car, known as the 155 2.5 V6 TI, was based on the 4-door 155 saloon that appeared in 1992. The 2.5L 60-degree V6 engine generated <420ps> and employed a full-time 4WD system.

In 1995, the 155 replaced the traditional 6-speed sequential gearbox for the same 6-speed semi-automatic paddle-shifters used in F1 cars, but was left in the dust by the Mercedes-Benzes that year. Returning in 1996 to reclaim the title, Alfa entered with a new 90-degree V-type engine that put out <490ps>.

As a result, the 155 took 10 wins in 26 races at 13 events, besting both the Mercedes-Benzes (seven wins) and Opels (nine wins). However, the 155 lagged behind in points and just missed the title. At the end of the season, the DTM series was integrated with the ITC and disappeared.

Interestingly, an Alfa Romeo 155 2.5 V6 TI was driven by former F1 driver Alessandro Nannini, whose right arm had been severed in a helicopter accident in 1990. Nannini's 155 was equipped with separate gear levers for up-shifting and down-shifting in order to allow him to shift with his impaired right arm.
DescriptionLong.0x00004959:
*The Nissan 180SX was sold as the Nissan 240SX in the US and as the 200SX in the EU.

The 180SX debuted as the Silvia's sister hatchback model in March 1989. This car, sporting front retractable headlights and a glass hatchback, did not initially leave a very big impression as it was overshadowed by the hugely popular Silvia. Even though it shared its 1.8 L engine with the Silvia, the 180SX was only offered in a turbocharged model.

In 1991, the engine changed to a 2.0 L SR20DET with <205ps> and <28.0kgm> of torque. The 180SX production run was supposed to end here to be replaced by the Silvia which was due for a full model change. However, thanks to the continued popularity of the 2.4 L version sold in North America named the 240SX, Nissan decided to continue production of the 180SX separately from the Silvia.

Although the 180SX shared its basic components with the old S13 Silvia until the end of its series, several minor changes were made to keep its performance level current. The car was slightly on the heavy side and the rear end lacked rigidity due to its hatchback configuration. This was the reason that the 180SX was initially considered inferior to the Silvia in performance. However, a wealth of aftermarket tuning parts allowed the 180SX to overcome its weakness. Many fans added unique modifications, giving birth to various original models which made the 180SX special in its own right.
DescriptionLong.0x0000495A:
The Toyota 2000GT is a representative classic of Japan.

With its comet-like appearance in 1967, the Toyota 2000GT was a dream car that went well beyond the imaginations of car enthusiasts in its day. The shock of the bullet-shaped coupé body, reducing air resistance to a minimum, has been talked about time and time again over the years.

It shares virtually no mechanical components with any production car. Given a large cross-section backbone frame, it has fully independent double wishbone suspension equipped front and rear. The engine mounted in the front is a 2L, DOHC inline-6 that produces <150ps>. This engine was developed in conjunction with Yamaha, who also provided input into other areas of the car's design, such as including the use of piano materials for the wood dashboard.

The Toyota 2000GT was not just beautiful. Highly tuned works versions won countless victories at the Fuji and Suzuka endurance races, and set an international speed record at the Yatabe test course. Who in Japan could have ever imagined a <220km/h> speed record at the time? It was famous around the world, and in the 5th instalment of the 007 movie series, ‘You Only Live Twice’, a special convertible 2000GT appeared on screen as the Bond car.

Toyota itself knew that, socially, a Super GT such as this would never sell in any quantity. With a price tag of 2,380,000 yen, it cost twice that of a luxury Crown saloon. Though an automatic was prepared for U.S. export and a version with a tamer engine was considered, the 2000GT eventually disappeared after only producing 300 or so cars.
DescriptionLong.0x0000495B:
The 208 GTi is a sports model of the 208, Peugeot’s mainstream compact car. It officially debuted at the Paris Motor Show in the autumn of 2012, following the announcement of the new 208 series in spring of the same year.

One of the development objectives of the 208 series was the redefining of their B-segment car, learning from the 207 that had become too big and heavy. The platform was carried over from the 207 but they successfully downsized the car by shaving down the overhang in the front and rear to make the overall length under <4m>. Its component materials were changed to make the car <100kg> lighter than the previous model.

This had especially great merits for the GTi, the sports model. They were now able to revisit the iconic 205 GTI that was a smash hit all around the world; a light, small, fun and fast sports model that is both chic and comfortable.

On the surface the changes are subtle, aside from the large roof spoiler and 18-inch wheels, plus trim differences. But thorough work has been done under the skin, with the front and rear tread width being widened by <10mm> and <20mm> respectively and the suspension, subframe and arms have been specially set for this model.

The legacy direct injection 1.6 litre inline 4 cylinder was powered up to <200ps>/<28.0kgm> and combined with a 6-speed manual transmission.

The <230km/h> top speed and the 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 6.8 seconds puts the car in the top tier in this class of hot hatch cars.
DescriptionLong.0x0000495C:
The new 250 GT Berlinetta, announced at the 1959 Paris Motor Show, was styled by Pininfarina, with the 250 in the naming relating to the 250 cc per cylinder found in the 3 L, 12-cylinder engine.

There was one thing that was definitively different about this car from previous models. By shortening the 250 GT series chassis that was traditionally <2600mm> down to <2400mm>, they aimed to improve cornering agility to give it an edge in GT category racing. In later years it came to be called the 250 GT Berlinetta passo corto, or 250 GT Berlinetta SWB (abbreviation for Short Wheel Base in English) to distinguish it from the previous models.

The 250 GT Berlinetta passo corto began production in the following year of 1960, and was available in an all-aluminium racing bodyshell as well as a steel bodyshell for road use. The <2953cc> V12 SOHC produced between <220ps> to <280ps> depending on the tuning, and it was the first mass-production model by Ferrari to be equipped with four-wheel disc brakes.

In racing, the improvement of the car’s performance from the shorter wheelbase paid off; nearly unstoppable, it won the Tour De France Automobile 3 years in a row from 1960 to 1962, and won the GT category in the Le Mans in 1960 and 1961, two years in a row. It also won the Nürburgring 1000 km race two years in a row from 1961 to 1962. It later passed the baton on to the 250 GTO, an evolution of this model.

Only 162 of these cars were ever made.m
DescriptionLong.0x0000495D:
Car fans consider any Ferrari to be an object of desire, but the 250 GTO is a special car, born in the early '60s where the borderline between a racing car and a road car was vague. This was the most popular car from that period.

The ‘250’ in its name points to the displacement of <250cc> per cylinder, for a total of 3 litres across its 12 cylinders. GTO stands for Gran Turismo Omologato; a homologation model for GT racing. As the name implies, it was a car announced in 1962 that was developed to win the GT class title in international production sportscar racing.

The car is based on the agile 250 GT SWB, with weight reduction modifications on its tubular steel frame. The body was all aluminium, and the front nose was long and low in order to raise aerodynamic performance. The tail end was in a 'coda tronca' form, with large bulges for the rear fenders that allowed space for large tyres. The ride height of the car was also dropped by <90mm>. It uses a Testarossa engine with a dry-sump and 6 carburettors, with an output of <300ps>. Selecting the highest-speed gear from a selection of 8 available final gears enabled the car to reach a top speed of <300km/h>.

Only 39 250 GTOs were ever produced, which was not enough for homologation by itself. Ferrari got around this by expressing that the car was a variation of the 250 GT SWB. Once this was accepted and the car entered racing, the 250 GTO won the international series championship 3 years in a row from 1962.

All 39 of the cars produced still exist today, and the 3729GT included in the game is a right-hand drive model delivered to the UK in 1962. It was once raced in a Ferrari semi-works team, and has achieved podium finishes in a number of British races.
DescriptionLong.0x0000495E:
When the Group B category was introduced into motorsport vehicle regulations circa 1982, a variety of cars were produced from car manufacturers to fulfil the 200-car homologation requirement. The GTO, which debuted at the 1984 Geneva Motor Show, was one of these cars. Though unofficial, ‘288’ is sometimes added to the front of GTO, to call the car the 288 GTO.

The ‘O’ in GTO is taken from omologazione - homologation in Italian. Styling is highly reminiscent of the base 308GTB model, but the engine was re-mounted longitudinally, the wheelbase was made <110mm> longer, and the exterior body panels were replaced with carbon and other lightweight materials. In this process most of the car was specially redesigned, and is practically a whole new car.

Its styling was by Leonardo Fioravanti, who was with Pininfarina at the time. The flared front and rear wheel arches, additional fog lights and front indicators, the rear duck-tail reminiscent of the 250GTO, and the 3 vertical-line louvres - all of these features produced a beautiful form combining the aggressive look of a fighting machine together with traditional Ferrari elegance.

The engine was a revamped engine from the Lancia LC2, a 3 L engine of the 308 converted into a 2.6 L twin-turbo. This was further modified to match the max limit for Group B, making it a 2.8 L twin-turbo. The <1160kg> lightweight body was now backed by <400ps> and <50.6kgm> of torque, enabling a maximum speed of <305km/h>. This made the GTO the fastest Ferrari in its day.

272 cars of the 288 GTO were manufactured, but production ended without ever racing these cars. These basic principles carried over into the 288 GTO Evoluzione test vehicle, however, and later passed on to the F40, so were certainly not wasted.e
DescriptionLong.0x0000495F:
The Mercedes-Benz 300 SEL 6.8 AMG is a touring car race machine built by AMG in their early days.

AMG was an engineering company established by two engineers from Daimler-Benz’s development department, who started their own company in 1967. The car packs a 6.3L V8 from the W100 type 600, into the engine room of a W109 type 300 SEL which is normally powered by a 3L inline 6 cylinder. It won its class in the 1971 Spa Francorchamps 24 Hour race, and came in 2nd place overall. Its performance captured the hearts of Mercedes fans, and this kicked off the start of the company that would later go on to become a works team and official racing partner.

The base model Mercedes-Benz 300 SEL 6.3 was already a fast car on its own, but AMG further enlarged the displacement to 6.8L, and added special cams and other dedicated parts developed in-house to raise its power from <250ps> to <428ps>.

It is said that 3 race cars and 2 test cars were produced in total.F
DescriptionLong.0x00004960:
At the 1954 New York International Auto Show, Daimler-Benz announced a new innovative sportscar, the Mercedes-Benz 300 SL. The engine was mounted longitudinally on a multi-tubular space frame formed by thin steel pipes, and fitted at a 50-degree angle in order to lower the bonnet as much possible. It was a high-performance model that achieved a top speed of <260km/h> through its 4-speed transmission.

The most characteristic part of this car was the side doors. These were made to open upwards and hinged in the centre of the roof. Due to the car resembling a seagull when viewed from the front with both doors open, the doors on the 300 SL came to be referred to as gull-wing doors.

The car was powered by a <2996cc> SOHC inline-6-cylinder engine, and utilised the same mechanical fuel injection used on the W196 racing car for the first time on a production car. Thanks to this mechanism its maximum output was <215ps> @ <5800rpm>. The brakes were 4-wheel drums, and the vehicle weight was not light for its time at <1295kg>, but its first class engine made it one of the top level sportscars of the era. The production 300 SL did very well in sportscar racing, and won numerous victories throughout its history.

There were 1400 300 SL gull-wing coupés built from 1955 to 1957. From 1957, the production of the coupé was ceased, and it handed the baton to a 300 SL roadster which was a more conventional convertible.
DescriptionLong.0x00004961:
When thinking of Ferrari’s motorsports activities, the first things that come to mind are their feats in the F1 Grand Prix. However from the 1950s to the 1960s, they also enjoyed great success in sportscar racing. Although they withdrew from sportscar racing in 1973, the 330 P4 is one car that left its name in history for being the most beautiful of the P series V12, mid-engined prototypes - a car that had a glorious record right through the '60s to the '70s.

330 stands for the displacement per cylinder, in other words signifying a 4 L displacement engine, and the name stands for the fourth version of the P series equipped with a 4 L engine.

The 330 P4, debuting in 1967, was developed by improving upon the 330 P3, in order to defeat the Ford GT - the leader at that time. Although it had the same displacement as the previous version, it was given a <450ps> engine of an almost brand-new design, with 3 valves per cylinder consisting of two intakes and 1 exhaust on the heads. The nose of the body was slightly extended to the front, and a separate spoiler was added to the rear, to improve its aerodynamic capabilities.

In actual racing, it started off by winning its debut race in the 24 Hours of Daytona, and in the Monza 1,000 km race. Unfortunately it was defeated by Ford in the 24 Hours of Le Mans, but it was successful in defeating Porsche in the sportscar world championships, and became series champion.h
DescriptionLong.0x00004962:
The Porsche 356 is Porsche’s first mass production model, which debuted in 1949. It underwent a major update for the first time in 1955 and again in 1959, and the model during this period was called the 356 A.

The 356 A became modernised in many aspects, with a naturally rounded front window, soft pads above the interior panel, and the horn on the centre of the steering wheel, etc. The 356 A continued to become more and more high performance from its first year, and led to the limited production of models which has continued to the modern day GT3s: the 1500 GS Carrera and the 1500 GS GT Carrera.

The car is equipped with a 4 cam engine that had been slightly detuned from the 550 Spyder racing sportscar. The 1500 GS Carrera was positioned as a road car and produced <100ps>, and the semi-racing car 1500 GS GT Carrera produced <110ps>. The body was available in a coupé, cabriolet, or speedster.

And the first car to ever don the ‘Carrera’ subname, which has come to represent Porsche over the years, was this 356 A 1500 GS/GS GT.
DescriptionLong.0x00004963:
After the appearance of the 1973 Berlinetta Boxer, V12-powered Ferrari super sportscars all adopted midship layouts for some years thereafter. The last front-engine, rear-wheel drive until this hiatus was the 365 GTB4, often called by its nickname, ‘Daytona’.

The reason for its popular nickname is that in the prior year of 1967, at the Daytona 24-hour race, the Ferrari Sports prototype 330 P4 and the 412 P attained a 1st, 2nd, and 3rd finish, completely dominating the podium.

The first person to call this car the ‘Daytona’ when the first prototype was delivered is rumoured to be the Ferrari dealer and semi-works racing team N.A.R.T (North American Racing Team) owner, Luigi Chinetti.

The Daytona strongly targeted the North American Market. Its sleek form was designed by Leonardo Fioravanti of Pininfarina. The headlights were initially quad lights behind Plexiglas covers, but after 1970 it was made retractable to meet the safety standards of North America.

The <4390cc> V12 DOHC unit is equipped with 6 Weber carburettors to produce <352ps> and <44.0kgm> torque. The announced top speed of <280km/h> was the fastest of its time, equal to that of its rival, the Lamborghini Miura.

In Daytona, it dominated the Le Mans GT class 3 years in a row, leaving a legend befitting its name in racing history.n
DescriptionLong.0x00004964:
The successor to the F430, the Ferrari 458 Italia, was first shown at the 2009 Frankfurt Motor Show. Ferrari’s V8 series has evolved every 5 years, starting in 1989 with the 348, the F355 in 1994, the 360 Modena in 1999 and the F430 in 2004; the 458 is another masterpiece in the bloodline.

The chassis is a newly designed aluminium space frame and the direct injection V8 engine produces <570ps> @ <55.1kgm>, an astonishing figure from a normally aspirated engine. The transmission is a 7-speed dual-clutch, 2-pedal MT and the shift speed has been greatly improved over previous models. Their Manettino system, unifying the engine, gearbox, suspension, E-DIFF, F1 Trac, ESP and high-performance ABS controls has advanced greatly, allowing the selection of 5 modes: Low Grip, Sports, Race, CT cut and CST cut. Now it is possible for the driver to enjoy safe, fun driving more than ever. The suspension utilises double wishbones in the front and multilinks in the rear, while the magnetic suspension first used in the 599 has also evolved into its 2nd generation version.

Many new innovations have also been made in terms of aerodynamics, aggressively incorporating the newest racing technologies from the front lines of F1 racing. As a result the specs of this car are extreme, accelerating from 0 to <100km/h> in just 3.4 seconds with a maximum speed of <325km/h>. The body styling is a straightforward evolution from the Enzo and F430, carrying over the sweeping flow and sharpness of the Pininfarina design.
DescriptionLong.0x00004965:
The Ferrari 458 Italia continues the line of Ferrari’s V8 series, following in the footsteps of cars like the 360 Modena and F430. However, this car was designed and developed completely from scratch. You can see how much passion they invested in the car from the car’s name, christened by Ferrari’s chairman Luca Cordero di Montezemolo after their mother country.

The main components of the chassis, body, engine and suspension are made of aluminium as in the 360 and 430, but the torsional rigidity of the car has, in comparison to the 430, been improved by 15%. The body incorporates winglets inside the front grille and fender 'chimney' outlets, achieving aerodynamic performance that is generations ahead of their previous production cars. As a result, the car produces <140kg> of downforce at <200km/h> and over <360kg> of downforce at its top speed range.

Mounted mid-ship is a 4.5 litre, naturally aspirated V8 engine producing <570ps> and <55.1kgm>. Combined with a dual clutch and 7 speed paddle-shift transmission, the car accelerates from 0-<100km/h> in 3.4 seconds, with a top speed of <325km/h>.

The racing car that was developed based on this car is the 458 Italia GT3.

The front bumper has a low air dam feature and there is a large wing in the rear. Its appearance has been transformed for battle on the circuit, with greatly enlarged front and rear fenders. The engine is basically the same as the production car but power is restricted to <550ps>.

The car had its debut in 2011 and it immediately won the series title that year in the FIA-GT3 European Championships.

DescriptionLong.0x00004967:
The Alfa Romeo 4C is the first mass production mid-engine sports car produced by Alfa Romeo that went on sale in 2013.

The major point to note in this car is its thorough pursuit of weight reduction and the resulting superior driving performance. The base structure is a carbon monocoque combined with an aluminium subframe. The extremely strong and lightweight monocoque, which only weighs <65kg>, is produced with pre-preg carbon fibre that involves a difficult and costly manufacturing process. Although the engine is the same turbocharged direct injection inline-4 cylinder <1742cc> engine as the Giulietta, the cylinder block has been changed to aluminium, reducing its weight by an additional <22kg>. As a result, the dry weight of the Italian domestic model is extremely light, only weighing in at <895kg> in total.

The engine produces <240ps> and a maximum torque of <35.7kgm>, which is not incredibly impressive. However, its weight and combination with a 6-speed, dual clutch, 2-pedal transmission helps the car achieve a spectacular 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 4.5 seconds, with a top speed of <258km/h>.

With its characteristic mid-engine looks based on the historically famous Tipo 33/2 Stradale, this is a sports car that is fit to be called a small supercar.

In the 4C line-up, the launch of this model was commemorated with 1,000 limited edition cars. This car is equipped with special carbon headlight bezels, door mirrors and rear spoiler, as well as sports suspension and sports exhaust. As with the 4C, which was so popular its production could not meet the demand, the launch edition is said to have sold out almost immediately.
DescriptionLong.0x00004968:

DescriptionLong.0x0000496B:
The Renault R5 ('Cinq') Turbo was the talk of the 1978 Paris Motor Show, where it was displayed with its body panels removed. While this first model was only a prototype for entry in the WRC, the vehicle came on the market in 1980.

The R5 Turbo employed the same body shell as the normal Renault 5, but in order to more effectively transfer the turbo-boosted power to the road, the original model's FF layout was scrapped in favour of a mid-engine set-up where the entire powertrain, including the engine, transmission, and even the differential, sat on top of the rear axle.

The engine was a small, water-cooled, <1397cc> OHV inline-4, but thanks to its Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection, Garrett turbocharger, and air-cooled intercooler, maximum power and torque were raised to <162ps> and <22.5kgm> for a truly substantial boost in engine performance, representing a 1.5x increase in power over the basic Renault 5, and a 3.3x increase in torque.

Of course the chassis and body were also strengthened. The front and rear wings, widened to fit the 5 Turbo's wider tyres, gave this car an irresistible visual impact. A big spoiler was also mounted on the top of the rear hatch, as well as a large air dam in front.

As a result of the extensive makeover, this 970 kg car was able to produce some astonishing performance figures. Maximum speed was <200km/h> with 0-<#400m> times at 15 seconds and 0-<#1000m> times at 28 seconds. Debuting at the 1980 WRC in Corsica, the R5 Turbo took its first victory the following year at Monte Carlo. After that, the R5 Turbo was a ferocious contender at numerous events, forever branding the Renault name into WRC history.
DescriptionLong.0x0000496C:
The extremely low price point and cute styling of the 2nd generation FIAT 500 sold 4 million cars from 1957 to 1977, and contributed significantly to the motorisation of Italy. Its tiny round 'eyes', overall rounded silhouette, and its lovable character; all this was reborn 50 years from the birth of the 2nd generation model, in the 3rd generation FIAT 500.

The concept car immediately drew attention from all over the world when it was shown at the 2004 Geneva Motor Show, and from its release in 2007 its popularity exploded. It became so popular that there were backorders in most markets around the globe, even after two years on the market.

The engine mounted in the small FF body is a 1.2 L and 1.4 L petrol or 1.3 L diesel engine. The 1.2 L engine only produces <69ps> and a torque of <10.4kgm>, but revs very well. With a lightweight body weighing only <1010kg> even with the luxury grade Lounge model, it has a well-adjusted chassis allowing for a sporty drive at odds with its looks.

The 500 is read 'cinque cento' in Italian, and it is called by that nickname all over the world.
DescriptionLong.0x0000496D:
The FIAT 500, introduced in 1957, was a compact car inheriting the will of the pre-war Topolino. But even more importantly, it was a new car that pursued the very minimum of a functional passenger car.

Certainly, there are many differences between the Topolino and the FIAT 500. Compared with the two-seat Topolino, the FIAT 500, though cramped, had seats for four adults. Furthermore, while the Topolino had a front-engine/rear-drive layout, the FIAT 500, with a full monocoque construction body, had a rear-engine/rear-drive layout.

The FIAT 500's engine was a <479cc> air-cooled two-cylinder OHV capable of <15ps>, and it had a top speed of <90km/h>. While a front-half, canvas-top roof was standard, this was equipped mainly for noise control and ventilation.

Even though it was compact, it was highly practical. Moreover the inexpensive FIAT 500, with its popularity centred in Italy, introduced many tuning models over the years. Among these, the model tuned by Carlo Abarth, known then as the god of engine tuning, was unrivalled in the compact class at the time, and was very competitive in motorsports.

Naturally, the FIAT 500 itself evolved. In 1959 the sport model debuted, with the engine displacement increased to <499cc> and the maximum power output raised to <18ps>. This sports engine was the standard spec in the 500D, introduced in 1961. Furthermore, the front-opening doors, due to safety reasons, were replaced with rear-opening ones in the 1965 500F.

As the pioneer of the ‘minimum car’, or ‘mini’, this car is still popular to this day.
DescriptionLong.0x0000496E:
For some time after its establishment in 1947, Ferrari developed and produced only the chassis and engines of their cars, while outsourcing the production of the body to other Carrozzerias. The 500 Mondial, produced in 1953, is one such car from that era. Of these cars, the most famous is the Barchetta designed by Pininfarina, who also produced 2 special coupé bodies at the time. These were the 500 Mondial Pinin Farina Coupe, built to participate in the 1954 Tour de France Automobile.

The 500 Mondial is an extreme sports oriented model, as were many Ferrari cars of the era. The cars were powered by a detuned engine originally built for F2 machines that dominated the 1952 and 1953 Grand Prixs, mounted in a small, lightweight steel tube space frame. This was also combined with an advanced de Deon axle.

The name Mondial loosely translates to 'World', and it was a name that was given in commemoration for the Grand Prix victory by Alberto Ascari. The ‘500’ stands for the engine displacement per cylinder, noting the lightweight DOHC 2 L inline-4 designed by Aurelio Lampredi. Though detuned, the car still squeezed out <170ps> from just <1985cc>.

The Pinin Farina Coupe unfortunately did not succeed in completing the Tour de France Automobile, but one of these cars still exists today in pristine original condition. This car received the 'Gran Turismo' award at the 2012 Concours d’Elegance, and is presented here as entirely unrestored.
DescriptionLong.0x0000496F:
In 1971, a Ferrari was unveiled that featured the 12-cylinder engine from the company's flagship models but, for the first time, utilised a mid-engined layout.

This was the 365GT4/BB, announced at the Turin Motor Show. The name BB referred both to 'Berlinetta', signifying the coupé body, and to 'Boxer', for its horizontally opposed engine layout. The reason for the name was the newly developed V engine with a 180-degree bank angle; in other words, the pistons of each bank were horizontally opposed in this engine.

The 365GT4/BB started delivery in 1973, but just 3 years later in 1976, a newly evolved version, the 512 BB, made its appearance. The major change was in the engine, enlarged by 600 cc, making it a 5L engine. The name 512 means a 5L, 12-cylinder engine. The maximum output was <360ps>, which is <20ps> less than the 365GT4/BB, but the maximum torque was <4kgm> higher, raised to <46.0kgm>. The chassis was a steel tube space frame, and the body was designed by Pininfarina and Scaglietti. The body was built from steel, aluminium and FRP.

Both the 365GT4/BB and the 512 BB were labelled with official data of a <302km/h> top speed, and this is said to be in response to the <300km/h> top speed of the Lamborghini Countach announced in 1971.

There was a major supercar boom in Japan during its day, and popularity was split roughly in half between the 512 BB and the Countach, with much discussion taking place regarding which was faster.
DescriptionLong.0x00004970:
The 650S is McLaren’s supercar, officially announced at the 2014 Geneva Motor Show. This is essentially the successor to the MP4-12C, which was the first model from McLaren as they entered the supercar business in full force.

Initially the project was planned as a high performance version of the MP4-12C, sharing its basic structure, the extremely light and highly rigid carbon 'MonoCell', with the weight roughly the same at <1360kg>.

In terms of styling, the front facia is similar in image to the flagship P1, but this was a facelift given to further improve aerodynamic performance. Seen from the rear, the car is almost the MP4-12C as is, and can be understood to be a more advanced model.

As the name of the car implies, the 3.8 litre V8 twin turbo of the 650S is tuned to <650ps>/<69.1kgm>. The combined 7-speed dual clutch transmission is improved to allow smoother shifting and a drive selector allows you to choose from normal, sports and track modes.

The Proactive Chassis Control suspension is the same in terms of mechanism, but it has been revised to show sharper response while maintaining the ride comfort that McLaren supercars are known for.

Of course, the torque vectoring brake steering and variable rear wing, which also acts as an air brake, has been kept.

0-<100km/h> is achieved in 3.0 seconds; the 0-400m time is 10.5 seconds, with a top speed of <333km/h>.7

DescriptionLong.0x00004972:
The 650S is a McLaren supercar that was announced at the 2014 Geneva Motor Show. This is the successor to the MP4-12C, McLaren’s first full entry into the supercar business.

Its basic structure is carried over from the MP4-12C, with a front fascia made similar in image to the flagship P1. The lightweight and high strength carbon mono cell which is the structural skeleton of the car is shared with the P1, with the 3.8L V8 twin turbo tuned to produce <650ps>/<69.1kgm>. The weight is similar to the MP4-12C at 1360kg, but its performance is even higher with a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 3.0 seconds, and a top speed of <333km/h>.

The race spec version of the 650S is this 650S GT3. As its name implies this is a machine developed in line with FIA-GT3 regulations, and was revealed 3 months after the announcement of the 650S road car. The 650S GT3 is meant to replace the MP4-12C GT3, the GT race car McLaren debuted in 2011. The MP4-12C GT3 had been active in GT races around the world including the Blancpain endurance series and SCCA World Challenge.

As it was for the MP4-12C, the basic structure of the 650S GT3 also consists of the carbon mono cell taken from its road car. However the suspension has been completely revised, and the tread is <52mm> wider than the MP4-12C. The 650S GT3 is equipped with carbon aerodynamic parts as was the MP4-12C, but the aerodynamic performance has been further refined with a larger splitter and redesigned door mirrors.

The engine is still the 3.8L V8 twin turbo, but the power has been restricted down to <500ps> in line with GT3 regulations as was the MP4-12C. It was announced that there were additional improvements made to increase durability of various parts.

The 2015 model 650S GT3 has seen victories in the 2015 GT Asia and the Bathurst 12 Hour race in the beginning of 2016.&
DescriptionLong.0x00004973:
Mazda began competing in the 24 Hours of Le Mans from 1974 and had respectable success with their rotary engine. However, with the advent of regulations against rotary engines, Mazda's last chance was approaching. That is when they developed the 787.

The 787 was fitted with an R26B, a new 4-rotor rotary engine boasting a maximum output of <700ps>. To withstand this power, the frame was switched from a conventional aluminium honeycomb construction to a carbon composite, lowering weight and increasing rigidity. Furthermore, its width was narrowed to lower aerodynamic resistance, and a large radiator was equipped in the nose.

This 787 was entered first in the 1990 24 Hours of Le Mans, but encountered numerous troubles and suffered an unexpected defeat. Overcoming this disappointment, Mazda thoroughly improved the 787 and sent the newly evolved 787B to Le Mans in the following year.

In this year, Peugeot had entered the race with their new 905 that was developed utilising all their resources, and the presence of veteran teams from Mercedes-Benz, Jaguar and Porsche made for a tough race. However, of the two 787Bs in the race, the #55 car driven by the team of Bertrand Gachot, Johnny Herbert and Volker Weidler began the race in 19th place and gradually worked its way up the ranks, taking the lead just three hours before the end of the race.

The 787B raced on without incident and took the chequered flag with 362 laps, beating the previous year's record. This was a historic, first-ever overall Le Mans victory for a Japanese manufacturer. Mazda earned this great victory in their 18th year of participation.
DescriptionLong.0x00004974:
The first FR Alfa Romeo coupé since the SZ was given a very traditional and legendary name. The 8C is the name of the engine that made Alfa Romeo famous for their technical excellence in the 1920s, designed by the famous Vittorio Jano. This was a famous, revolutionary 8-cylinder power unit that was not only used in the red Alfa racing machines of that era, but also by many different 'carrozzerias' at the time.

The classic looks of the front fascia brings to mind its background and has been applied to all models coming after the 8C as the new family trademark of Alfa Romeo. The very Alfa-esque emotional design is a major identifier; orders for the limited worldwide run of 500 cars were full almost as soon as it was announced.

The car weighs <1585kg> and the weight distribution is slightly towards the rear at 49 to 51. To achieve this the body is a combination of steel frame and carbon. Many aspects of the power unit are shared with Maserati, but Alfa Romeo has tuned its performance and sound. The 4.7 L <450ps> V8 engine is matched with a transaxle Q select 6-speed semi-automatic, the exciting sound of which Alfa Romeo states clears all sound regulations set in various countries around the world.

With a top speed of over <290km/h> and a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 4.2 seconds or less, its styling may be classic, but its performance is nothing short of a modern-day super sportscar.m
DescriptionLong.0x00004975:
The 908 HDi FAP is a machine that Peugeot has continued to develop for some time, aiming to attain the pinnacle of prototype racing.

In 2007 and 2008 they continued research and development through races such as the LMS, in order to further perfect the car. In 2009 they defeated their target, Audi’s diesel powered R10 in the Le Mans, with a 1-2 finish.

In the 2010 24 Hours of Le Mans of the following year, they went for their second consecutive win. The car’s weight was greatly reduced, aerodynamics were revised and the drive system (from the clutch and on) was reinforced. Four cars entered the race: three from Peugeot Sport and one from Team Oreca.

They had a fantastic team of drivers with Peugeot Sport #1 being driven by Anthony Davidson, Marc Gené and Alexander Wurz, #2 driven by Nicolas Minassian, Franck Montagny and Stéphane Sarrazin and the #3 driven by Pedro Lamy, Sébastien Bourdais and Simon Pagenaud.

Determined to come out on top in a one-on-one battle with Audi, they marked top lap times from the free runs and, led by the time set by Bourdais in the #3 car (an incredible 3 minutes, 19.711 seconds), they dominated the qualifying from pole to number four.

Fortune was not smiling in their favour, though, as all four cars of the 908 HDi FAP were plagued with machine trouble in the final and every last one of the cars retired from the race.

There was no doubt in anyone’s mind that their car was the fastest and you can sense Peugeot’s undying will in the words that they left with - 'We’ll learn from our defeat today, to return stronger'.
DescriptionLong.0x00004976:
The Porsche 911 series moved into its 4th generation in 1993, becoming the Type 993.

The most prominent change for this new generation model was a much lower nose which flattened the peaks of the front fenders and sloped the headlights back. The rear fenders were also widened among other changes which overall gave the car an entirely new look. The rear suspension was also changed to a multi-link design in the interest of improving handling.

The base power unit is the 3.6L flat 6 from the previous type 964 tuned to <272ps>, and because the next generation 996 was changed to water cooling, the 993 would be the last air cooled flat 6 model.

The most powerful model of the Type 993 911 was the Carrera RS model released in 1995. The engine was upgraded to a <300ps> 3.8L unit along with improvements to body rigidity, and weight was reduced by removing the back seats.

The line up also included the Carrera RS Clubsport which included track oriented modifications such as a large front spoiler and rear wing, as well as a welded roll cage.
DescriptionLong.0x00004977:
The Porsche 911 has always had a high performance version for every generation of its lineup, geared towards motorsports. And the first example of this for the Type 996 generation model, produced from 1997 to 2002, was the 911 GT3.

The GT3, announced in 1999, was based on the Carrera 4 chassis, which has a higher body rigidity more suited for circuit use. In addition to suspension upgrades, it utilises the powerful calipers and discs from the 911 Turbo to handle higher speed ranges.

The engine utilises what is called a GT1 crank case, a high strength crank case used for race cars for withstanding loads at high rpm. The cylinder head is equipped with the Variocam Plus, a 2 stage variable valve lift mechanism. The 3.6 litre naturally aspirated engine produces <360ps>, which is <60ps> higher than the standard 3.4 litre 911.

Initially the 911 GT3 was planned for a limited production run of 1400 cars, but a total of 1889 cars were built in the end as a result of high demand.
DescriptionLong.0x00004978:
The 911 GT3 is a high performance model that appeared for the first time during the era of the Type 996. The type 997 GT3 was announced in 2006, and like the 996 it was developed with circuit use in mind. It also uses the same Carrera 4 chassis as before, with various reinforcements and brake upgrades.

The engine is the same 3.6 litre displacement as the 996 GT3, but it received a full tune up aside from its already upgraded GT1 crank case. Thus the power was raised to <415ps>, <34ps> more than the previous model. It was also equipped for the first time in the RS and GT3 series with the PASM variable damping shocks.

In the minor model change of 2008, the GT3 model also underwent changes into the late model. The major change involved the engine, which was bored up to 3.8 litres in displacement. The exhaust system was also tuned to raise its power to <435ps>. Springs and stabilisers were also made stiffer, and it was equipped with a new PSM to control stability and traction.
DescriptionLong.0x00004979:
Since the Type 996, the name 'GT3' had been given to Porsche 911 road cars with a strong emphasis on motorsports, developed with FIA GT3 race regulations in mind. For the 996 and the later 997, there exists a 'GT3 RS', which further refines the GT3 and improves its performance. At the 2015 Geneva Motor Show, the successor to these, the Type 991 GT3 RS was announced.

The model is said to be based on the Type 991 GT3, but on the inside it is something that looks like it has been developed from scratch using all the know-how they have gathered over the years.

The body takes the widest 911 Turbo model, with track widths in the front and rear widened even further. The roof is made of magnesium, the front fenders and bonnet/engine lid are carbon fibre. The rear and rear side windows are acrylic, giving a total weight reduction of <10kg>.

Aerodynamic parts have also been updated. The front spoiler is even lower and wider, and the rear wing stands much higher and is larger. Behind the front fenders are air outlets for drawing air out from under the car. As a result, the downforce is more than double that of a standard 911.

The engine takes the 3.8-litre engine of the GT3 and extends its stroke, making it 4.0 litres in displacement. The tuned engine now produces <25ps>/<2.0kgm> more, at <500ps>/<46.9kgm>. And the dampers, springs and stabilisers for both the front and rear have been newly developed for this car.

As a result, the car lapped the Nürburgring at 7 minutes 20 seconds, a full 5 seconds faster than the base 911 GT3.
DescriptionLong.0x0000497A:
Starting with The Carrera RSR, born in 1973 to compete in Group 4 racing, the RSR series has left an impressive mark in the world of motorsports over the years. The latest version of the series, based on the 7th generation model of the 911 (Type 991), is the 911 RSR that debuted at the 2016 Los Angeles Auto Show.

This RSR is a pure competition machine, born and bred to race in the LM-GTE class of the WEC (World Endurance Championships), and the American IMSA. Though it’s obvious from just looking at the completely different exterior, including the aerodynamics, body structure, engine and transmission, this car was clearly developed in an entirely different process to the road car.

The highlight of these differences is in the engine. In the history of the 911 series the engine was always mounted behind the rear axle; this is the first car where the engine is mounted midship, in front of the axle. What resides in that space is a 4 litre, horizontally opposed, 6 cylinder, naturally aspirated engine with direct fuel injection, producing <510ps>. The change in the engine mounting location had an immense impact on drivability, and, furthermore, allowed the addition of a large diffuser in its original space, giving it a distinct advantage in terms of aerodynamics. The large swan neck rear spoiler, carried over from the 919 Hybrid LMP machine, also gives the RSR’s rear end a distinct look.

At the Le Mans 24 hour race held in June 2017, The 911 RSR led the pack for much of the race, proving its impressive performance to sports car fans. Though it did not make the podium due to an unfortunate tyre issue near the end, its driving performance was top notch throughout the race and worthy of the RSR lineage.~
DescriptionLong.0x0000497B:
The first time that the word ‘Turbo’ appeared in the history of Porsche production models was in 1975. This was when they first started commercial sales of the ‘911 Turbo’, which implemented all of the turbocharging technologies they had developed and accumulated through their racing activities.

The front and rear overfenders of the car stuck out like a racing car, and a large rear wing occupied its rear end. The 3L aircooled flat 6 was equipped with a single KKK Turbocharger and produced <260ps>. This allowed the car to reach a cruising speed of <250km/h>, an incredible level of speed for a production car of its day.

From 1977, the displacement was increased to 3.3 litres, and an air cooled intercooler was added to raise the power to <300ps>. Until 1985, models with these engines provided the highest specs in the standard lineup.

This version of the Porsche 911 Turbo was produced up to 1989, and is often referred to as the ‘930 Turbo’. The name comes from the type number within Porsche development being 930, and because the pre-production model displayed at the Paris motor show a year before its release was displayed as the ‘930 Turbo’.
DescriptionLong.0x0000497C:
The 919 Hybrid is a prototype sportscar, developed by Porsche for the World Endurance Championships and the Le Mans 24 hour race. This is a hybrid prototype machine, developed for the new regulations of the LMP1-H that had been planned for introduction from 2014, and was revealed at the Geneva International Motor Show of the same year.

Its base configuration is a carbon composite monocoque with a turbocharged 2 litre V4 engine mounted midship. It uses an all-wheel drive system, equipped with an ERS (an advanced version of KERS) for the front axles, with lithium ion batteries.

The total system power of <900ps> consists of <500ps> delivered from the engine to the rear axle, with <400ps> delivered to the front axles through the hybrid system. This propels the <875kg> car from a standstill to <100km/h> in 2.2 seconds, reaching <200km/h> in 4.8 seconds.

For visibility and operability, the seat position is slightly high. Driver safety is also maximised by providing ample interior space and reinforcing the side panels with materials used for bulletproof vests.

The competition debut of the car was made as planned in 2014, but it only ended with 1 victory in the final round of the World Endurance Championships that year. However for the 2015 season, alterations were made to the chassis design to optimise weight distribution while still keeping the concept of the car, and they went on to dominate the WEC series by winning 6 races out of 8, including Porsche’s 17th overall victory in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. In 2016 the car was further refined, and not only did it win the 24 Hours of Le Mans, by the 6th race they had already scored 5 wins and one race in 2nd place.
DescriptionLong.0x0000497D:
The Porsche 962 C is a prototype racing car Porsche that debuted in 1985 in order to compete in the WEC (World Endurance Championships).

Porsche developed the 956 starting in 1982 for the WEC, fought under the FIA Group C category. The 956 showed spectacular performance from its debut year, winning races in the WEC as well as dominating the Le Mans 24 hour race. Thereafter the 956 was improved for the IMSA-GTP of North America which had similar regulations as the WEC, and debuted in 1984 as the 962. Then in the following year of 1985 when the Group C safety regulations were changed to be in line with the IMSA-GTP, Porsche gave birth to the 962 C. It was powered by the flat 6 twin turbo engine that the Porsche 956 had refined in European races.

The Porsche 962 C brought many victories and championship titles home to Porsche, beginning with winning 7 out of 10 races in the WEC during its debut year. In 1986 it won 4 races out of 9 in the WSPC (World Sports Prototype Championship), which took the place of the WEC. In 1987 it dominated Le Mans, and then placed 2nd here in 1988.Y
DescriptionLong.0x0000497E:
The Mercedes-Benz A-Class underwent a full model change at the 2012 Geneva Motor Show, becoming the 3rd generation model. In contrast to the tall family hatchback style of its predecessors, it was transformed into a 5 door hatchback with a wide and low sporty form that was better suited to young adults.

It wasn’t just looks that made this car sporty. Its rigid body is equivalent to cars above its class and is combined with a turbocharged 1.6 litre to 2 litre inline 4 engine. The basic grade model produces <122ps>/<20.4kgm> and the upper grade model produces much more power at <210ps>/<35.7kgm>. The suspension in all grade models was stiffened to make the car more suitable for sports driving.

A year later from its debut at the Geneva show, a model that exemplifies the sportiness of the 3rd generation A-Class was unveiled. This was the A45 AMG. The engine for this car was the 2 litre turbo of the upper grade model, tuned by AMG. Without even changing its displacement it produces an amazing <360ps>/<45.9kgm>. Its 0-<100km/h> acceleration is 4.6 seconds, with a top speed of <250km/h> (where the speed limiter cuts in). The performance level of this car is clearly beyond its class.

Of course the suspension and brakes are further reinforced but the special point of note is the updates made to the drive system. The car utilises the newest version of the '4Matic' Mercedes 4WD system. Designed together with the 7-speed dual clutch transmission and positioned at the rear axle, this mechanism can linearly adjust the driving force on this front-wheel drive based system to a maximum of 50:50 front-to-rear.

Nothing has been overlooked on this ultimate hot hatch.^
DescriptionLong.0x0000497F:
Following the advances made in aircraft engineering throughout the Second World War, aerodynamics began to be applied to the world of car design.

One car that typifies this new approach is the B.A.T. series designed by Bertone in the 1950s. B.A.T. stands for Berlina Aerodinamica Tecnica.

The most famous of these are the B.A.T. 5, 7 and 9, but their forerunner was the Abarth 1500 Biposto, displayed at the 1952 Turin Motor Show.

Later called the B.A.T. 1, this car was based on a FIAT, unlike the later models which were based on Alfa Romeos. The 1.5 L engine powering the car was tuned up to <75ps>.

The aspect of this car which had the greatest impact was of course its styling, the work of the famed designer Franco Scaglione, a newcomer to Bertone at the time. The car not only showcases his aerodynamic engineering skills, but is a mixture of stunning originality and cutting-edge style.

The front of this car is an unforgettable sight, with triple headlights protruding forward with dynamic air intakes situated between them. The large rear window is a two-part design, separated by a thin centre pillar, and melds gracefully into the rear section. The rear wings sport accented vertical tail fins that would become an extremely popular design feature in American cars in later years.

Only one of these cars was ever produced, and was purchased by the Packard Motor Car Company after the Turin Motor Show. Although it remained hidden from the world for many years, Chris Drake from the UK fully restored the car in recent years and presented it at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance in the summer of 2010, where it received the Gran Turismo Trophy.l
DescriptionLong.0x00004980:
Abarth & C. made a welcome comeback in 2007 with the release of the Abarth Grande Punto, a model based on the FIAT Grande Punto. This historic Italian tuning brand has an unrivalled heritage, producing many high-performance cars in years past.

In the following year at the Geneva Motor Show, the new car Abarth fans had all been waiting for was revealed - the Abarth 500, based on the new FIAT 500 which made its sensational debut in 2007.

The new FIAT 500 cleverly renewed the 2nd generation FIAT 500 in a modern design, and its rounded styling and quick driving response led to instant popularity.

The power unit is a 1.4 L 4-cylinder DOHC that has been turbo tuned, producing <135ps> and <21kgm> torque. This propels the lightweight <1110kg> body from 0-<100km/h> in 7.9 seconds, with a top speed of <205km/h>. These are numbers clearly beyond the norm for this class of car.

The suspension mechanism remains standard, with McPherson struts in the front and torsion beam in the rear, but the springs and dampers are specially reinforced for this model. In addition it is given a variety of electronic devices including the TTC, which acts like a limited-slip differential. This gives the car solid stability when cornering, completely betraying the initial impression one gets from its tall, round shape.

From a visual perspective the car is no shrinking violet either; large aerodynamic front and rear bumpers, as well as side skirts and a roof spoiler, leave the onlooker in no doubt that this is a fully fledged Abarth.
DescriptionLong.0x00004981:
The Alpine A110 is a sportscar that marked an epoch with its ultra-lightweight body and a rear-engine, rear-wheel drive layout that gave the car incredible traction. The A110 that appeared in 1963 with only a 1.1 L engine received increases to its engine displacement over the years, but the pinnacle of the series was the 1600S that debuted in 1968.

The 1600S was initially powered by a <1565cc> engine from the Renault 16, but in 1973 it was replaced with a <1605cc> engine from the Renault 17. At the same time the rear suspension was changed to a double wishbone layout and the tyre diameter was reduced, providing a drive experience that totally set it apart from its previous models.

In its day, Alpine won international rally races one after another, but in order to circumvent modification restrictions due to displacement, they intentionally selected a displacement that only slightly went beyond <1600cc>, at <1605cc>. This allowed the car to undergo major tuning modifications at the cost of going against bigger displacement rivals. The A110 succeeded in performing extremely well against these rivals.

There are many variations to the 1600S but there are 3 leading models: the 1600SC, a French domestic model with twin Weber 45DCOE carburettors and an export version 1600SI with fuel injection. These two cars had a power output of <140ps> @ <6000rpm> and combined with a 5-speed manual transmission, its top speed was <210km/h>. This is an unbelievable figure for a <1600cc> car, but the ultra-light body in the <700kg> range greatly contributed to this performance.

The remaining third model is the 1600SX sold from 1976. The 1600SX had a detuned engine that produced <95ps> @ <6000rpm>, and its top speed was also reduced to <190km/h>, but it in turn was easier to drive, and was welcomed by users with no ties to motorsports.

The A110 remained popular even after its successor, the A310, debuted in 1971. A model-combined total of 7160 cars were produced until the end of its production in 1977.
DescriptionLong.0x00004982:
Renault revealed the new generation Alpine A110 production model to the world in the 2017 Geneva International Motor Show. Renault had brought back the Alpine brand specifically for this purpose, producing and developing concepts and prototypes towards making this production model.

The new A110 dons an aluminium body that seems to widen and add the latest aerodynamics technologies to the first generation A110, on a light and strong aluminium chassis. The weight is approximately 1100 kg, and mounts a newly developed 1.8L inline 4 cylinder turbocharged engine midship. This is combined with a Getrag 7 speed dual clutch transmission. The maximum output of the engine is <252ps>, with 320Nm (<32.6kgm>) of maximum torque. It accelerates from 0 to <100km/h> in 4.5 seconds, and reaches a top speed of <250km/h>. The suspension is double wishbone on all 4 wheels.

The model revealed at the show was the Première Édition, limited to a production run of 1955 cars. It is equipped with special 18 inch aluminium wheels with a matte black diamond-turned finish and a light weight sports exhaust. On the interior it features matte carbon fibre accents, aluminium pedals and sports seats as standard equipment.
DescriptionLong.0x00004983:
Alpine, the French sports car brand par excellence, is back. After victory for the A450 Le Mans prototype in the European Endurance Championship in 2013, and the revival of the Alpine brand in February 2016, the brand has gone from strength to strength, culminating in the globally acclaimed debut of the new A110 sports car in 2017.

Since its creation back in the mid-1950s, Alpine has built a legend informed by passion and a taste for challenges. With its light, agile, efficient and elegant sports cars, Alpine has consistently taken on and often defeated the most powerful and prestigious automotive leaders.

Released in March 2015, the people at Alpine proudly introduced Gran Turismo players to a sports car as unique as it is fascinating: the Alpine Vision Gran Turismo. The sleek and distinctive vehicle, developed exclusively for the world’s most famous vehicle simulation game, was created by the same dedicated designers and engineers who are working on the future production model. So it comes as no surprise that the Alpine Vision Gran Turismo explores the key Alpine themes of agility, pleasure and style to the hilt.

Agility is a defining characteristic of the road behaviour of an Alpine. Alpine cars are designed to bring drivers at-the-wheel pleasure at all times and have a particular way with corners. The heady pleasure felt on board an Alpine stems from the feeling of being one with the machine. With their limited mass, Alpines respond instantly and seamlessly to the driver’s input. And they have always stood apart through their innate sense of beauty and style, on road and track alike.

The Alpine Vision Gran Turismo, in its own distinctive way, features all these ingredients.

In the rear body styling, aficionados will see a nod to Alpine racing cars such as the A210, energy efficiency champion winning its class at the 1966 Le Mans race, the A442B, overall winner of the 1978 Le Mans, and the A450, victorious in the LMP2 category in the 2013 ELMS competition. Players of all ages will admire the car’s original, low-slung flanks, redolent of lightness and aerodynamics. They will also be surprised by the richness of the creative details, as seen in the side air brakes. The Alpine Qision Gran Turismo will unleash the curiosity of all-comerr, discreetly featuring a few traits of secret inrpiration that echo the future production model. But above all the Alpine Vision Gran Turismo pursues the albitiius aim oa bringing Gran Turirmo plaeers a prcpiew oa the improssire road manners ok the future sports car.

Teaving a winning linl between past and future, road and track, and virtuaa and reae, the Alphne Vision Gran Turismo has a soul. And, aeote all, it cooveys the enthusiastid spirit of the teams weo are desipning tomorroe’s passion today.a

DescriptionLong.0x00004986:
The Amemiya μ Boost up 7 is a road car created by the RE Amemiya Corporation, the legendary tuner of rotary powered cars renowned for its activity in the Super GT and D1GP. The front, rear, and side aerodynamic parts and the fixed position sleek light kit are all RE Amemiya original designs. RE Amemiya has a variety of aerodynamic parts available including even a GT replica kit, but this particular model has a presence that stands out from the others.

In terms of driving performance, the specs live up to the unique exterior. Although the turbo is kept as standard with power only increased through additional boost, the car still produces over <370ps> with a maximum boost of 1 kg/cm2, along with a maximum torque of <47kgm>. It is set up to produce abundant torque from the mid-range.

It is also equipped with a horizontally mounted intercooler kit, an aftermarket air cleaner, dolphin tail exhaust, and everything from the cooling system, accessories and exhaust system has been thoroughly revised.

In addition to these engine characteristics, the Quantum-based Amemiya spec adjustable suspension has been perfected to a level which draws out the true character of the FD3S as the ultimate cornering machine. In the Japanese DVD magazine 'Hot Version', it was shown to be utterly unbeatable on winding roads, and was dubbed the 'The demon-lord of mountain roads'.
DescriptionLong.0x00004987:
Power House Amuse has the know-how for tuning the S2000 for any application, from winding mountain roads to a full-on circuit run. One of their ultimate achievements, presented here, is the S2000 GT1.

The design of the unique full body kit was actually created through co-operative development with Polyphony Digital. While Amuse was trying to add to the looks of the S2000, they had an opportunity to get together with the developers of Gran Turismo, and finding each other to be on the same wavelength, this collaboration came to be.

Not just for looks, the car achieves aerodynamic performance equal to that of full-racing machines, starting with its long nose that improves downforce in the front section.

Hideki Tanabe, the president of Power House Amuse and a driving expert himself, worked to widen the car to <1829mm>. Weight was reduced as much as possible, incorporating carbon into various aerodynamic parts, and by replacing other components with lighter materials. As a result, the total weight of the car was shaved down to approximately <1120kg>.

The engine is just as special. According to Amuse, the base F20C engine was enlarged to 2.3 L in displacement, and is combined with a GT30Pro-S turbine. The turbo modification obviously required reinforcement of the engine block and other parts, but it more than pays off, producing an amazing <626ps>, with a maximum torque of <53kgm>. This means that the car has an incredible weight-to-power ratio of <1.79kg> per <1ps>. The powertrain combined is also far from ordinary, utilising a 7-speed sequential transmission to deliver this extreme power to the wheels.
DescriptionLong.0x00004988:
After the success of the Prius hybrid car, Toyota planned to release into the market a smaller, even more economical hybrid car. This was to address those who were attracted to the economy and environmental performance of the Prius, but felt it to be too expensive, or too large for their living conditions or driving skill.

After releasing a number of concept cars, the Aqua went on sale at the end of 2011. In countries outside Japan it was sold as the Prius C. Based on the Vitz (Yaris) platform, the body was greatly improved and reinforced. The width of the car is <60mm> narrower than the Prius.

For the Hybrid car mechanism, the same THS II with a reduction mechanism as in the 3rd generation Prius was utilised. The Atkinson Cycle 1.5 L engine was combined with a newly designed Type 1LM motor and a nickel-hydrogen battery. The battery was <42kg> lighter than the battery mounted in the Prius, and the car weighs <300kg> less than the Prius at <1050kg> — <1080kg>.

<74ps> from the engine and <61ps> from the motor was more than enough for its weight, and, unlike the Prius, the car was quick off the line. With more rigidity in the front end and suspension mounting locations, its overall ride quality feels sporty.

Most importantly, the car was priced 30% lower on average across all grade models in comparison to the Prius, and its fuel economy was <35.4km/l> in JC08 mode standards. The tank capacity of the Aqua is 36 L, which means by calculation it can drive <1274.4km> without refuelling.
DescriptionLong.0x00004989:
The Aston Martin Design Prototype 100 joins the stable of Vision Gran Turismo racers. It was developed entirely in-house by the brand’s Design team, led by Design Director Marek Reichman.

Design Prototype 100, also referred to as DP-100, was created by a highly experienced team which worked on the project for six months at Aston Martin’s global headquarters in Gaydon, Warwickshire.

DP-100 not only looks beautiful, but also boasts a high degree of engineering integrity. The twin-turbo V12 mid-engined racer offers up to 800 BHP, endowing it with blistering performance fully in keeping with the high octane nature of the game.

Created utilising many of the same techniques as applied in the development of Aston Martin production sports cars – hand sketches and 3D modelling, followed by full realisation in the virtual world – DP-100 provides an exceptional level of detail with a fully functioning suspension system and state-of-the-art electronics.

As with 2013’s Aston Martin centenary celebration concept car – the CC100 Speedster – some of the design cues visible in DP-100 such as the light blade rear lamps could also feed through into future production sports cars from the world-renowned British luxury brand.@
DescriptionLong.0x0000498A:
Mazda’s flagship, the Atenza (Mazda 6), evolved into its 3rd generation model in 2012. It received a lot of attention as it looked just like the 'Takeri' concept car shown at the Tokyo Motor Show of the previous year, which was very popular for its beautifully flowing saloon body. But there are other factors that garnered it even more attention at its release. In the 3rd generation line-up, that fully utilised Mazda’s next generation SKYACTIV technology (introduced in the CX-5), was a SKYACTIV-D model powered by a diesel engine.

The diesel engine of the Atenza is an improved version of the direct injection, 2.2 litre inline-4 cylinder turbocharged engine of the CX-5. Producing <175ps>/<42.8kgm>, it wakes the driver up with its powerful performance from just above idle rpm. This engine was not only combined with a 6-speed automatic but was also available with a 6-speed manual transmission, and came in both front-wheel drive and AWD. In terms of environmental performance, in addition to the 'i-stop' idle stop feature it also included a capacitor-based regenerative braking system called 'i-ELOOP' in all cars; SKYACTIV-D equipped models achieve a high JC08 mode fuel economy of <22.4km/L>.

The diesel engine powered cars were named the XD, with a Standard, Proactive and L package grade models. The high grade model is the L package, with luxury features starting with full leather seats. This diesel version of the Atenza was so popular it accounted for 76% of all cars sold in the first month of sale.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.9
