DescriptionLong.0x0000498E:
The machine that fought to win the GT500 Class for Toyota / Lexus in the 2014 to 2016 seasons of the Super GT Series is the Lexus RC F, based on the production car which started sales in October 2014.

Due to new regulations from 2014, the weight and rigidity of the monocoque and its centre of gravity were matched to that of DTM cars. The dampers, brakes, and rear wing were all made common with the DTM. And because the top half of the body with the RC F silhouette could not be modified in design due to these regulations, downforce is gained by reworking the bottom half. The power unit is a turbocharged 2 litre inline 4 with direct injection: the RI4AG engine. This unit is shared with the Super Formula, and tuned for use in the Super GT.

The 2016 model was the final version of this car. Because of increased constraints of the regulations limiting the fuel restrictor flow from <100kg/h> to <95kg/h>, improvements were made to create more power with less fuel, along with various other improvements to the car.

The au TOM’S RC F, carrying the ace car number 36 of the Lexus Team TOM’S, finished 2nd in round 6 and 3rd in round 3, ending in the series in 5th overall out of 15 cars.
DescriptionLong.0x0000498F:
Audi is making electromobility an extremely thrilling experience with a purely electric-powered racing car of the future.

The Audi e-tron Vision Gran Turismo was initially only fully developed by Audi Design exclusively for the race simulation in the 'Vision Gran Turismo' competition, launched on the occasion of the 15th anniversary of the series. As a further highlight, Audi decided to have the concept car produced by AUDI AG in a prototype construction as a single piece and to use it as the race taxi in the Formula E electric racing series. It is therefore the first virtual concept car in the 'Vision Gran Turismo' series that is fully functional on real race tracks.

The racing car of the future consciously picks up the design elements of the Audi 90 IMSA GTO, with which Audi Sport thrilled fans in the North American IMSA GTO racing series in 1989, with drivers such as Hans-Joachim Stuck, Walter Röhrl, Hurley Haywood and Scott Goodyear. The car was far ahead of its time back then, owing to the combination of the consistent lightweight construction, and the quattro drive, paired with a powerful five-cylinder turbo engine.

The Audi e-tron Vision Gran Turismo is also ahead of its time: it serves as an ambassador for the sportiness and dynamics of electromobility at Audi.

The Audi e-tron Vision Gran Turismo, which fans of the Audi brand will be able to experience virtually in-game, is powered by three 200 kW (<272ps>) electric motors. Two motors for the rear axle and the third for the front. The system power is 600 kW (<815ps>). With a kerb weight of <1450kg>, the electric racing car has a weight-to-power ratio of <1.78kg> per horsepower, with an almost ideal weight distribution of 50:50 percent between the front and rear axles.

The Audi e-tron Vision Gran Turismo has a purely electric permanent four-wheel drive with a variable power distribution. Similar to the Ingolstadt manufacturer’s Formula E race cars, the Audi e-tron Vision Gran Turismo has only one forward gear.j
DescriptionLong.0x00004990:
The Audi Vision Gran Turismo was fully developed by Audi Design exclusively for the race simulation in the 'Vision Gran Turismo' competition, launched on the occasion of the 15th anniversary of the series. There are two versions of the digital version: a hybrid version and a purely electrical version.

The hybrid version of the Audi Vision Gran Turismo combines a V6 turbo engine with an electric front axle. This model enables you to compete virtually in races and championships with comparable Vision Gran Turismo Concept Cars and other hybrid cars.

The racing car consciously picks up the design elements of the Audi 90 IMSA GTO, with which Audi Sport thrilled fans in the North American IMSA GTO racing series in 1989, with drivers such as Hans-Joachim Stuck, Walter Röhrl, Hurley Haywood and Scott Goodyear. The car was far ahead of its time back then, owing to the combination of the consistently lightweight construction, and quattro drive, paired with a powerful five-cylinder turbo engine.

The Audi Vision Gran Turismo has a permanent four-wheel drive; in this case, e-tron quattro. Audi achieved the first victory of a hybrid-engined racing car at the famous 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2012 owing to the combination of an electrically-driven front axle and a conventionally-driven rear axle.

The front axle of the Audi Vision Gran Turismo is powered by a 400 kW (<544ps>) motor-generator-unit (MGU-K), which recovers energy when braking. Combined with a 3.4 litre V6 turbocharged engine with 550 kW (<748ps>) at the rear, the hybrid race car has a system output of 950 kW (<1292ps>) and even exceeds the performance of modern LMP1 hybrid racing cars. The weight-to-power ratio has a value that many racers can only dream of: less than one kilogram per horsepower.

The sequential 7-gear racing gearbox is ideal for the enormous system performance, and is actuated by rockers on the steering wheel. While the all-electric version drives on 18-inch wheels, the hybrid racing car has 20-inch wheels on the front axle and 21-inch wheels on the rear.
DescriptionLong.0x00004991:
The Lamborghini Aventador LP 750-4 Superveloce, released in 2015, was the highest performance model of the Lamborghini lineup until the rise of the Aventador S in 2016 which introduced major improvements.

The Superveloce (abbreviated SV) simply means ‘Super Fast’. The SV designation dates back to the famed Miura, and is a moniker that is given only to the highest performance flagship models of Lamborghini.

The 6.5 litre naturally aspirated V12 engine of the LP 750-4 SV produces <50ps> more power than the standard Aventador at <750ps>. Combined with a 7 speed semiautomatic transmission and all wheel drive, it reaches 0-<100km/h> in 2.8 seconds, <200km/h> in 8.6 seconds, and <300km/h> in 24.9 seconds. If you keep on the throttle beyond this, the car will continue to accelerate to speeds in excess of <350km/h>. It also shows incredible stopping performance with a <100km/h>-<0km/h> braking distance of just <30m>.

This model was to be a limited edition with a production run of only 600 cars worldwide, but an open top LP 750-4 SV roadster was later sold in a limited production run of 500 cars.\
DescriptionLong.0x00004992:
The Murciélago had been the flagship car of Lamborghini for almost 10 years since its debut in 2001, but by 2011, it was time for a new leader. The heir in this lineage that descended from the famous Countach is the Aventador, which debuted at the 2011 Geneva Motor Show.

The Aventador inherits the iconic scissor doors that open upwards, identifying it as Lamborghini's top model. However, because the silhouette of the car is not much different from the Murciélago, at first glance the car might not seem so different.

Looks can be deceiving, however; inside it has been completely redeveloped and has advanced like never before. The steel tube space frame of the Murciélago has been replaced with a carbon monocoque and forward/rear aluminium subframes, and almost all body parts have been made in carbon or aluminium. As a result the car weighs roughly <100kg> less than the Murciélago, with a dry weight of <1575kg>. This is extremely light for a car of this class.

The newly developed mid-mounted engine is a 6.5 L DOHC 48-valve V12. The maximum power of <700ps> @ <8250rpm> and maximum torque of <70.4kgm> @ <5500rpm> are transferred to the ground through an electronically controlled forward/aft torque-splitting mechanism and a single clutch 7-speed semi-AT that shifts 40% faster than the newest e-Gear on the Gallardo.

The suspension utilises a pushrod-type double wishbone configuration often used in racing, applied for the first time ever on a production car. As a result of all the improvements made, the top speed of the Aventador has increased from the <342km/h> of the Murciélago to <350km/h>. The 0-<100km/h> acceleration is now 2.9 seconds, having been improved by 0.3 seconds, and of course its stability in high-speed corners is unrivalled.

In an era where everyone is shouting eco-friendly performance, this is a rare, outstanding supercar which gathers praise for its high power and even higher performance.
DescriptionLong.0x00004993:
Appearing in 1991, the Honda Beat created the lightweight 2-seater trend, along with cars like the Suzuki Cappuccino and the Mazda AZ-1.

The proportions are <3295mm> in length, <1395mm> in width and <1175mm> in height. At only 760 kg, it is an ultra-lightweight vehicle. It was a full fledged 2-seater with no roll bar, and though the top was folded manually, because of its light weight it could be easily opened or closed by a single person.

The weight distribution was ideal at 43% for the front and 57% for the rear, and the rear wings were equipped with real air intakes for cooling the engine. In pursuit of perfect handling, tyres of different diameters were adopted, 13 inches for the front and 14 for the rear. The brakes too were performance oriented, utilising four-wheel disc brakes for the first time on a lightweight car.

The <656cc>, inline-3-cylinder normally aspirated engine delivers <64ps> and features multi-throttle and engine control systems brought about from F1 technology. The gearbox was a 5-speed MT, with its shift stroke tuned to be very short.

Users commented that the drive was quite delightful. Even without driving on winding roads, it was possible to enjoy the pleasures of a sportscar simply by driving along familiar streets. The production of the Beat continued until 1996, reaching total sales of 33,672 units. Though it was a pricey vehicle, the Beat is one of the jewels many people wish Honda had continued to produce.)
DescriptionLong.0x00004994:
The Beetle is an important part of Volkswagen’s history and heritage. But contrary to its cute looks, this car has also had its time in the limelight of motorsports as far back as the 1950s. Early in its history the Beetle won the East African Safari Rally 3 times, and was a part of the top group in the Greek Acropolis Rally. There have been one-make races based on the new Beetle that debuted in 1998, and in more recent years it has seen notable success in the Global Rallycross held in the U.S.

This Beetle Gr.3 is a model that traces this racing legacy of the Beetle. The greatly modified exterior and internals contain the essence of racing victory that Volkswagen has nurtured over the years.

The body is widened to allow bigger diameter wheels, and the roof has been lowered to reduce the frontal projected area, giving it a look similar to a modified classic chop-top Beetle. The front spoiler, the air outlets from the front tyres to the door panels, combined with a giant wing in the rear tells a lot about the performance levels of this car.

The powertrain consists of a DOHC 2-litre inline-4 with a high-pressure turbocharger, combined with VW’s proven 7-speed DSG. Its power will vary depending on the Balance of Performance (BoP) per race, but is of course more than adequate for fighting in the Gr.3 category races.

This racing Beetle lives in a different dimension to the cute Beetles you see on the streets.h
DescriptionLong.0x00004995:
Following in the tradition of the successful BMW touring cars of the 1970s, the BMW design team has created an uncompromising road racer for the modern era.

Crisp proportions and a dynamic silhouette give the BMW Vision Gran Turismo the appearance of speed, even standing still. Front and rear spoilers ensure optimum down-force, while all air conduction elements reduce drag and lower the vehicle’s total weight through the use of carbon fibre.

The paint finish in BMW M colours traces the flow of the airstream, recalling BMW Motorsport's successes.

The technology in the BMW Vision Gran Turismo is just as impressive as its uncompromising design. A powerful three-litre six-cylinder inline engine with M TwinPower Turbo technology delivers a maximum power of 404 kW/<549ps> between <6200rpm> and <7300rpm>. Its peak torque of 680 Nm/<69kgm> is developed at just <1900rpm>. A sequential six-speed transmission, operated by gearshift paddles on the steering wheel, distributes engine power to the driven rear axle.

The outstanding performance characteristics of the BMW Vision Gran Turismo, which weighs only 1,180 kilograms, include perfect 50:50 axle load distribution.A
DescriptionLong.0x00004996:
The compact sports car market has been losing momentum in recent years, but Toyota and Subaru got together with an aim to reinvigorate this market with the Toyota 86 and the Subaru BRZ.

While these two cars have different facia and interiors, the cars are brothers born from a common concept. The BRZ is Subaru’s first front engine rear wheel drive, initialled BRZ for 'Boxer Engine', 'Rear wheel drive' and 'Zenith'.

The BRZ aims to provide a sports car in which anyone can enjoy driving, with a compact body <4240mm> in length, <1775mm> in width, with a wheel base of <2570mm>. Configured as a 2 door notch-back coupé with sashless doors, the focus of the styling is on sportiness and a low centre of gravity.

The engine is Subaru’s signature 2 litre horizontally opposed engine for low centre of gravity, combined with Toyota’s D-4S fuel injection technology. This allows the engine to produce an impressive <200ps> while naturally aspirated. With strut suspension in the front and double wishbones in the rear, the primary focus of the suspension tuning focuses on the fun of sports car driving, and ease of control.

The BRZ, debuting in 2012, has undergone various improvements almost every year, raising its level of refinement. In the 2015 model the characteristics of the electric power steering were revised and the vehicle rigidity was reinforced to further raise its steering feel and ride quality.
DescriptionLong.0x00004997:
Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo is a project as realistic as possible for Bugatti fans to introduce a thoroughbred Bugatti to the virtual world. The result is a symbiosis of technology, tradition and aesthetics, where every design feature has an actual purpose.

The Bugatti designers drew their inspiration from the brand's racing tradition. Bugatti enjoyed great success in racing in the 1920s and 1930s. Historical inspiration for the modern virtual race car came, in particular, from the Bugatti Type 57 Tank and its victories in the 24 Hours of Le Mans races in 1937 and 1939.

The design of the Vision Gran Turismo shows at first glance that Bugatti DNA meets cutting-edge racing technology. Marked by large convex surfaces in contrast with concave transitions and strong lines, the proportions of the vehicle are uncompromisingly athletic and designed for maximum performance. The designers have unmistakeably integrated key features of the Bugatti design DNA into the virtual race car's design with every vehicle component having a real performance function. The horseshoe on the front grille acts as a support for the front splitter. The centre fin, which derives from the legendary Type 57 SC Atlantic, makes an important contribution to the car's dynamic stability and accommodates the kinematic system for the rear wing, which controls the air brake and the drag reduction system (DRS). The architecture of the interior continues the clean lines of the exterior. Every aspect of the interior is geared to racing.

The virtual race car was developed in close collaboration with the Bugatti engineers and is based on modern racing technology and aerodynamic analyses. To attain the performance goals, the Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo is driven by a W16 engine, which delivers the engine power of 1,230 kW (1,650 BHP) and 1,580 Nm (161.1 kgf m) to all four wheels. The engineers have calculated that the Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo can drive at over 400 km/h (250 mph) on four sections of the virtual Le Mans track reaching an overall max speed of 447.59 km/h (278 mph).

The Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo is the ultimate race car, and at the same time a true Bugatti.L

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.1 regulationt by Gran Turismo.
DescriptionLong.0x00004999:
The 6th generation model of the Chevy Camaro, America’s legendary sports car, was revealed in the spring of 2015.

The styling followed the retro-modern design that was highly popular in the market in the last generation. However, the inside of the car received a full makeover. The platform was changed from the ‘Zeta’ platform of the previous model to the ‘Alpha’ platform shared with cars like the Cadillac CTS, but with roughly 70% of its parts developed specifically for the Camaro.

The body utilises aluminium in various parts, improving the rigidity of the body by 28%, but with a weight reduction of over <90kg>. The suspension mounted on this body was also newly designed, with multi-link MacPherson struts in the front, and a 5 link suspension in the rear.

The biggest news regarding the engine was that a turbocharged 2 litre inline 4 producing <279ps> and <40.8kgm> of torque was added to the lineup. Improvements were also made to the existing 3.6 litre V6, raising both power and torque slightly to <340ps> and <39.3kgm> respectively. In addition, an LT1 6.2 litre V8 – the same engine as the Corvette – is also available in the lineup, producing <461ps> and <62.9kgm> torque.

The sports grade model powered by this LT1 is the ‘SS’. Equipped with 20-inch wheels and Brembo brakes, and in the case of manual transmission models, it comes equipped with active rev matching as well as an optional magnet ride control suspension.m
DescriptionLong.0x0000499A:
The Ford Mustang was a hit compact sports coupé that was dropped into the world of American cars at a time when bigger was always better and luxury meant everything. While the success of the Mustang was due to its more than adequate performance, low price, and a well planned advertising campaign, there was a car designed to outdo the Mustang in every way; this was the first generation Chevrolet Camaro that debuted in 1966.

While attracting a lot of attention at the time of its debut, it still could not overtake the Mustang in sales. The remedy that was introduced to alleviate this situation was the high performance Z28 model. The 302 cu.in. displacement of the engine was set to match the regulations for the 305 cu.in. (<5000cc>) 'Trans-Am' races, and with this highly tuned engine and a chassis that can handle the power, the existence of the built-to-race Z28 greatly contributed to raising the image of the Camaro and driving its sales.

The final 1969 model is the most popular out of all the Camaros throughout the years as the icon of the golden era of automobiles in America. But even out of these the Z28 is on a whole different level, and is especially desirable to many.w
DescriptionLong.0x0000499B:
The 6th generation Chevrolet Camaro further modernised the 5th generation design which gathered praise for its retro-modern styling, while dropping approximately <100kg> of weight for higher sports performance.

The most powerful model in the lineup is the ZL1. Equipped with the ‘LT4’ 5.7L V8 from the Corvette Z06, it produces <659ps> and <89.8kgm> torque, with a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 3.5 seconds and a top speed of <318km/h>.

Chevrolet has also provided a '1LE' performance package starting from the 3rd generation models forward, adding further to the performance of the Camaro. For the 2018 model, announced in 2017, this package included a large deflector, rear wing, diffuser, dedicated suspension and specially developed tyres. The Camaro Z1 with this package marked 7 minutes 16.04 seconds on the German Nürburgring, greatly surpassing the performance of your average supercar.y
DescriptionLong.0x0000499C:
The GT race series in Japan was renamed the 'Super GT' when it became an international series from 2005. Until 2004, it was called the 'All Japan Grand Touring Championship (JGTC)', and from its start it boasted the largest number of spectators for a motorsport in Japan. For this reason, Japanese automobile manufacturers poured in much energy into this championship series.

The Toyota Supra entered the championship from 1994, and it was like a direct challenge against the Nissan GT-R that had dominated the series 3 years in the row, from the first year of the championship in 1993. 3 years later in 1997, the Supra finally defeated the GT-R to become series champion. The historic machine that achieved this feat was the #36, Castrol Tom’s Supra.

The drivers were Michael Krumm and Pedro de la Rosa, and they entered as the second machine of Tom’s from the second round of this year. In the 5 rounds excluding the opening round, it came strong, winning 1st place twice, and placing once in both 2nd and 3rd place, to win the series.

The machine itself had not changed greatly from the previous year. The only significant difference was the change from the H pattern gearbox to a Hewland 6-speed sequential transmission. Other than this, the engine displacement had been lowered to 2 L, in order to allow for a lower minimum weight under the race regulation rules. The 3S-GT engine producing nearly <500ps> is almost as is, and its increased body rigidity, changes in suspension geometry, and improvements in aerodynamics, are all in the standard evolutionary process of a racing machine.
DescriptionLong.0x0000499D:
Save for very few exceptions in the past, Porsche has traditionally participated in sports car racing with the 911. This long running tradition was broken in 2015, when Porsche added a GT4 motorsport base model to the Cayman line up.

The Cayman GT4 was the fastest Cayman in its history, with many components carried over from the 911. The engine is a 3.8L horizontally opposed 6 cylinder from the Carrera S, producing more power than the 911 Carrera at <385ps>. The front suspension and brakes use components from the 911 GT3, and greatly exceed the performance levels of the other Caymans in terms of stability and braking.

But its evolution did not end there. In the following year in 2016, Porsche further refined the GT4 in the Cayman GT4 Clubsport.

This special Cayman is a pure race version for track use. Any and all creature comforts remaining on the roadgoing Cayman GT4 were stripped away to make this a complete competition machine.

In the interior a roll cage protects the driver, and the seats have been replaced with full bucket seats. To shave every last second off lap times, the 6 speed manual transmission is replaced with a DCT and the suspension and brakes use components equal to the 911 GT3 Cup car. The engine power is still the same as the GT4 model, but the suspension and drivetrain are all tailored for using full slick tyres in the world of competition.

Being a mid-engined car, there are many who praise the advantage of the Cayman over the rear engined 911. The GT4 Clubsport is the ultimate version of the Cayman, which takes full advantage of its character.
DescriptionLong.0x0000499E:
The 1st generation Dodge Challenger debuted in 1970 as a sister car to the Plymouth Barracuda, using the same E-body.

The body was available in hardtop and convertible forms. In the mid-1960s, many popular pony cars (cheap, high-performance, stylish cars) were released in the U.S., starting with the Ford Mustang and followed by cars like the Chevrolet Camaro and Pontiac Firebird. The Challenger was released after this trend had peaked, but was still very much welcomed by the public at the time.

One of the major reasons was probably its style, with its low, sharp silhouette and bottle-shape lines. The design, created by Carl Cameron, who had designed the 1966 Dodge Charger, would later carry over into the 3rd generation Challenger which debuted 40 years later at the 2006 North American International Auto Show.

The 1st generation Challenger consisted of the Challenger 6, Challenger V8 and Challenger R/T (Road/Track) models. In addition, a T/A model was homologated for participation in the SCCA Trans-Am racing, but the R/T is the highest performance model out of the commercially mass-produced lineup.
DescriptionLong.0x0000499F:
In the 1970 SCCA Can-Am, Chaparral learned from their mistakes in the 2H: a car that challenged new aerodynamics theories, and created the 2J, a car that was, in a way, even more unique than the 2H.

Its structure made it a first in the world of motorsport. The air flowing under the body whilst moving is sucked out by fans at the back of the car, and by sealing the area between the body sides and the ground, it produces massive downforce. In order to drive these two fans in the rear, it mounted an air-cooled, 2-cycle snowmobile engine in addition to its normal engine.

Weaving between the cracks of the regulations, the Chaparral 2J was nicknamed 'The Vacuum Cleaner', and astounded everyone. Aside from its radical looks, its driving performance was top class, pushing aside the works McLaren M8D that was previously unbeatable that year, and taking pole position in round 7 at Road America and round 10 in Riverside.

Upon the SCCA receiving complaints from entrants who feared this radical advancement, they banned the use of engines for any purpose other than driving right before the 1971 season, and the Chaparral 2J was forever left to gather dust in the garage.

With this move, Chaparral lost its passion for the SCCA Can-Am. They also decided that it would be impossible to defeat the rock-solid works McLaren using conventional designs, and they withdrew for a time from the SCCA Can-Am as well as all other racing activities.
DescriptionLong.0x000049A0:
Conceived as a 'Garage 56' Le Mans Experimental Prototype, the Chevrolet Chaparral 2X Vision Gran Turismo is a look into the future of motorsports and inspired by the combined sensations of flying in a wing suit and a Moto GP race bike... an experience where the 2X pilot flies around the circuit, headlong, just inches from the race surface. The 2X’s Chevrolet power unit is unlike anything seen on the track before... it literally thrusts itself down the track with laser pulse shock waves generated by an advanced propulsion system from Chevrolet.

The driving position creates one of the most immersive and exciting experiences ever imagined in four wheel motorsports. The vehicle architecture and design take its shape as a result of the 'forward flight' driving position, one where the pilot becomes at one with the structure of the car. Once on board, with the canopy retracted to the closed position, the 2X forms a totally unique envelope around the pilot’s outstretched body. Hand and foot controls operate independently and involve all of the frictionless, magnetic bearing wheels. Vehicle acceleration, deceleration and direction is controlled by the movement & physical inputs of the 2X pilot, a true application of four points of control. Braking is handled by a combination of Brembo magnetic re-gen calipers and deployable AeroBrake panels in the 2X bodywork.

The integral BodyFrame is created using a unique 'layup schedule' which allows the entire structure to act in unison with the 2X suspension. The main body also incorporates the super-ridged propulsion structure which ensures absolute accuracy of the thrust parabola to the laser pulse cone. The variable positioning of the thrust cone vanes serve to create propulsion and downforce by the simultaneous use of this multi-vane adjustability and a lower Thrust Vectoring panel. The combination of these two technologies allows the Chaparral 2X pilot to fine tune downforce to the exact spot on a given circuit, actually 'pressing' the tyre’s contact patch onto the track surface and enhancing mechanical grip where needed most.

The Chevrolet Chaparral 2X Vision Gran Turismo. The spirit of Jim Hall’s amazing legacy of motorsport innovation embodiec in a bold statement. One which will revolutionise the futtre of Le Mans Experimental prototypes. Like nothhng you’ve ever seen or heard before.M
DescriptionLong.0x000049A1:
The Charger SRT Hellcat, which was sold from 2014, is a production model with extreme performance capabilities, even when compared to the long history of Dodge Chargers since 1966.

The 3rd generation Charger that debuted in 2005 had the bold styling that was reminiscent of muscle cars of the past, as well as being equipped with the iconic 'Hemi' engine unit that symbolises high performance Chryslers. It gained great popularity as a truly American high performance saloon; there is even a model equipped with a 6.4L Hemi that produces <477ps>.

But this Hellcat goes way beyond the norm. SRT, the high performance model development team of Chrysler, developed the car further with no holds barred, creating a supercharged 6.2L Hemi producing <717ps> and with a maximum torque of <81.6kgm>. Combined with a reinforced 8-speed AT, the car reaches supercar level performance, achieving 0-60 mph acceleration in just 3.7 seconds and a top speed of <328.3km/h>.

In terms of technology, it is similar to its sibling model that was released just ahead of the Charger, the 2 door coupé Challenger Hellcat, but the Charger’s quarter mile time of 11 seconds is 0.2 seconds faster than the Challenger. These figures greatly exceed that of its European rivals and the car has become the fastest 4 door saloon in the world. Even at this level of performance, the price is only $63,995. Many were surprised not only about its incredible performance but also the fact that it was so reasonably priced.
DescriptionLong.0x000049A2:
Unveiled in 2014, the Charger SRT Hellcat is the most powerful production model of the long running Dodge Charger series, first released in 1966.

The third wave Charger debuted in 2005 as an all-American high performance 4-door sedan, but the Hellcat was on a completely different level. The 6.2L Hemi engine was meticulously tuned by SRT, Chrysler's high-performance development team, who added a supercharger to bring the maximum engine output up to an astounding <717ps> with <81.6kgm> maximum torque. Coupled to a reinforced 8-speed automatic transmission, the car is able to achieve a 0-60 mile of 3.7s and a top speed of <328.3km/h>.

While the mechanical elements of the car are almost identical to the Challenger Hellcat model, the Charger is able to run the 1/4 mile in 11 seconds flat, 0.2 seconds faster than the Challenger. It's figures like these that make the Charger an apt rival to its European competition.

*This safety car version is an original model created by Gran Turismo.
DescriptionLong.0x000049A3:
The SEMA show is the world's largest annual custom car show hosted in Las Vegas, Nevada in the U.S. every autumn. And at SEMA every year, Gran Turismo picks out cars that fits the philosophy of Gran Turismo for the ‘GT Awards’. The car that won ‘Best of Show’ in the Gran Turismo Awards of 2013 was this 1967 Chevrolet Nova.

The original Nova is a popular small car of Chevrolet built between the 1960s and the 70s. While there were high performance top grade models powered by V8 engines, at the base is a simple, functional car that was made as a daily driver for youths and families.

The shop which turned this modest family car into a crazy hotrod is Chris Holstrom Concepts, a specialty shop from Washington state. Chris Holstrom stripped the Nova down and started integrating high performance parts to create this Monster Nova.

Under the bonnet is the LS9, a supercharged 6.2L engine from the Corvette ZR1. Its output has been raised to 700 horsepower, and to withstand this incredible amount of power the rear suspension and differential housing utilise reinforced parts. BAER 6 pot calipers are used for the brakes, and the wheels with continental sport contact 5 tyres are forged rims with 18 inches in the front, 19 inches the rear.

There have been no aerodynamic accessories added to the exterior, maintaining the look of a stock model. This is an automotive miracle, fusing together the chic look of the 60s with modern day performance.
DescriptionLong.0x000049A4:
The Civic Type R is a sports model that was developed from the family car Honda Civic and, since its debut in 1997, has continued to excite sports driving enthusiasts from around the world.

Its history had come to a close in 2012, but came back in 2015 when the 4th generation Civic Type R was born.

The base model was the 9th generation European 5 door model. On the exterior there is a large front spoiler, rear wing, side skirts and rear diffuser. These were not just for looks but as a result of repeated wind tunnel and road testing, in order to minimise air resistance and improve downforce. Even the front and rear over fenders are for fitting the wider tyres properly.

The power unit is a dedicated 2.0 litre direct injection, turbocharged inline 4 with VTEC that produces <310ps>/<40.8kgm>, providing power levels unprecedented in the Type R series to date. This enables a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 5.7 seconds, with a top speed of <270km/h>, making this the highest performance Civic in its history.

The suspension utilises a dual axis strut in the front that reduces torque steer by roughly 50% in comparison to the standard Civic, with an adaptive damper system that can be adjusted.

This 4th generation Type R took on the Nürburgring Nordschleife, which resulted in a lap time of 7 minutes, 50.63 seconds, successfully overwriting the record for commercial front-wheel drives on this track.
DescriptionLong.0x000049A5:
This is an original tuned model created by Gran Turismo, based on the Honda Civic Type R (EK) '97.

The following is the description of the base model:

The Honda Civic is a long-selling model that first appeared in 1972. The mainstream model of the 6th generation EK Civic, appearing in 1995, also called the Miracle Civic, was given a high fuel economy, high output 3-stage VTEC, and was also equipped with a CVT called the Honda Multimatic.

The body types made available were a 3-door hatchback and a 4-door saloon called the Ferio, and it received good reviews, even becoming Japan’s Car of the Year.

Two years later in August 1997, the Type R of this 6th generation Civic made its first appearance. Based on the 3-door hatchback model, the car attracted much attention as the first Type R Civic.

The engine of the Civic Type R was a B16B, 1.6 L inline-4-cylinder DOHC 16-valve engine, and equipped with VTEC it produced an amazing <185ps> @ <8200rpm> despite being a normally aspirated engine. The body was made lighter as in the other Type Rs, and was equipped with a harder, lower suspension, enlarged four-wheel disc brakes and ABS with a sports setting.

In addition, it was equipped standard with Recaro bucket seats suited for sports driving, and a small diameter MOMO steering wheel with an airbag. With a special Championship White body colour, a red Honda emblem and machined titanium shift knob, it greatly emphasised its sporting image.

The lightweight, compact and high-performance Civic Type R was very active in racing, invoking one-make Civic races and actively competing in races like the Super Taikyu endurance series, and was loved by many amateur racers even 10 years after its first release.~
DescriptionLong.0x000049A6:
The Honda Civic is a long-selling model that first appeared in 1972. The mainstream model of the 6th generation EK Civic, appearing in 1995, also called the Miracle Civic, was given a high-fuel-economy, high-output 3-stage VTEC, and was also equipped with a CVT called the Honda Multimatic.

Two years later in August 1997, the Type R of this 6th generation Civic made its first appearance. Based on the 3-door hatchback model, the car attracted much attention as the first Type R Civic.

The engine of the Civic Type R was a B16B, 1.6 L inline-4-cylinder DOHC 16-valve engine, and equipped with VTEC it produced an amazing <185ps> @ <8200rpm> even though it was a normally aspirated engine. The body was lightened, as with the other Type R models, and was equipped with a harder, lower suspension, enlarged four-wheel disc brakes and ABS with a sports setting.

The lightweight, compact and high-performance Civic Type R was very active in racing, invoking one-make Civic races and actively competing in races like the Super Taikyu endurance series, while still captivating many amateur racers.
DescriptionLong.0x000049A7:
The Clio R.S. 220 EDC Trophy is the sports version of the 4th generation Clio developed by Renault Sport, the motorsports department of Renault. It was introduced at the 2015 Geneva Motor Show as an even higher performance model than the R.S. 200 EDC. The name ‘Trophy’ is a special name given to extraordinary sports models that are suited for the track.

There are 2 major differences between the R.S. 220 EDC and the older R.S. 200 EDC. The car was given a different turbocharger, the intake and exhaust were tuned, and the ECU map was changed in order to increase the output of the 1.6-litre inline-4 turbo by 10% to <220ps>; as is indicated in the digits of the car’s name. The rev limit is also higher, raised from <6500rpm> to <6800rpm>. The maximum torque output is <26.5kgm>, a <2.0kgm> increase from the R.S. 200. The gearbox EDC has also received changes to the software, shortening the shifting speed by 50%. Even the stroke of the shift change paddles were made smaller by 30%.

The other major change was the implementation of a ‘Chassis Trophy’, giving the car a chassis that has the best sports setup in the series. The dampers and springs of the suspension were reinforced, a hydraulic bump stop was added, and the ride height is <20mm> lower in the front and <10mm> lower in the rear. The steering gear ratio was made quicker from 14.5 to 13.2.

The R.S. 220 EDC Trophy was taken on the Nürburgring Nordschleife by a German car magazine, and marked an incredible 8 minutes 23 seconds on the track. This was the fastest time ever for a car in the compact hatchback category at the time.

DescriptionLong.0x000049A9:
The Clio R.S. V6 (Lutecia R.S. V6 in Japan) is a midship sportscar, created by removing the rear seats from a Renault Clio and mounting a 3 L V6 engine, from upper grade models like the Laguna, in its place.

It was specifically built for motorsports, and was used in one-make races before the F1 in Europe. This is the road-going version of those cars. It has been said to be the return of the R5 Turbo that left its name in the WRC in the early 1980s.

The 3 L V6 produces <233ps> @ <6000rpm>, with a maximum torque of <30.6kgm> @ <3750rpm>. The transmission is available only in a 6-speed MT.

The suspension uses specially designed struts for both front and rear, and the tyres are 205/50R17 in the front, and 235/45R17 in the rear. In order to fit the wide tyres, the body is given flared fenders in both the front and rear, but the shape of the fenders is not wild like in the R5 Turbo, and is designed to flow beautifully with the body.

In the Paris Motor Show, held in October 2002, the Phase 2 minor change version made its appearance. There were changes to the exterior, and, along with the standard Clio, it was given the new design for all new generation Renaults. At the same time the interior design was updated, and the tyre size has been increased to 18'.

Though the engine displacement is the same, the maximum output was increased to <255ps> @ <7150rpm>. The rpm at which maximum torque is produced is increased to <30.6kgm> @ <4650rpm>. The suspension geometry has also been revised, and with an additional sub-frame in the rear, its driving performance has been improved as well.S
DescriptionLong.0x000049AA:
The FIA Speed World Challenge, a world endurance championship in which the Shelby Cobra competed, differed from the GT Class in that an engine displacement limitation was not established.

In order to defeat their rival Ferrari in this series, Shelby American decided to mount a large displacement engine in their entry. At the time, Ford conveniently had their 7L 427 ‘Side Oiler’, a pure racing engine for stock car racing. It was decided that the Cobra would be fitted with this engine, and the development of the Shelby Cobra 427 started near the end of 1964. Its prototype was completed in the spring of 1965.

The major problem that immediately arose was that in comparison to the <350ps> produced by the 289 unit, the 427 Side Oiler produced roughly <500ps>. Phil Remington, who was in charge of design at Shelby American, determined that the existing suspension would not be able to handle this much power. Therefore the characteristic side-mounted leaf suspension was abandoned and changed to a conventional double wishbone with coil dampers.

The Shelby Cobra 427 cleared its 100-unit minimum production and acquired the FIA homologation, and the car ventured into competition in the SCCA A production class from the opening of the 1966 season. In the end, 348 Shelby Cobra 427s were built, with 88 of these being competition spec models or test cars.

Incidentally, the 427 S/C is a road model with competition spec equipment, and there were only 31 of these cars that were built to this spec from the beginning.
DescriptionLong.0x000049AB:
The AC Cobra had dominated the racing scene of the 1960s, and its coupé version was the Shelby Cobra Coupe.

The strength of the base AC Cobra was in its lightweight body and large-displacement American V8. With quick handling and extreme acceleration performance, it was a top contender throughout the racing world. However, its open body was a detriment aerodynamically, and it did not do as well in high-speed tracks. It especially lagged in the Le Mans 24-hour race with its long straightaway, and Shelby American, who had expanded to racing in Europe, was in need of a Cobra with better aerodynamics.

The coupé body, designed by famed designer Pete Brock, had a long nose to contain the 4.7L V8, with a short deck ending soon after the rear tyres. It was full of cutting-edge aerodynamic designs including the ‘coda tronca’ design with its vertically cut-off rear end.

Thanks to this new body, the car, which had almost the same specs as the original AC Cobra (aside from some suspension improvements), achieved a top speed that was <30km/h> faster than the original. Its racing performance was spectacular, showing incredible results in big events held in North America and GT class racing events in Europe within a short span of 2 years.
DescriptionLong.0x000049AC:
Daihatsu’s first fully convertible 2-seater sports kei car, the 'Kopen', shown at the 1999 Tokyo Motor Show, gained a huge amount of support, and was pushed to production as the 'Copen' in June 2002.

It is a model that follows in the footsteps of cars like the Mazda AZ-1, Honda Beat, and Suzuki Cappuccino of the 1990s, but while these cars were created in the days of the economic bubble in Japan, the era and background in which the Copen was developed differs greatly. Because of this, it is notable that they have performed very thorough marketing, and made significant efforts that exceed the boundaries of kei cars in various details for this car.

The Copen is built at a dedicated line within the 'Expert Centre' in the Daihatsu headquarters plant, where highly skilled technicians at Daihatsu are gathered. Given a high-strength, lightweight body, specially tuned suspension, luxurious features like the MOMO steering wheel and a 5 layer coat of paint, it is produced at an extremely high quality that makes the car suitable to be called a 'premium' car.'

In addition, the Copen is equipped as standard with the 'Active Top' electric roof, the first ever for a commercial kei car. The system developed by OASys, a company co-founded by Webasto of Germany and Pininfarina of Italy, opens or closes the top in just 20 seconds.

Offering the car in AT as well opened the range of possible users, selling many more cars than first anticipated, exceeding 40,000 cars sold in 2007.

In 2003, export was started to the UK and Australia, and though initially it was almost identical to the domestic model, from 2005 a 1300 cc model was produced, mainly for the European market.
DescriptionLong.0x000049AD:
The Dodge Super Bee is a muscle car released by Chrysler in 1968. Though there were a number of higher priced rival performance vehicles around at the time, the Super Bee became popular as a reasonably priced model which omitted all the frills except its driving performance.

The first Super Bee debuted in 1968. Based on the Dodge Coronet with a mid-sized body, it launched with the 2 door coupé that was lightest in weight, and a 2 door hard top model was added in 1969.

What made the Super Bee special was its powerful engine lineup. It was offered with nothing but high power engines – either with a <340ps> 6.8L, <395ps> 7.2L, or a <431ps> 7.0L Hemi.

To match its increased power, the car came with reinforced suspension as standard, and it was offered with options and performance kits that focused on sports driving. And while it was equipped with an expensive high performance engine, optional accessories and provisions for comfort were mostly omitted. This resulted in a stoic, spartan model made solely for driving.

In 1970 the chrome bumper was changed and the car was given a facelift with a two part grille. Then in the following year of 1971 it was replaced with the second generation model which was based on the Charger.

DescriptionLong.0x000049B2:
A full model change in the autumn of 1967 brought the new C3 Corvette Stingray as a 1968 model. It was very reminiscent of the 'Mako Shark II' show model, which was displayed at the New York International Auto Show in April of 1965.

This concept sought to show off the Corvette in a new light, specifically as a grand tourer. Chief designer Bill Mitchell's design ideas were extremely important factors in the achievement of this goal.

Working as Mitchell's right-hand man was a man named Larry Shinoda, a Japanese-American who had worked as a detail designer on the original Stingray. Taking many hints from Mitchell's concepts, Shinoda's image of the next generation GT car materialised as the Mako Shark II.

With a dynamic, curvaceous exterior, and an interior stuffed with the newest electronic gizmos, it was indeed the Corvette of the future. The essence of this idea was thoroughly incorporated into the street model that was to become the C3 Corvette.

In 1969 the standard engine's displacement was brought up from 327 ci to 350 ci, but maximum output remained unchanged at <300ps>. At the same time, the small-block option changed from the 327 ci L79, to the 350 ci L46, with maximum output again unchanged at <355ps>.

Though at the time talk was all about the power of the big block Corvette, the small block held the advantage in handling with its lower front-end weight. The epitome of this was the replacement of the top-grade L46 by the <370ps> LT1. Available around 1970, this was acclaimed as the best handling of all the C3 Corvette combinations.E
DescriptionLong.0x000049B3:
When one thinks of American high-performance cars, the mainstream models are those that fit high-powered engines in coupés and saloons. However there is one model that continues to be manufactured as a pure sportscar: The Chevrolet Corvette.

Interestingly, even the Corvette didn’t start life as a dedicated sportscar. The first Corvette was more a styling-focused open-top model, and it was not given a powerful V8 until 10 years after its debut. The true sports models started with the 2nd generation C2 Corvette.

The body was based on the first Sting Ray, the Corvette Stingray Racer Concept prototype, and was a drastic change from the classic '50s style to that of an aggressive competition appearance.

As with the body, the chassis was completely redesigned from the ground up. The high-tension ladder frame was given a short wheelbase, with 4-wheel independent suspension, with the aim of increasing the car's agility.

The 5.4 litre OHV engine produced over <300ps>, and the massive torque produced by the large displacement V8 defined its character. The combination of this power with a lightweight FRP body produced rocket-like acceleration, and gave it the overwhelming performance so loved by Americans.
DescriptionLong.0x000049B4:
Debuting in 1953, the 1st generation Chevrolet Corvette would go on to win numerous trophies in the world of racing. The next step was the development of the Corvette SS race car which debuted in 1957, a project led by Zora Duntov - the man often dubbed 'the father of the Corvette.'

While aesthetically similar to the base Corvette, the underpinnings of the SS were completely different. Designed for use in racing, it featured a shortened tubular frame upon which was mounted a <307ps> fuel-injected 283 engine, and the car achieved a top speed of <292km/h> in testing.

However in the same year those plans were scrapped after the American Automobile Manufacturers Association (AMA) agreed to ban the direct participation of manufacturers in racing, following a number of accidents in NASCAR and other motorsporting events. There was a successor to the SS though, in the form of the Stingray Racer.

The car inherited the frame and body covering the engine, almost as is, from the Corvette SS. The final car, created by the newly appointed GM Styling department Chief, Bill Mitchell, and designer Larry Shinoda, also borrowed styling elements from a blackballed next-generation Corvette prototype.

This Stingray Racer entered a variety of races as a private personal race car of Bill Mitchell, and won two consecutive SCCA Class C modified titles for 1959 and 1960.
DescriptionLong.0x000049B5:
The Chevrolet Corvette is a thoroughbred American sportscar, with looks that have always had a certain glamorous appeal. These have always allowed it to sit proudly even next to mighty supercars such as Ferraris. Since the launch of the C6 Z06 model in 2005, it is no longer defined by looks alone and has fully joined the ranks of supercars in performance as well.

The ZR1 that debuted in the 2008 North American International Auto Show even gained some performance advantages that exceed Ferraris and Lamborghinis. In the lightweight and strong aluminium and magnesium frame of the Z06 was mounted an engine that far exceeds the performance of the <505ps> Z06 engine – it was given a supercharged 6.2 L V8, LS9 engine producing <647ps> @ <6500rpm> and <83.5kgm> @ <3800rpm> torque. The engine is built one-by-one by hand, and combined with a 6-speed MT with close-ratio gears.

The suspension has been specially tuned, and the brakes are now carbon ceramic. The wheel arches, bonnet, and roof panels are carbon fibre, reducing the weight down to 1508 kg. Though modest, it receives a special front lip spoiler, side steps and rear spoiler. In other words, anything and everything possible that could be done to maximise driving performance has been implemented on this model.

Most people have the image of a straight-line drag racer when they think of an American sportscar. But this ZR1 ran the old Nürburgring course with a time record that even exceeds the Nissan GT-R at the time. With a top speed of <330km/h>, 0-<60mph> (approx. 100 km/h) acceleration in 3.4 seconds, quarter mile in 11.3 seconds, the ZR1 is truly the greatest Corvette ever built.
DescriptionLong.0x000049B6:
In 1990, a special performance model named as the ZR-1 was added to the Corvette line-up. The characters ZR-1 simply represented the option code, which was also appended as-is to the model name. It had its roots in a racing package that had existed for a period of three years from 1970 to 1973.

The parts that went into the ZR-1 were extremely varied, and ranged from suspension and wheels to body parts, but the real heart was in the engine, the LT5. It matched the standard L98 Corvette engine with 350 ci displacement, and the same bore and stroke dimensions. However, the cylinder block was made of aluminium and mounted with 4-valve DOHC cylinder heads co-developed by Chevrolet and Lotus.

This was the first time a DOHC 4-valve engine was fitted in a Corvette. Utilising the latest combustion logic, the power unleashed by the DOHC heads was astounding. The LT5 squeezed out <380ps>, compared the standard <250ps>.

The ZR-1 matched this special performance with an incredibly high price and assembly under a constrained delivery system. The cylinder blocks were cast by a 3rd-party manufacturer, and the engines were assembled by hand by experienced craftsmen.

The price of the standard Corvette coupé was just under $32,000. The ZR-1 option package alone was an additional $27,000 plus. A year later the price jumped to $31,000 making it nearly double the price of a standard Corvette. It has been proposed that even with such prices, the ZR-1 was barely profitable for Chevrolet.

*Please note that the model included in Gran Turismo is the prototype model built in 1989.
DescriptionLong.0x000049B7:
The Lamborghini Countach was the company’s first supercar, and was unleashed onto the world back in 1971 at the Geneva Motor Show. The original show car, the LP500, remained just that, as the Countach didn’t actually go into production until three years later with the launch of the LP400. This was far and away the closest car to the radical original design concept, and only about 150 of this model were ever made.

Through the years, an LP400S and LP500S went into production, and in 1985, a 5000 Quattrovalvole, setting its sights directly onto Ferrari’s refreshingly styled Testarossa, was released. This Countach featured four valves per cylinder to its boisterous V12 that was increased in displacement to 5.2 L, its maximum power output now reaching a ceiling of <455ps>.

Gran Turismo has opted to include the very last car model in the series, the 25th Anniversary Lamborghini Countach, released in 1988. This model celebrated Lamborghini's 25th year as a car manufacturer and had roughly the same specs as the 5000 Quattrovalvole, but with the addition of some extra stylised exterior bits and a new rear bumper due to safety regulations. This version was also the best-selling Countach over the course of this Italian wild child’s full production run, which ended in 1990 at 657 units.r

Toyota’s ‘Crown’ luxury saloon received a full model change in 2012 to become its 14th generation model.

The Crown had undergone mainly conservative changes in its long history, but the 12th generation model had its main components greatly updated. The 14th generation model also follows this path. The platform is carried over from the previous model, and while the steering design is slightly sporty as with the previous 2 generations, the front fascia was updated.

The lineup consisted of a classy ‘Royal’ version and a sporty ‘Athlete’ version. While the shape of the Royal model’s front mask is reminiscent of its name, a crown, the Athlete has edges that look like lightning bolts, and the grille is wider and sharper looking. This greatly changed its image from the traditional mild mannered look of a Crown.

The engine is available in 4 types, with a 3.5L and a 2.5L V6, a 2.5L inline 4 hybrid, and a turbocharged 2L inline 4. e

DescriptionLong.0x000049BB:
The CTR3 is a Ruf original sportscar released in 2007, taking the place of their flagship CTR and CTR2.

Until this car, Ruf had developed their CTR based on the Porsche 930, and the CTR2 on the Porsche 993 Turbo. However while the CTR3 used some parts from the Porsche 997, the design and development of the car was done independently by Ruf.

And the midship layout of the chassis is also very different from the previous CTR series. Mounted in the rear of the space frame together with a newly designed horizontally mounted 6 speed sequential transmission, the engine is also not just a tuned +C4:C63.8 litre 911 engine, but a newly designed 3.8 litre intercooled twin turbo flat 6, producing <700ps> and <90.7kgm> torque.

With a top speed of <380km/h> and a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 3.2 seconds, it was one of the fastest cars of its time.
DescriptionLong.0x000049BC:
The D-Type is Jaguar’s racing sports car announced in 1954, with 68 cars produced until 1957. The D-Type is the successor of the C-Type, and its fundamental mechanisms are a direct evolution of its predecessor. However, the central part of the tubular frame was now a monocoque structure, and the 3.4L inline 6 cylinder engine produced <253ps> in the early models, and the final model was raised to <274ps> for a large boost in performance.

As with the C-Type, the design of the body is by Malcolm Sayer. The fin behind the driver seat was added after repeated wind tunnel testing, and became a major styling characteristic of the car along with its flowing body details.

The car debuted in racing in 1954. At the 24 Hours of Le Mans it unfortunately retired out of the race, while it was in first place for a while and even set the fastest speed record. The Number 12 car is the works car from this race.

In 1955, a long nose version was created with revised aerodynamics, and fuel injection was added in 1956. Many improvements were added throughout the years, and the car won the 24 Hours of Le Mans 3 years in a row from 1955 to 1957.
DescriptionLong.0x000049BD:
The top level Formula Racing in Japan, the Super Formula Series switched the chassis of their race cars to the Dallara SF19 for the 2019 Season competition.

The SF19 is a successor to the SF14 that was used from 2014 to 2018, also designed by Dallara of Italy. Carrying over the agile and light weight concept, the new car was made to meet the F1 safety requirements established by the FIA in 2016, including the introduction of the HALO cockpit protection system for improved safety. It also incorporates revisions in its aerodynamics to balance competition and entertainment value, improving controllability when in close proximity to other cars so that it will be easier to overtake.

The car continues to use the NRE (Nippon Race Engine) introduced in 2014. This is a turbocharged 2 litre inline 4 cylinder with direct injection, specially developed by Toyota and Honda under common regulations and sharing the same components such as the turbine and ECU. The maximum output is unchanged at over <550ps>, but there is a very fierce development competition within the narrow range allowed between the two engine producers.
DescriptionLong.0x000049BE:

DescriptionLong.0x000049BF:
The winner of the 2015 Gran Turismo Awards at SEMA was an S30 Datsun Z, nicknamed the 'Fugu Z'. The car was built by the actor Sung Kang, known for his role in the 'Fast and the Furious' movie series. It is based on a 1973 240Z which he bought in a stock state, and it was custom built to his desired specifications.

The most notable feature of the exterior is the Rocket Bunny body kit consisting of very wide fenders and front/rear spoilers. And of course the car is not just for looks. The engine is the famed RB26DETT from the Skyline GT-R converted to natural aspiration, with mechanical tuning bringing its power up to <220ps>. Using E85 Indy car fuel, it can produce about <300ps>.

To withstand this power, a roll cage is welded to the interior. In order to reduce weight, the dashboard and console are custom made by CarbonSignal.

The name of the car 'Fugu' refers to the Japanese poisonous puckerfish. The fish is very poisonous, so it can lead to death if not treated properly. And the same can be said for the car.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C0:
The DB11 is a GT car that is the mainstream of Aston Martin, first announced at the 2016 Geneva motor show. It is the successor to the DB9, produced for 12 years starting in 2004.

While it takes on the traditional long nose coupé design of Aston Martin, the elegant but modern styling which deviates from the production Astons of the past is by Marek Reichman, their Vice President and Chief Creative Officer. Air is guided in from the front grilles and C pillar, going through the inside of the body and drawn out to produce aerodynamic effects, reducing lift and securing downforce.

The base structure utilises a new bonded aluminium VH platform, a completely new design evolved from the past models. Between its front axle and the cockpit is an also newly developed 5.2 litre twin turbo V 12. With a maximum output of <608ps> and a maximum torque of <71.4kgm>, it is linked with a ZF 8 speed, achieving 0-<100km/h> in 3.9 seconds with a top speed of <322km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C1:
The DB3S is a sports racing car that was active in racing until the mid 1950s. Its base was the DB3, developed during the famed David Brown years of Aston. While born in an era where the borderline between a road car and a racing car was fairly vague, the DB3, developed using DB2 components, was clearly for racing use.

Its further evolved DB3S model had a curved styling aiming to optimise and improve aerodynamics. Many structural changes were made for performance improvements, including the shortening of the wheel base and weight reduction. The inline 6 cylinder engine was tuned from <166ps> in its DB3 years to <185ps>, then to <228ps>, then ultimately to <243ps>. The car proved its performance in actual racing, with victories seen in not only British domestic races but in international races as well.

31 examples of the DB3S were produced. Out of these, the car with vehicle chassis number ‘1’ received the Gran Turismo Trophy at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, hosted in the U.S. in 2013.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C2:
The Aston Martin DBR9 GT1 is a racing machine created by Aston Martin Racing to compete in GT1 category races. The base car is the DB9, and its name is taken from the DBR1, the first racing car of the Aston Martin DB series which won the 1959 Le Mans 24 Hour Race with a 1-2 finish, as well as many other sports car races.

In addition to reinforcing the road car chassis, the body panels were all changed to carbon fibre excluding the roof. The gorgeous interior characteristic to Aston Martin road cars has been stripped, with even the dashboard replaced with carbon fibre for less weight. The car was made over <600kg> lighter this way, weighing in at only <1100kg>.

In addition to a wider fender, there is an additional front underspoiler, side skirts, rear diffuser and wing, plus the bottom of the car is made fully flat for improved aerodynamics.

The 5.9 litre V12 engine has undergone engine ECU tuning, raising its power from the <456ps>/<58.1kgm> of the road car up to <608ps>/<71.4kgm>. This is combined with an Xtrac 6 speed sequential transmission.

The DBR9 GT1 won its debut race at the 2005 Sebring 12 hour race, and until the GT1 category disappeared at the end of 2011, it had a spectacular career in racing. In 2006 it won the team and drivers' titles in ACO Le Mans Series, and in the FIA-GT it won the manufacturers' title. In 2007 and 2008, it won the GT1 class of the Le Mans 24 hour race 2 years in a row.J
DescriptionLong.0x000049C3:
The original Lancia Delta was a family-oriented hatchback designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro. However, when Group B was dropped from the WRC, Lancia chose the Delta as the base for their new Group A model and from that moment on the car's future was set.

In 1987, Lancia gave the Delta a high-performance turbo engine and a 4WD system, then debuted it in the WRC. From that year on, Lancia won an unprecedented six straight WRC championships, but during that time it was forced to go through an endless series of evolutions. Such is the existence of a competition rally car.

By 1991 Lancia was hard-pressed by its rival Toyota, and in response announced the ultimate Delta at the Frankfurt Motor Show: the HF Integrale Evoluzione.

The Evoluzione featured a larger front grille as well as enlarged air vents in the bonnet in order to improve engine compartment ventilation and cooling. As a result, power was increased from <200ps> to <210ps>.

One point of note was the widening of the wheeltrack by <60mm>. The signature blister wheel arches were further flared, increasing overall width to <1770mm>. Furthermore, by biasing the 4WD torque split toward the rear the car was made to behave more like a rear-wheel drive. A spoiler was also attached to the end of the roof, designed to generate downforce.

This Evoluzione made its WRC debut the following year in 1992, admirably contributing to the ongoing series of Lancia victories. Sadly though, Lancia's parent company FIAT decided to withdraw Lancia from the WRC, so the Evoluzione's activity came to an end that year.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C4:
In 2014, the Mazda 2 (Demio) entered its 4th generation with a full model change.

Styling-wise it employed Mazda's own 'KODO' design philosophy also found on their higher grade models, giving the car a presence that puts it on par with design-conscious European models. Another notable feature is that in addition to petrol engines, the car was also available with Mazda's newly developed 1.5L turbodiesel 'SKYACTIV-D' engine. This engine boasted performance equivalent to a 2.5L petrol engine, tuned to produce <25.5kgm> of torque for the 6-speed automatic model, and <22.4kgm> for the 6-speed manual model which was also able to achieve a stunning <30.0km/L> on the Japanese JC08 mode fuel economy test. These diesel models proved to be very popular, with over 60% of the initial orders being for diesel engined cars.

There are 3 model grades available for diesel cars. This included the base XD model, the XD Touring which includes practical options such as LED lights and cruise control, and the XD Touring L Package which offered such luxury options as white leather seats and a leather bound steering wheel, though the entire lineup offered quality beyond what was expected of its class.8
DescriptionLong.0x000049C5:
In 1999, the Lamborghini Diablo was given a minor exterior update that replaced the retractable headlights with fixed lights. In the Geneva Motor Show of the same year, the ultimate road-going limited version of the Diablo GT was announced.

The Diablo GT is based on the Diablo GT2, a pure racing car developed for the FIA-GT championships that was detuned and modified for street driving.

The 6 L V12, based on the Diablo GT2 engine, produces <575ps> and <64.3kgm> torque. On the outside, many of the outer panels were replaced with carbon fibre, reducing its weight by <40kg> from the Diablo SV at the time, down to <1490kg>. It showed superb performance, with its top speed reaching <338km/h>.

It was also given a special bumper spoiler to contain a larger oil cooler, and air outlets were added to the bonnet for discharging the heat from this cooler. All of these changes came from the experience gained in the Diablo GT2; in other words, everything different about this model came straight from the racing circuit.

There were only 80 cars produced, and the 80th car is displayed in the Lamborghini Museum at their headquarters. Being the ‘Ultimate Diablo’, it still captures the hearts of Diablo fans everywhere.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C6:
Ferrari had seen success in midship layout machines in the racing world, but 1968 was the year they decided to release a road car packed with this technology. The resulting Dino 206 GT was a beautiful Berlinetta with a flowing all-aluminium body, combined with a <1987cc> aluminium V6 instead of Ferrari’s traditional V12s. Another interesting point of note is that it was not given the Ferrari name, being sold as the 'Dino' alone, as though it were a model from a different brand.

The name Dino is taken from the eldest son of Ferrari’s founder, Enzo Ferrari. This was the nickname of his son and engineer Alfredo Ferrari, who passed away in 1956 at the age of 24. The 65-degree DOHC V6 engine, which he proposed while in the hospital, was successful in racing machines from 1957, and the 206 GT was a car that was in part used to homologate the F2 engine.

The Dino GT received a makeover in 1969, and became the 246 GT. The high-cost, difficult to produce aluminium body was changed to steel, while the engine and block were changed to cast iron. To compensate for the increased weight, the displacement was increased to <2418cc>, with output and torque improved from <185ps> @ <17.9kgm> to <195ps> @ <23.0kgm>. It achieved a top speed of <235km/h>. Other improvements included a longer wheelbase for better controllability, and its handling performance is still praised to this day.

In 1971 a Targa top 246 GTS was added to the lineup, and combined with the Berlinetta, a total of 3761 cars were produced until 1974.C
DescriptionLong.0x000049C7:
The 'DS' luxury brand of Citroën that began in 2009 became a completely independent brand separate from Citroën in 2015. This DS3 is a premium compact car announced in 2009, and while the platform and base mechanism is shared with the simultaneously announced C3, it was is further improved with its own unique styling and superior quality.

The DS3 Racing car announced at the 2010 Paris Motor Show is a special model developed by Citroën Racing, their competition department that competes in the World Rally Championships (WRC). The 1.6 litre direct injection turbo engine from the DS3 Sport Chic is boosted from <156ps>/<24.5kgm> to <207ps>/<28.0kgm> with additional work done to its turbo and exhaust system. The car is tuned throughout, with the chassis tread width widened by <30mm> and ride height lowered by <15mm> with special dampers and springs. The brakes are upgraded with 4 piston calipers and large diameter rotor discs and the wheels are changed from 17 inch to 18 inch rims. The interior and exterior are given bold colour combinations, setting it apart from other DS3s.

It was initially announced to be a limited production run of 1000 cars worldwide, but it became so popular that 2000 additional units were produced in 2011.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C8:
The origins of Jaguar trace all the way back to 1922, when William Lyons began gathering collaborators to start producing a motorcycle sidecar. By 1961, Jaguar was introducing the world to a completely new 2-seater sportscar, the E-type.

The E-type's engine was the same old-fashioned powerplant that had been used in the XK series ever since 1949, but the frame, suspension and body styling were built with progressive ideas that presaged the new era to come.

The first E-type was the last model with which Lyons, already withdrawing from the forefront, would be directly involved. The long, wide and low body proportions drew from the tradition of the C-type and D-type racing sportscars, and later they would have a great influence on sportscar styling around the world.

In addition to the convertible, the E-type line included a fixed-head coupé with a side-opening tailgate. The engine was a <3781cc> DOHC straight-6 with triple SU carbs and produced <269ps> @ <5500rpm>. Because of its light weight at 1219 kg, it reached a top speed of <210km/h> and boasted a 0-<100km/h> acceleration time of 7.2 seconds.

The brakes on all four wheels were servo-attached discs, born and bred on the racing field. In fact, the E-type was a pioneer as one of the first consumer cars to adopt disc brakes.

Given this performance, the roughly £2,630 price at the time was extremely reasonable. 7820 E-types were produced through 1964, and of those, 90% or more crossed the Atlantic Ocean and landed in the United States.-
DescriptionLong.0x000049C9:
The SEMA Show, one of the largest custom car shows in the United States, hosts the annual Gran Turismo Awards. In 2012, the 10th anniversary award went to a 1969 Ford Mustang customised by Eckert's Rod & Custom.

Based in Oregon, United States, Eckert's Rod & Custom has been working on the restoration and customisation of classic and muscle cars for over 25 years.

The winning car, named the Mach Forty, might appear at first glance to be a beautifully restored first-generation Mustang Fastback, but as its success would suggest, there's a lot more going on under the bonnet. Most of the body has been rebuilt, and the floor from the rear seats to the boot has been cut out to allow for a remade Ford GT power train to be installed, transforming the vehicle into a mid-engine design.

The supercharged 5.4L V8 power unit is custom-tuned to achieve a maximum of <862ps>, and includes a dial control fitted inside the car that allows the output to be adjusted from approximately <608ps> to <862ps>. Extensive work has been carried out in order to reinforce the body so that it can contain the raw power on offer. Other modifications include the suspension, reused from the Corvette C6, and a traction control system.

Eckert's Rod & Custom fused together two famous cars from Ford history into a bold concept, delivering a spectacular result that is truly worthy of the 10th anniversary award.7
DescriptionLong.0x000049CA:
The Enzo Ferrari is an ultra premium sportscar with a limited production of 399 cars, built in commemoration of the 55th anniversary of Ferrari.

The Enzo was designed by Ken (Kiyoyuki) Okuyama, a Japanese designer in Pininfarina at the time. The highly aerodynamic body is reminiscent of F1 machines of the day. It is notable that not only the body panels, but most of the frame is built of carbon composites.

The 6 L V12 engine was specially designed for the Enzo, and produces a massive <660ps> of power and <67.04kgm> torque. The suspension is double wishbone in front and rear, and combined with Brembo carbon-ceramic disc brakes, it can withstand full-speed runs on race circuits. With its powerful engine and lightweight body, its maximum speed is in excess of <350km/h>.

Though it mounts the high-power engine midship as in the F40 and the F50, it is also given gull-wing doors, air conditioning, and a semi-automatic transmission called the F1-matic. Measures have been taken against noise and vibration by mounting the engine to the subframe that is buffered by bushings, and it is designed to be more of a road car than the F50, which was closer to a pure race car.E
DescriptionLong.0x000049CB:
The Super GT is the most popular touring car race in Japan. Of the GT500 and GT300 categories in this race, a stepped bottom regulation was applied to the GT500 class starting in 2007. The regulation until then was a flat bottom, and the new rule was added to reduce cornering speeds by adding a <30mm> skid plate under the car.

The Honda NSX compensated for this regulation well and showed their speed, dominating the series by winning 5 rounds out of the total 9 rounds in 2007. In the following year they had to adhere to a regulation requiring the main frame to be used 2 years in a row, because of the overwhelming speed in the previous year a <50kg> weight handicap was applied to the NSX as a special performance adjuster from the opening of the series (<40kg> from round 3), and their engine restrictor was made even smaller.

In response, Honda revised detailed specifications of the <3494cc>, 32B V6 engine, to improve drivability. By additionally improving aerodynamics and reducing weight to minimise yaw momentum, they took on their rivals.

There were 5 NSXs competing in 2008, and the EPSON NSX, run by Nakajima Racing, was the only machine using DUNLOP tyres. For this reason they had a disadvantage in terms of data sharing, but Loic Duval and Katsuyuki Hiranaka bravely took part in the series, and finished in 2nd place in the 8th round at Autopolis, which was their highest position that year.

In that year's Super GT, where the Nissan GT-Rs showed their incredible performance, the two ranked in 10th place overall for the year.
DescriptionLong.0x000049CC:
The Jaguar F-Type that debuted at the 2012 Paris Motor Show is a sports car that was born as the heir to the famous E-Type, which itself ceased production in 1975. There was already a coupé & convertible XK series in the Jaguar line-up, but while the XK is a high performance grand tourer in line with the XJS, the F-type is a pure high performance sports car.

Initially the car started out as a convertible with an electric soft top and its styling and performance garnered high praise. One year later an elegant coupé model that was almost identical to the C-X16, the concept car of the F-type, was shown almost simultaneously at the Los Angeles Auto Show and the Tokyo Motor Show. The F-Type R Coupé was the high performance model in the line-up.

The 'R' designation indicates that this has the most powerful engine, the tightest suspension and the sportiest exterior and interior of the series. This, of course, applies to the R Coupé, where the high performance <495ps> 5 litre supercharged V8 engine of the most powerful convertible was tuned to <550ps>. This gave the car a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 4.2 seconds and a top speed of <300km/h>, at which point the speed limiter cuts in. Its electronic controls, such as the adaptive suspension and torque vectoring differential, have also been tuned to a sportier taste.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.^

DescriptionLong.0x000049CF:
The W08 EQ Power+ is a machine developed by Mercedes AMG Petronas Motorsport to compete in the 2017 F1 Grand Prix.

Mercedes made a full return to F1 racing in 2010 after a 55 year hiatus. They were one of the top 4 contenders from their starting year, but gradually gained in strength year by year, and from 2014 to 2016 they achieved double Constructors' and Drivers' championship title wins 3 years in a row. So aside from the changes to match new regulations for 2017, there seemed to be no major change in philosophy for their machine.

However there were frequent scenes where the drivers seemed to struggle with the setup as compared to last year, and where the car was fast in mid to high speed corners, it seemed to struggle with tracks that contained many low speed corners.

The power unit said to have produced approximately <950ps> was the most powerful out of the 2017 machines, and it was fast overall throughout the season. With Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas at the wheel, they achieved a fantastic 15 pole positions and 12 victories out of 20 races. Again this year resulted in a double title victory for Mercedes, winning both the Constructors' and Drivers' championship titles.
