DescriptionLong.0x00004A52:
The 3rd generation PRIUS was first announced at the January 2009 North American International Auto Show.

The improvements in the 3rd generation model were not just about environmental characteristics. It was also designed to be fun to drive.

In terms of mechanisms, the body lines were made sharp and aerodynamic, and in addition to enlarging the engine to 1.8 L, over 90% of the hybrid system was redesigned. As a result, it was endowed with the highest fuel economy in the world at <38km/l>, and truly established that the pursuit of eco driving can be fun.

The number of new users enjoying eco driving has clearly increased, and though the sales target was 10,000 cars per month, it made record sales of 18,000 cars in just a month after its release. Its high fuel economy and fun driving characteristics continued to attract users, and the PRIUS was on top of the sales charts for new cars 6 months running up to November 2009. The role of the PRIUS in establishing hybrid cars on the market was huge, and it was selected as Japan’s Car of the Year for 2009.

There is no major difference in mechanism between the 3 model grades of 'L', 'S', and 'G', but of course the tyres and other equipment details are slightly different among them. True PRIUS enthusiasts select their grade model by guessing the slight differences in fuel economy that could be caused by these differences. The top of the line 'G' grade is fitted with leather-wrapped steering and smart entry systems to raise its quality, but it is actually not the best grade to choose in terms of fuel economy.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A53:
Audi introduced full-time 4WD technology into the World Rally Championships in 1981, and showed incredible performance right from the outset. In 1982 they achieved a double victory for both the manufacturers' and drivers' titles, a drivers' title victory in 1983, and a double title again in 1984.

Year-on-year the car continued to improve, and in the autumn of 1983 they sold 200 of the 2133 cc 5-cylinder turbo-powered Sports quattros for Group B homologation, and it entered racing from 1984.

In 1985 at Tour De Corse, a further improved Sports quattro made its debut. This was the Sports quattro S1, also called the Sports quattro E2 in some countries.

The engine itself was basically unchanged but it incorporated improvements such as the misfiring anti-lag system, and the final output of the engine was increased to <600ps>. One improvement of note was also the transmission, a 6-speed semi-automatic with a clutch sensor in the shifter. Later in the year it was also given an aerodynamic body with front spoilers and large front wheel arches to match, together with rear arches with air inlets and a rear wing. By this time the car had matured into the ultimate rallying quattro.

In the same period, Audi modified a WRC spec Sports quattro S1 to hillclimb specifications and took part in the Pikes Peak International Hill Climb. The results were spectacular, with Michèle Mouton and Walter Röhrl winning and resetting the track record in 1985 and 1987 respectively.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A54:
The Audi R18 is a LMP1 class race machine developed by Audi to compete in the FIA World Endurance Championships (WEC).

The first appearance of the race machine dubbed the 'R18' was in 2011. This later evolved into the 'R18 Ultra' in 2012, and 'R18 e-tron quattro' from 2013-2015, continually evolving over its years in competition. The Audi R18 is the successor to this series, but while it carries over the R18 name, this was a very different machine from the past iterations, developed from scratch.

First, the aerodynamics were greatly revised. The front center section looks like a very narrow version of the high nose section of an F1 machine. Between this and the left and right fenders there is a wing, also like that of a formula car. The shapes of the front and rear fenders were also changed, with positions and sizes of the wheel housing air outlets changed as well. This car had a very different style from that of the previous R18 e-tron quattro.

Another major difference is the engine. While still a 4L turbocharged diesel, the regenerative energy storage device was changed from an electric flywheel to a lithium-ion battery, and the amount of regenerative energy discharge was increased from 4MJ to 6MJ. The output of the front MGU was also greatly increased from 200 kW (<272ps>) to 350 kW (<476ps>)

In the 2016 World Endurance Championship Series, 2 cars were entered from Audi Sport Team Joest. The R18 raised constant good results by winning 2 races, placing 2nd in 5 races, and 3rd in 2 races. Ultimately they achieved a respectable 2nd place in the Constructors point rankings for the year. However Audi decided to withdraw from the World Endurance Championship Series from the end of this season.}
DescriptionLong.0x00004A55:
The Audi R18 TDI is a prototype racing car developed by Audi for participation in Endurance races, such as the famed '24 Hours of Le Mans'.

This is a model that takes its heritage from a series of diesel-powered racing cars such as the R10 in 2006 and the R15 in 2009. The major difference between this and previous Audi LMP1 machines is that it features a closed body again, for the first time since the 1999 R8C.

While the previous R15 produced <600ps> from its 5.5 L V10 turbo engine, the R18 produces <540ps> from a 3.7 L V6 turbo. The closed body design was utilised to alleviate this loss of power by improving aerodynamics. The reason for these changes is due to the main objective of the car’s design to incorporate a near-futuristic hybrid system, which required the car to be as light as possible. This was the main reason for choosing a lighter V6 engine over the more powerful V8 engine allowed in the race regulations. The body is a carbon monocoque and even the gearbox housing was made of carbon to shave off more weight.

Much thought was given to the design of the engine as well. With a 120-degree V6 engine that mounts a single turbo between the cylinder banks, they were able to lower the centre of gravity and increase airflow on both sides of the engine.

The car’s racing debut was in the second race of the LMS in May 2011. In the pinnacle of the series at the Le Mans 24-hour race, the car from team Joest driven by Benoît Tréluyer, André Lotterer and Marcel Fässler succeeded in achieving the overall win in the race.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A56:
The Audi R18 TDI is a prototype racing car developed by Audi for participation in Endurance races, such as the famed '24 Hours of Le Mans'.

This is a model that takes its heritage from a series of diesel-powered racing cars such as the R10 in 2006 and the R15 in 2009. The major difference between this and previous Audi LMP1 machines is that it features a closed body again, for the first time since the 1999 R8C.

While the previous R15 produced <600ps> from its 5.5 L V10 turbo engine, the R18 produces <540ps> from a 3.7 L V6 turbo. The closed body design was utilised to alleviate this loss of power by improving aerodynamics. The reason for these changes is due to the main objective of the car’s design to incorporate a near-futuristic hybrid system, which required the car to be as light as possible. This was the main reason for choosing a lighter V6 engine over the more powerful V8 engine allowed in the race regulations. The body is a carbon monocoque and even the gearbox housing was made of carbon to shave off more weight.

Much thought was given to the design of the engine as well. With a 120-degree V6 engine that mounts a single turbo between the cylinder banks, they were able to lower the centre of gravity and increase airflow on both sides of the engine.

The car’s racing debut was in the second race of the LMS in May 2011. In the pinnacle of the series at the Le Mans 24-hour race, the car from team Joest driven by Benoît Tréluyer, André Lotterer and Marcel Fässler succeeded in achieving the overall win in the race.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A57:
On 21st August 1989, 16 years since the 'Kenmeri' GT-R was discontinued, the long awaited GT-R name returned to the 8th generation SKYLINE series.

Its engine was the newly developed 2.6L DOHC inline-6 twin-turbo, the RB26DETT. With ceramic twin-turbos, it produced <280ps> and <36.0kgm> of torque and it was lavishly filled with motor sports technology, including 6 linked throttle bodies, natrium-filled exhaust valves and a reinforced cylinder block. The drive system included the revolutionary ATTESA E-TS system, an electronically controlled torque-split 4WD system with a strong focus on 'getting the car to turn.'

The suspension utilised Nissan's unique multilink layout for both the front and rear, and it was combined with their Super HICAS 4-wheel steering technology. Aluminium callipers were introduced for the brakes, with 4-pot opposing pistons in the front and 2-pot opposing pistons in the rear.

The GT-R had made a 16-year comeback with a mission to win in Group A racing and Nissan placed all the technology it had at that time into the GT-R. It is well known that it successfully won many consecutive races and was an unbeatable presence on the circuit.

In addition to the limited edition NISMO version sold later on, there were also the later V･spec and V･spec II models that were further evolved in performance.*
DescriptionLong.0x00004A58:
In August 1993, the SKYLINE evolved into the 9th generation R33. However, the R32 GT-R was still produced until November 1994. The R33 GT-R did not debut on the market until January 1995.

Because the R32 GT-R was a legendary car that made its mark in history, everyone had their doubts as to whether the R33 GT-R could be better than the R32. Nissan cleared any doubt with actual hard numbers in their well-known television commercial, the Minus 21-second Dream. The R33 shortened the laptime of the R32 on the Nürburgring circuit in Germany by 21 seconds.

The concept of the R33 GT-R was 'the ultimate driving pleasure'. The engine was once again the RB26DETT which had become legend in its 1st generation. By raising boost pressure and improving the control CPU, torque and response in extreme operational ranges were improved, as well as its performance at the high speed range.

The revolutionary ATTESA E-TS 4WD system had also evolved, making the front-to-rear torque distribution closer to an FR car and improving controllability in turns. The V･spec was included as a catalogue model and an even more powerful ATTESA E-TS Pro was added. To enhance the rigidity of the body, a strut tower bar was added in the front and rear, and the car was made lighter by replacing the bonnet and front wings with aluminium.

To commemorate entry in the Le Mans, an LM Limited edition was also sold in 1996.^
DescriptionLong.0x00004A59:
The R34 GT-R model made its debut in January of 1999. Compared to the large R33, it was given a toned body, <75mm> shorter in length, and <55mm> shorter in wheelbase. Body rigidity was maximised and the advanced aerodynamics provided both cooling and downforce.

The engine was still the RB26DETT originally in the R32, but further refinements had been made, increasing torque and response, as well as reducing its weight. The effect of the ceramic turbos with reduced friction was significant and maximum torque finally reached the <#40kgm> mark.

Chassis performance was tremendously improved, allowing the car to be controlled exactly to one's bidding. The drive distribution controlled by the ATTESA E-TS Pro made it possible to change the orientation of the car on a whim. The steering no longer even feels like a 4WD, and even when compared to the legendary R32, its driving performance gives you a sense that this car is truly generations ahead.

The high-performance V-spec was the first production car to utilise a carbon rear diffuser that generates downforce and came standard with an active LSD. This V-spec was enhanced further in October 2000 to the V-spec II, equipped with a carbon bonnet with NACA ducts. In May 2001, the high-comfort M-spec, which took a hint from the suspension settings of Le Mans cars, was also offered.

In January 2002, a limited Nür edition, named after the Nürburgring circuit in Germany, made its debut. It was a special model equipped with an N1 spec RB26DETT. The history of the 2nd generation of GT-Rs which transformed the sportscar world ended here with this final model, due to newly introduced exhaust regulations.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5A:
The roots of the R8 lie in the Le Mans quattro concept car shown in 2003. In the commercial version of the car, the name was changed to the R8, after the prototype racer which successfully won several times in a row in the Le Mans 24-hour race.

The body utilises Audi’s ASF (Audi Space Frame), an aluminium structure chassis, and the body and shell weigh in at a mere <210kg>. There are no compromises for quality; with most of the body built by hand, an X-ray inspection device is used to check all welds at the micron level.

The centre section of the rear spoiler which lifts up at speeds above <100km/h> is a latticed grate, not affecting aerodynamics when standing, but dissipating heat from the exhaust when retracted.

The 4.2 FSI engine is a direct injection 4.2 L V8 that produces <420ps>. The drive system to relay this enormous amount of power is the quattro full-time 4WD system, the hallmark of Audi. A viscous coupling is utilised for the centre differential, and the variable drivetrain distributes 10-35% of the drive force to the front wheels.

In addition, Audi poured their newest technology into their supercar, implementing the Magnetic Ride system which includes dampers that utilise magnetic particles, and the R-tronic system that shifts using hydraulic pressure.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5B:
The Renault R8 Gordini was a sports model released in 1964 as a high-performance version of the compact ‘8’ Saloon. Amédée Gordini tuned the car by the request of Renault.

The 8 base car was full of advanced technology, such as a newly developed 5 bearing engine and being the first in its class to utilise four-wheel disc brakes.

Gordini utilised these advantages well. The <1108cc> engine with superior revving and endurance characteristics was an excellent component for 'The Sorcerer' Gordini to work his magic. The utilisation of a cross flow head with a sub combustion chamber and two twin-choke carburettors roughly doubled engine output to <95ps>, while maintaining the original displacement.

In 1966, the R8 Gordini 1300 was announced, with an engine displacement of <1255cc>. This car produced <103ps> with a 5-speed gearbox, extending its top speed by <5km/h> to <175km/h>.

The R8 Gordini dominated the Tour de Corse 3 years in a row from 1964, as well as many other competitions. From 1966, the world's first one-make race, the 'Gordini Cup', became the training ground for French racers, and produced many professional drivers. As such, this car is an icon of the French motorsports scene from the latter 1960s.

Its characteristic lunch-pail-like styling is still loved by fans everywhere. It is still popular as a collectors' car today, half a century after its first release.m
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5C:
The FIA-GT3 regulation racing car based on the Audi R8, the R8 LMS/R8 LMS Ultra, was successful in GT races around the world.

However, in March 2015 the R8 LMS racing car also underwent a model change in line with the full model change of the commercial R8.

The point of focus in the 2nd generation R8 LMS was safety. With crumple zones set in the front and rear of the car, the utilisation of the 'PS1' Audi Protection Seat from LMP machines and a roof rescue opening for the first time in a GT machine, this model already exceeded the safety standards for the next GT3 regulations to be instated from 2016.

Major changes have been made to the aerodynamics as well. Starting with downforce related changes, such as the now almost completely flat underfloor and a diffuser that has been enlarged in the design change, even the air circulation within the cockpit has been reconsidered to minimise the wear of the driver. As many improvements as possible have been incorporated within the tight GT3 regulations.

While using the production Audi space frame and a V10 engine built on the same production line as the mass produced engine, the vehicle weight has been reduced by <25kg> as a result of reviewing its material composition. The suspension was newly designed and the 6-speed paddle-shift transmission and traction control were also newly developed. Approximately 50% of the parts are shared with the mass production car, but the car has been thoroughly tuned where it needs to be.

This second generation R8 LMS debuted in the Nürburgring 24 Hour Race right after its sales began, taking the overall win in the race.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5D:
Nissan placed a lot of effort into Group C car racing in the 1980s, and developed an all-new 3.5 L twin-turbo V8 while carefully analysing the vehicle regulations for that class.

They mounted this engine in a chassis co-developed with the British company Lola. Dubbed the R89C, the car was entered in the European World Championships, the American IMSA, the All Japan Championship and the 24 Hours of Le Mans. Furthermore, they worked on developing their own chassis based on the R89C, and continued to improve performance.

However the FIA revised the vehicle regulations for Group C in 1990, and made the decision to prohibit turbocharged engines from 1991. Nissan would start the development of a new Group C car in response to this, but took notice that the All Japan Championship would continue races under the old Group C regulations until the end of 1992. Because of this, the development of the Group C car with the existing turbocharged engine continued, and the R92CP was the final version of the development.

The R92CP in the 1992 All Japan Championship was simply undefeatable. It closed the era of turbocharged Group C cars by winning all 6 races. The VRH35 engine had an officially announced output of over <900ps>, with the Le Mans qualifying special generating <1200ps>. This R92CP reached a maximum speed of over <400km/h> on the main straight at the Fuji Speedway, and it was said that it was still gaining speed before having to decelerate for the first corner. The down force of the body was extremely strong, reaching up to 3.5 tonnes.

In addition, the R92CP was a cutting-edge machine that raised concerns for the cockpit environment, with its design based on reducing fatigue of the driver. Its overwhelming victory was gained thanks to the meticulous thought and consideration that went into analysing an endurance race.e
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5E:
The NSX CONCEPT-GT is a racing machine of Honda, which raced from 2014 to 2016 in the GT500 class of the Super GT series. The base NSX is a concept car announced by Honda in 2012, a car in development for production as the new generation NSX. The concept utilised a hybrid system, combining a midship mounted V6 with electric motors.

As with other GT500 cars, the NSX concept GT is made under the new regulations introduced in 2014 which incorporated vehicle regulations of the DTM. The difference is that the 2-litre turbocharged inline 4, with direct injection that is uniquely developed under the same format between various companies, is mounted midship, and it incorporates a hybrid system in the same manner as the road car planned for production. However, in order to make it so that it does not give it an unfair advantage, a minimum weight was set, and the output of the electric assist and energy usage was also limited.

Though it experienced many issues in the initial year of participation, the NSX CONCEPT-GT started to pick up pace in 2015. However, in 2016, they experienced issues with supply from the battery manufacturer, and participated that year without the hybrid system. The Raybrig NSX CONCEPT-GT is one of those cars. In 2014 they placed 11th in the team rankings with Takashi Kogure and Hideki Mutoh driving, and in 2015 they achieved 3rd place in the series rankings with Naoki Yamamoto and Izawa Takuya at the wheel. 2016 was not a good year for any of the Honda teams, however, ending the series in 12th place.P
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5F:
The RC F is a high-performance coupé of the Lexus brand, announced at the 2014 Detroit Auto Show. Lexus has incorporated the character 'F' in the names of their high-performance models, signifying the Fuji Speedway. The RC F is again a model that greatly improves upon the performance of the RC sports coupé announced at the 2013 Tokyo Motor Show.

The engine is based on the 5-litre V8 of the IS F, with new titanium valves, forged connecting rods and newly designed cylinder heads and exhaust system. Its output is <456ps>/<53.0kgm>, raising power by <33ps> and torque by <1.5kgm> from the base engine. This is combined with an 8-speed automatic transmission with paddle shifters.

The VDIM, which centrally controls vehicle dynamics, was also further refined for circuit driving when set to Sports Mode. Its electronic devices have been further advanced and the car is also equipped with the first torque vectoring system in the world to be incorporated into a front engine, rear-wheel drive. This is because one of the core development concepts was to allow veteran and beginner drivers alike to enjoy dynamic sports driving performance.

With only the LFA as the exception, this is the sportiest model in Lexus history.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A60:
Lexus had been running a RC F based machine in the VLN series and the Super GT series since 2015, but this was as a specially allowed vehicle with no homologation. They used this experience to move forward with their development, and entered the RC F GT3 prototype in round 9 of the 2016 Fall VLN series. Here they successfully won the SPX class for specially permitted cars.

The prototype was developed with the intent of eventually delivering a GT machine to GT3 race teams around the world, so it was to be controllable for even amateur racers, and provide reliable performance with reinforced components. By changing designs through thorough durability calculations for every component, weight was reduced while securing rigidity. The design of various parts including the front and rear fenders was also changed to further improve aerodynamic performance. The engine is a 5 litre DOHC V8 of the production model tuned to over <540ps>. This car acquired homologation, and debuted as the Lexus RC F GT3 in 2017.

In the following year of 2017, the car was also provided to Emil Frey Racing of Switzerland, who were a part of the development team for the RC F GT3 machine. Participating in the GT Open Championship of Europe, they won 4 races out of 14, and placed 3rd in the season team rankings.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A61:
In the line up of the RC luxury coupé cars revealed by Lexus in 2014, there was a high performance model: the RC F. Based on this car, the RC F GT3 was developed as a racing machine to compete in the popular GT3 category races being held around the world.

The introduction of the RC F GT3 had already been in the works at the development stages of the road going commercial model, and its development proceeded in parallel with that of the road car. The V8 powering the standard RC F was converted to a dry-sump lubrication system and had its displacement increased to 5.4 L. This is combined with a 6 speed sequential gearbox, for a maximum output of <500ps>. Because the body houses large diameter slick tyres, the car features over fenders. Meanwhile, weight has been reduced wherever possible, with the vehicle weight kept down to <1300kg>.

Starting from the 2017 season, the RC F GT3 entered, and performed very well, in the American IMSA series (GTD category), the European International GT Open series, and the Japanese Super GT (GT300 class) races.

In the International GT race, it won the 2nd race at Silverstone for its first victory, and in Japan it won for the first time in the second round of the Super GT, held at the Fuji Speedway.

The RC F GT3 Prototype, represented here, is a car that was built for evaluating performance, just before the RC F GT3 acquired homologation. This car won the VLN (Nürburgring Endurance series) round 9 held on October 8, 2016. At the time of that race entry the car was still unpainted, with its carbon surfaces fully exposed, but the livery on the car here is of Emil Frey Racing, a top Swiss team who compete in the International GT Open.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A62:
The RC F is a high performance coupé of the Lexus brand, announced at the 2014 Detroit Auto Show.

Lexus has incorporated the character 'F' in the names of their high performance models, signifying the Fuji Speedway. The RC F is again a model that greatly improves upon the performance of the RC sports coupé announced at the 2013 Tokyo Motor Show.

The engine is based on the 5-litre V8 of the IS F, with new titanium valves, forged connecting rods and newly designed cylinder heads and exhaust system. Its output is <456ps>/<53.0kgm>, raising power by <33ps> and torque by <1.5kgm> from the base engine. This is combined with an 8-speed automatic transmission with paddle shifters.

The VDIM, which centrally controls vehicle dynamics, was also further refined for circuit driving when set to Sports Mode. Its electronic devices have been further advanced and the car is also equipped with the first torque vectoring system in the world to be incorporated into a front engine, rear-wheel drive. This is because one of the core development concepts was to allow veteran and beginner drivers alike to enjoy dynamic sports driving performance.

In terms of styling, its silhouette is common with the standard RC but there are additional aggressive details, such as the air outlets on the engine bonnet and at the rear end of the front fenders. On the boot is a variable rear spoiler that changes angles automatically according to speed.

With only the LFA as the exception, this is the sportiest model in Lexus history.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A63:
At the 2007 Frankfurt Motor Show, Peugeot displayed a concept car that was instantly recognisable for its elegant, flowing lines: the '308 RCZ'. This sports car was notable for its wide and low silhouette, with a cabin offset forward due to its midship layout. From the centre of the roof to the rear glass, a double-bubble design was utilised, giving it a unique style.

This was a design study based on the 308 but it gathered a lot of attention, with many fans wanting to see the car actually produced. To answer their call, the car was finally released in 2010 with a style that was virtually unchanged from the prototype. It was named with no 308 designation, but simply as the ‘RCZ’.

The engine is a 1.6 litre inline 4-cylinder turbo, with two models producing <156ps> and <200ps> respectively. The <200ps> version is given an engine that becomes more lively as the engine RPM becomes higher, and a suspension system carried over from the original 308 series is made stiffer for sports driving. The combination gave the car a level of performance that provided a fulfilling sports driving experience.

Then in 2012, the RCZ underwent a minor change. This was mostly a stylistic change with the opening of the grille made smaller, adding a black light unit and LED position lights, and the overall facelift of the front end gave it a chic style and appearance.

The GT Line is a grade model added from 2015, with a special front grille, double exhaust pipes, 19-inch wheels, and red-stitched black leather interior for a sportier look.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A68:
*The Eunos Roadster was sold as the Mazda MX-5 in Europe and as Mazda MX-5 Miata in the US.

The Eunos Roadster was the car that revived the lightweight sportscar category at the end of the 20th century. With a lightweight, compact body, a 1.6 L straight-4 DOHC engine, and a rear drive layout, it was a very traditional, lightweight 2-seater cabriolet.

The Japanese release was in September 1989. Initially the engine was the 1.6 L, B6-ZE, producing <120ps> and <14.0kgm> of torque. An aluminium powerplant frame connected the transmission and the rear differential, successfully creating a direct and rigid shift feel. A newly developed double wishbone suspension was used all around with four-wheel disc brakes, and it is said that everything relating to driving on this car was designed with a total disregard for cost. This is probably why driving the Eunos Roadster is often compared to the exhilarating feel of riding a horse, even more so because it is a cabriolet. The fundamental pleasure and the ability to control this car to your will captured the hearts of both new and veteran drivers everywhere.

In August 1993, some minor changes were implemented and a new 1.8 L DOHC, BP-ZE engine was introduced, raising the power to <130ps> and <16.0kgm> of torque.

In the 2nd minor change of August 1995, the final gear ratio and flywheel were modified, evolving towards the 1800 Series 2.

Many limited edition models were produced for the Eunos Roadster, and with Mazda having produced 531,890 units through to the end of 1997, this model set the world record for production of a 2-seater cabriolet and is even registered in the Guinness Book of World Records.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A69:
*The Eunos Roadster was sold as the Mazda MX-5/Miata in Europe/US.

This is an original tuned model created by Gran Turismo, based on the Mazda Eunos Roadster (NA Special Package) '89. The following is the description of the base model:

The Eunos Roadster was the car that revived the lightweight sportscar category at the end of the 20th century. With a lightweight, compact body, a 1.6 L straight-4 DOHC engine, and a rear drive layout, it was a very traditional, lightweight 2-seater cabriolet.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A6B:
The 4th generation Mazda roadster, the code 'ND' model, was announced for the first time in physical form at the New York Auto Show in April 2014. Although this was only a display of the chassis, engine, drivetrain and suspension, it could immediately be seen that the heavy items were mounted low and towards the centre of the chassis, that major efforts were made to reduce weight and that the driver sat slightly behind the centre of the car. The display succeeded in raising expectations of fans worldwide.

The next major update was in September of the same year. The styling was revealed simultaneously in Japan, the US and Europe and its sale was announced to begin in 2015.

The car has a low nose and shoulder line and is wide and low overall. Its elegant lines are glamorous, but the size of the body is still smaller than the previous type NC model. The car was received well worldwide, both in terms of size and design.

In 2015 more details regarding the car began to surface. The size of the car is <3915mm> × <1735mm> × <1235mm>, with a wheelbase of <2310mm>. The weight of the car is between <990kg> and <1060kg> depending on the grade model. The engine is a <1496cc> DOHC inline 4 producing <131ps>/<15.3kgm>. The transmission is offered in a 6-speed MT and a torque converter AT.

Pre-orders began in March 2015 and the available grade models were also introduced: the basic S model, the S special package with upgraded driving performance and the luxurious S leather package. The S model is not equipped with an LSD or rear stabiliser and the standard equipment is fairly simple.

However, at the same time this grade model weighs less than a ton at <990kg>, giving you a taste of the true nature of the new 'ND' Roadster.

*The Mazda Roadster was sold as the Mazda MX-5 in Europe and Mazda MX-5 Miata in the US.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6C:
Renault Sport is a group that has been making high-performance models based on Renault cars for many years now. The one-make race car revealed by this leader of French sports machines in the summer of 2014 was the R.S.01.

This purebred competition machine shows the deep partnership between Renault and Nissan. While the carbon monocoque chassis is co-developed between Renault and Dallara, the exterior was designed by a Japanese designer and the engine is a VR38DETT from the Nissan GT-R, tuned by NISMO.

The <4710mm> long, <2000mm> wide body only weighs <1100kg>. This lightweight chassis is propelled by a <550ps> V6 twin turbo. The expertise of Renault Sport has been applied to the aerodynamics and cooling for the car, so there are no doubts regarding its aptitude as a race car.

Renault Sport has also produced an offshoot version of this machine, the R.S.01 GT3. This is a machine modified to meet the FIA GT3 homologation, while maintaining the essence of the original R.S.01. There are elements of the conversion that actually tone down the car in terms of performance; carbon brake discs are changed to steel discs, and the engine power has been held down. However the GT3 category is now the most popular category of sports car racing; if it means that the R.S.01 will be seen more often on the track, it is a welcome change.*
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6D:
The Renault Sport R.S.01 is a special one-make race machine produced in small quantities for the 'World Series by Renault', hosted by Renault Sport. It was introduced from the 2015 season as the successor to the Mégane Trophy.

The body utilises a carbon monocoque developed together with Dallara, the Italian racing car constructor. The vehicle weight is held down to under <1100kg>. The engine is a midship mounted Nissan GT-R 3.8L V6 twin turbo tuned by NISMO, Nissan’s motorsport department. With an output of over <500ps> and over <61.2kgm> of maximum torque, and combined with an SADEV 7 speed sequential transmission, the car can hit speeds of over <300km/h>.

Based on this R.S.01, the Renault Sport R.S.01 GT3 was developed for entry in the FIA-GT Championships, and was announced at the French Paul Ricard circuit in November 2015. The R.S.01 GT3 had to be toned down in order to meet the GT3 regulations of the FIA; a restrictor was added to the V6 twin turbo engine to bring down the power, and the brakes were changed from carbon ceramic to steel discs. To meet the minimum weight specified by the FIA, over <50kg> of ballast weight needed to be added, and the aerodynamics were also revised. However, because the base car was designed as an exceptionally high performance machine, it is a car that has lots of room to spare in terms of performance when taking on challenges. X
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6E:
The MAZDA RX-VISION is a concept car announced at the 2015 Tokyo Motor Show. Based on Mazda’s 'KODO - Soul of Motion' design theme, this was a challenge to create the most beautiful FR sportscar that Mazda could come up with. This car is also powered by the next generation rotary engine 'SKYACTIV-R', a dream that Mazda wants to bring to life in the future.

Overcoming numerous technical difficulties, Mazda successfully introduced a commercial rotary engine through the Cosmo Sport back in 1967. Thereafter as the only manufacturer to mass produce rotary engines, they worked to improve output, fuel economy, and durability, and even took the overall victory in the 1991 Le Mans 24 Hour Endurance Race in their 787B.

The MAZDA RX-VISION GT3 CONCEPT expresses the design beauty of the base car in the form of a more aggressive race car. To meet the performance requirements of the Gr.3 category, the design draws from the 787B engine concept, with a 4 rotor engine brought back to life using SKYACTIV technology. This new rotary engine is mounted in a lightweight body to achieve unprecedented performance.N
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6F:
The Mazda RX500 is a concept sportscar that was built in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the founding of Toyo Kogyo, Mazda's original company name. It showcased Mazda’s rotary engine, the world’s first commercially applied rotary engine, which was first utilised on the 1967 Mazda Cosmo Sport.

The unforgettable bullet-shaped form was designed internally with a focus on aerodynamics. In the clay model stage there was a coupé model with a beautiful rear section, and a race version with a rear wing, but as a result of the focus on aerodynamics, this form, which produced a Cd value of 0.31 in wind tunnel testing, was utilised. The upward-opening door was introduced even before the appearance of the Lamborghini Countach.

The engine that is mounted amidship in the steel tube space frame is a 10A rotary engine that was built for the Spa 24 Hours race, producing over <250ps>. The transmission is a 4-speed manual from the RX87 Luce Rotary Coupe. The top speed was expected to be <250km/h>, and the brake system featured 4-pot calipers and 4-wheel ventilated disc brakes for deceleration from the high speed range. This was cutting-edge for its time, as very few racing cars used a setup like this in its day.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A70:
The RX-7 evolved into its 2nd generation 'FC3S' in October of 1985.

The futuristic 2nd generation model was shorter in length, but was wider and taller than the first RX-7, with a weight increase of approximately 200 kg. This was covered for by the newly designed 13B engine. With the displacement capacity of each rotor enlarged to <654cc> and combined with a turbo, the performance was improved to a maximum output of <185ps> and <25.0kgm> of torque.

The rear suspension evolved into a multilink layout, with a combination of semi-trailing arms and lateral rods. The rear suspension featured a unique toe control hub, enhancing the stability of the rear tyres while cornering.

The FC3S series also featured the Infini version, a limited edition model representative of a spartan driving style. The Infini was a high-performance, 2-seater model, omitting the rear seats and equipping BBS alloys, special shock absorbers, and an aluminium bonnet. The first Infini version appeared in August of 1986, but it was sold in limited releases seven times before production of the FC3S ended in 1991, and was a signature model of the RX-7.

In 1989, the RX-7 was given several minor changes. The 13B featured a new independent twin-scroll turbo and, with a high compression ratio, the power increased to <205ps> and <27.5kgm> of torque. The last model of Infini produced <215ps> and <28.0kgm> of torque. On the exterior, the three round tail lights was a distinctive feature of models after the minor change.

In 1987, a cabriolet was also added as a different twist away from the normal spartan racing image. It was a success in the US, and especially popular among female drivers.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A71:
The FD3S, the 3rd generation RX-7, debuted in December 1991. The name 'Savanna' given to the previous versions was dropped, and it was renamed the ɛ̃fini RX-7.

In order to accommodate wider tyres, the FD3S was significantly widened, but its bonnet, spare wheel, jack, and front and rear double wishbone suspension were all made of aluminium, keeping the vehicle weight down to a miraculous <1200kg> despite the size increase.

The engine was a 13B Turbo as in the FC3S. However with its new sequential twin-turbo, power output was raised to <255ps> and <30.0kgm> of torque. The weight-to-power ratio of the lighter Type S reached <4.90kg/ps>, and the car was the fastest RX-7 ever released, with huge potential.

The FD3S continued to evolve. Body rigidity, the computer, and ABS specifications were upgraded year after year. The Type I, created in 1991, evolved to Type II and III, and finally to the Type VI in 2000.

One of the highlights in this evolution was the limited edition Type RZ, the first Japanese car equipped with 40/45 low-profile tyres. Later in 2001, the Type R Bathurst R was sold with height-adjustable suspension, very unusual for a standard production car.

Of course the engine was improved as well. In 1996, the ECU, intake and exhaust were revised, enhancing power to <265ps>. In 1998, after refining the cooling system and engine, the <280ps> mark was finally reached. The weight-to-power ratio was now <4.50kg/ps> for the Type R, a performance figure equal to that of supercars.

However, the RX-7 was unable to survive the environmental standards of the 21st century. In August 2002, The RX-7 Spirit R was released as an anniversary model as the last of the series, marking an end to 25 years of production.O
DescriptionLong.0x00004A72:
The Toyota S-FR is Toyota’s lightweight sports car. This is 'a concept aiming to provide perfect control in an entry model, allowing the driver to enjoy interacting with the car in its everyday use'.

The body design contains the design essence from the famed Toyota Sport 800, with a long nose and cute rounded body. Meanwhile it also adds contemporary touches, matching the design to modern tastes.

At the 2015 world premiere the engine and other information were not revealed, introducing only the body size and other measurements; a <2480mm> wheel base, <3990mm> length, <1695mm> width, <1320mm> height, and the fact that it would be a 4 passenger vehicle. The front to rear weight distribution would aim to achieve 50:50 with 2 passengers on board, and the transmission would be a 6 speed manual.

In the 2016 Tokyo Auto Salon in January, Toyota also displayed a racing spec S-FR Racing Concept. Based on the cute and simple style of the S-FR, it was given a whole series of carbon fibre aerodynamic parts, including overfenders, front underspoilers, canards and a large rear wing. By exploring a design for maximising on-track performance, they showed new possibilities for the S-FR./
DescriptionLong.0x00004A73:
The Toyota S-FR concept was first revealed at the 2015 Tokyo Motor Show. The sporty car was compact at <3990mm> in length and <1695mm> in width, with a weight of only <980kg>. together with a long nose and short deck style and front midship rear-wheel drive layout, the car immediately gave an impression of being fun to drive. Though there are no plans for the commercial sale of the car, it gathered great attention from the visitors of the show.

The racing version of this car is the S-FR Racing Concept, revealed at the 2016 Tokyo Auto Salon. As the name implies, this is also a concept car.

With fenders flared out by <20mm> per side, a large air outlet on the engine bonnet, and carbon aerodynamic parts such as the large front spoiler, rear wing, side skirts and rear diffuser, the additions change the impression of the car from its rather cute original styling to give it the visage of a GT racing machine.

While the street version of the S-FR concept was <1320mm> in height, this car has been lowered by <50mm> down to <1270mm>, and with virtually no road clearance, the suspension settings are predicted to be quite hard. The front brakes utilise drilled disks, and horizontally opposed 4 pot calipers.

Even at this stage no details were given regarding the engine, and there was no announcement of any future commercial sales. However, of all the cars displayed at the Auto Salon that year, it gathered a lot of attention.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A74:
The Silvia is a series of speciality coupés from Nissan, and its 5th generation model, produced from 1988 to 1993, is the S13.

Initially Nissan had positioned the S13 as a fashionable dating car, but because it was a mid-sized FR which was already becoming rare at the time, and because of its strong engine and controllable chassis which made it suited for sports driving, it was loved by many street racers.

The Silvia came to be identified as a car for sports driving because of the S13. Of the S13s, the high-performance model in its early series was the Ks model. Its CA18DET turbocharged DOHC inline-4 engine, producing <175ps> @ <6400rpm> and <23.0kgm> @ <4000rpm>, was more than adequate for the <1140kg> car, and combined with the finely crafted rear multilink suspension that Nissan worked very hard to develop, it was a car which you could enjoy driving in any setting.

In February of 1990, a diamond select series was added to the Ks, Qs, and other grade models of the Silvia, which offered many optional parts including automatic A/C, aluminium wheels, and rear spoiler as standard equipment.N
DescriptionLong.0x00004A75:
After the S14 failed to achieve commercial success, the 7th generation Silvia (S15) made its appearance on the scene in January 1999. The biggest selling point of the S15 was that its body size was reduced, putting it in the same size class as the S13. It clearly tried to distance itself from the previous deviation towards luxury and set its direction as an appropriately sized FR sportscar.

The S15 continued to use the SR20 engine found in the S13 and S14. Fine tuning had progressed even further, with the naturally aspirated version producing <165ps> and <19.6kgm> torque, with the turbo version producing <250ps> and <28.0kgm> torque. The S15 was offered in two main grades, the naturally aspirated Spec S, and the turbocharged Spec R. Manual versions of the Spec R received a 6-speed transmission.

The S15 inherited its chassis from the S13 and S14, but to increase its appeal as an FR sport model, a major revision was made. By improving body rigidity, braking power and the suspension, and by adding a helical LSD, performance was increased dramatically in comparison to the previous model.

The Spec R, with its <250ps> engine and 6-speed manual transmission, boasted an admirable weight-to-power ratio of <4.96kg/ps>. Its ideal handling and high level of performance allowed drivers to feel a sense of flexible manoeuvrability. In the year 2000, a convertible model, the Varietta, was introduced with a naturally aspirated engine.

Though the S15 was the only compact FR car left in Japan, it didn't meet the exhaust emission standards for year 2000 and production ceased in August 2002. This marked the end to the Silvia dynasty that had lasted for an incredible 38 years.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A76:

DescriptionLong.0x00004A77:
Honda's classic S series included three-digit numbers representing their displacement in their names, as in the S500, S600 and S800. In April 1999, 28 years after the debut of the S800, the series was resurrected with a four-digit name in the S2000, created in honour of Honda's 50th anniversary.

Every part of the S2000 was specially developed in order to maximise its handling characteristics as a sports car.

Despite being an open-top convertible, the car's high rigidity 'High X-Bone' monocoque body provided equal or higher rigidity than comparable closed body vehicles. With a 9000 rpm limit almost unheard of in production cars, the naturally aspirated F20C 2L inline-4 engine is able to produce a maximum power output of <250ps>. It also boasted low fuel consumption, achieving a fuel efficiency of <12.4km/L> in the Japanese 10-15 standard test. The 6-speed manual transmission was also a custom design, and the development team poured their efforts into a complex secondary reduction gear in order to reduce weight and improve shift feel.

In July 2000, the Type V was added to the line-up, featuring the VGS system which could adjust the steering ratio according to car speed and turning angle. In 2007, the Type S was introduced which overhauled the aerodynamics and suspension in order to heighten the car's enjoyability on winding roads.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A78:
The S660 is an open top sportscar sold by Honda in 2015. This convertible sportscar in the ultralight Kei car class follows in the footsteps of the Honda Beat which ceased production 19 years earlier in 1996.

In terms of mechanical layout, the car is a rear midship 2 seater model. The body was newly designed from scratch, and the structure consists of straight lines and smooth curves. 60% of the whole car, from the centre tunnel, side sills and side frame uses ultra-high tensile steel, and the rear subframe is made of die cast aluminium. While keeping the total weight down in the low <800kg> range, the static twisting rigidity of the car even exceeds that of the S2000.

The roof is close to a Targa top in design, where just the area above the head can be removed. The soft top can be rolled and removed, to be stored in a box under the front bonnet.

The engine was developed based on the turbocharged <660cc> DOHC inline 3 used in cars like the N-BOX, and produces <64ps>/<10.6kgm>. The transmission is available in a 6 speed manual with close ratio 1st to 5th gears, and a paddle shift CVT with sports mode.

The suspension uses struts for all 4 wheels, and the car is given 4 wheel disc brakes. A torque vectoring system suppresses understeer in turns by applying slight brakes on the inside of the front wheels. The tyres are a special model that was developed together with Yokohama Tyres, which balances the front and rear grip. With all of these details combined, the car achieves unbelievable cornering speeds for a Kei model, all the while keeping a very neutral and fun handling performance.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A79:
Having dominated the world of two-wheeled racing in races such as the Isle of Man TT and World GP, Honda made its much anticipated debut in the world of four-wheeled cars in 1963. The car announced was an ultra-compact, 2-seater sportscar, the S500. Soichiro Honda, the hero of the Japanese post-war automotive industry, built this sportscar from scratch and took the industry by storm.

The Honda Sports line started with the S500, but less than half a year later its displacement was increased for more power in the S600. A special fastback coupé was also added to the lineup of convertibles and it performed very well in racing. At the time and even now, there were very few production cars which could rev up to <10000rpm> in stock factory specifications. As soon as you heard that soprano engine note, you knew that an 'S' was coming.

2 years later, the S800 with an even larger engine was added, and by the time the improved S800M made its appearance, the Honda sportscar was at a plateau of perfection. The suspension had become a true automotive 4-wheel design, and it was able to go flying into corners.

Starting with the S800, the Honda Sport series featured an exceptionally short shifter only <10cm> in length, which allowed effortless shifting from the car's low seats. Delivering a true sportscar experience and driving feel, these cars would become popular classics the world over.i
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7A:
The Sauber C9 was a Group C car developed by the Swiss constructor Sauber, led by Peter Sauber, in 1988. Beginning in 1986, Mercedes-Benz began supplying Sauber with Group C engines. And in 1988, Mercedes-Benz announced their return to Works racing activities for the first time since the 1955 Le Mans 24 Hours, with the Sauber team announced as their Works team.

Mounted on the aluminium monocoque chassis was a 5.0 L V8 turbo engine. In the 1988 WSPC (World Sports Prototype Championship), the Sauber Mercedes C9 succeeded in a pole-to-win finish in the opening round, and went on to win five of twelve races. In 1989, Mercedes-Benz changed the engine to a 4-valve per cylinder DOHC that increased maximum power output to a stunning <720ps>. The high-displacement V8 with its low-pressure boost and emphasis on torque was designed for a single purpose: to become the series champion.

The C9 works vehicle also had a completely new image this year, with its all-silver body. Many were intimidated by this, as they saw it as the return of the old Mercedes Works, who were feared in their day as the 'Silver Arrow'. The C9's overwhelming strength that year earned them a 1-2 finish at the opening round of the World Sportscar Championship at the Suzuka Circuit, and a 2-3 finish at Dijon.

In June, the C9 was entered in the Le Mans 24 Hours. Car #63 achieved a magnificent first place finish, while car #61 earned a respectable second place, with car #62 placing fifth.

The C9 continued to be successful in races thereafter. In 1989, with a recorded seven wins in eight races, Schlesser became the drivers' champion and Sauber became the team champion.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7B:
The Volkswagen Scirocco that made its comeback in 2008 is a sports coupé that was developed utilising the base components of the Golf.

The turbo and supercharger 1.4 TSI combination gained high praise for its performance when it debuted, but in 2009 an even better performance model was introduced. This was the Scirocco R, a model imbued with the technology fed back from the Scirocco which won its class in the Nürburgring 24-hour race, two years in a row.

The car’s low ride height, as well as its wide tread body styling, hints at its road holding capabilities. It is also garnished with special front/rear bumpers, side skirts and a roof spoiler reminiscent of the Nürburgring race car. Of course, the suspension and brakes are greatly improved and the 2.0 TSI direct injection turbo engine, combined with the twin-clutch DSG transmission, produces <256ps> @ <6000rpm>. This is the same engine as the one powering the Golf R which debuted almost at the same time. However, while the Golf R uses the 4motion four-wheel drive system, the Scirocco remains front-wheel drive in order to keep its weight down.

As a result, it is <120kg> lighter than the Golf R at <1410kg>, and is the quickest high spec sports model in the Volkswagen line-up.

With its dynamic engine sound, sharp cornering and daily utility, this is a unique mix that fills the roles of both a practical and a sports driving car.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A7D:
*The Nissan 180SX was sold as the Nissan 240SX in the US and as the 200SX in the EU.

The 180SX debuted as the Silvia's sister hatchback model in March 1989. This car, sporting front retractable headlights and a glass hatchback, did not initially leave a very big impression as it was overshadowed by the hugely popular Silvia. Even though it shared its 1.8 L engine with the Silvia, the 180SX was only offered in a turbocharged model.

In 1991, the engine changed to a 2.0 L SR20DET with <205ps> and <28.0kgm> of torque. The 180SX production run was supposed to end here to be replaced by the Silvia which was due for a full model change. However, thanks to the continued popularity of the 2.4 L version sold in North America named the 240SX, Nissan decided to continue production of the 180SX separately from the Silvia.

Although the 180SX shared its basic components with the old S13 Silvia until the end of its series, several minor changes were made to keep its performance level current. The car was slightly on the heavy side and the rear end lacked rigidity due to its hatchback configuration. This was the reason that the 180SX was initially considered inferior to the Silvia in performance. However, a wealth of aftermarket tuning parts allowed the 180SX to overcome its weakness. Many fans added unique modifications, which paved the way for a very original model; the S13 Silvia front end was mated to the 180SX, and the car was specially dubbed the Sil-Eighty.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7E:
The Mercedes-Benz Vision SLR was first shown at the North American International Auto Show in 1999, and stole the show. Its production model finally made its appearance at the Frankfurt Motor Show in 2003.

Officially called the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren, its construction is handled by the famous British F1 constructor McLaren. The SLR's main identifying characteristic is its carbon monocoque body. With the exception of its aluminium engine bay, the SLR utilises carbon everywhere else in its monocoque body, keeping its weight down to <1768kg>. In comparison to the SL55AMG, it is over <200kg> lighter.

The SLR's power unit is a twin-supercharged 5.5 L SOHC V8, tuned by AMG, that has a maximum power output of <625ps> @ <6500rpm> and a maximum torque of <79.6kgm> @ <3250rpm>-<5000rpm>. The SLR has the same 5-speed automatic transmission that the SL uses, but has sport, comfort, and manual settings. In addition, the manual setting offers the ability to customise gear shifting speeds.

Of course, the brakes use the SBC (Sensotronic Brake Control) system, and the brake discs are fibre-reinforced ceramic. The front brakes use Brembo 8-pot calipers and the rear uses 4-pot calipers. Both the front and rear suspension use a conventional, double wishbone mechanical suspension.

The weight-to-power ratio of the SLR is an unbelievable <2.8kg/ps>. Official data states that the car can accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in only 3.8 seconds with a top speed reaching <334km/h>. The SLR McLaren was an astounding 435,000 Euros in its native Germany and £330,000 in the UK.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7F:
The SLS AMG, with its gull-wing doors reminiscent of the classic 300 SL, debuted at the 2009 Frankfurt Motor Show as a super sports car, built from the ground up by AMG. In Japan it was shown for the first time in September of the same year, not at a motor show but at the Gran Turismo booth of the Tokyo Game Show.

It is often thought of as the successor to the SLR McLaren, but the body structures of the two cars are very different. In the SLS AMG, the high-cost carbon monocoque body was abandoned for a new all-aluminium body; the weight of the bare monocoque is only <241kg>. At a total weight of just over <1600kg>, it is undoubtedly very light for a car that exceeds <4600mm> in length and is powered by a V8 engine.

The front-mounted engine is a new 6.3 L V8 with dry-sump lubrication, dubbed the M159 internally in the company. Its maximum output is <571ps> @ <6800rpm> with a maximum torque of <66.3kgm> @ <4750rpm> and the transmission is a newly developed 7-speed DCT (dual-clutch transmission) in a transaxle layout. The driveshaft and torque tube are made of carbon fibre.

The driving modes can be set to Comfort, Sports, Sports Plus, Manual and Launch Start. Manufacturer specs boast a 0-<100km/h> acceleration in 3.8 seconds, with a maximum speed of <317km/h>. The static weight distribution is optimal at 47:53, giving it superb handling performance befitting a super sportscar. 50 years from the birth of the first 300 SL, the SLS AMG is packed with the history of Mercedes sports cars and the DNA of AMG.C
DescriptionLong.0x00004A80:
The Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG, which debuted at the 2009 Frankfurt Motor Show was a super sportscar developed independently by AMG, the high performance car development division that also serves as the motorsports division of Mercedes.

It was immediately in the spotlight all over the world for having gull-winged doors reminiscent of the famous 300 SL, as well as for the fact that it had performance specs on par with Italian rivals.

Mounted front mid-engine in the all aluminium space frame was the M159, a tuned 6.2 litre V8 engine based on the AMG63 series engine. It produced <571ps> and <66.3kgm> of torque and combined with a Getrag 7-speed DCT, it achieves 0-<100km/h> in 3.8 seconds with a top speed of <317km/h>.

The SLS AMG GT3 was a racing car based on this SLS AMG, modified to comply with FIA GT3 regulations.

The front and rear bumpers and side sills have been changed to a more aerodynamic design, adding an adjustable wing at the rear. The front/rear wings were also widened, and a cooling duct was added to the bonnet. Aside from being functional, the styling is notably more aggressive. The engine is shared with the commercial car and although there are no official figures, it is said to have been tuned to exceed <600ps>.

The transmission was changed to a full racing 6-speed sequential with paddle shifters. Composite brakes were utilised with competition ABS, the steering was made direct-ratio and the car was given a special adjustable suspension.

This car participated in races starting in 2011 and out of the 101 races it took part in this year, it won 25 times.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A82:
The Toyota Sports 800, nicknamed the 'Yota-Hachi' (Hachi meaning 8 in Japanese) by many, appeared in 1965 to prove that light weight and compact size are what make a sportscar. It was also one of the earliest cars in the world to feature a mechanism where the roof could be removed while leaving the B-pillars on the car, a system which later came to be called Targa tops.

There is clever innovation in its build as a sportscar. What they tried to achieve was a complete adherence to simplicity rather than utilising complex components. Because of this most of the parts were carried over from the Publica economy car, and when you floored the accelerator you could hear the characteristic whirr and 'put-put' of the horizontally opposed 2-cylinder air-cooled engine, complementing its rounded cute looks with a humorous sound.

Despite its demeanour, however, the car was actually a wolf in sheep's clothing. With its simple design and use of aluminium and acrylic parts throughout the body, it had a vehicle weight of only <580kg> - which was a considerable advantage as a sports car. The <790cc> engine only produced <45ps> even with twin carburettors, but because of its light weight it was capable of <155km/h>, equal to <1500cc> class cars of its day.

Although 'eco-friendly' and 'conservation' have become buzz-words of the 21st century, the 1965 Toyota Sports 800 was a groundbreaking model that was way ahead of its time, together with its timeless design.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A83:
The SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo is an uncompromising, unrestricted single seat mid-rear engine, all-wheel drive vehicle.

The main power plant is a nearly flat, 144-degree 6.98-litre V10 engine generating in excess of 1,000 horsepower, supported by a pneumatic sub-unit. Offering 4 levels of assistance, the pneumatic power unit uses regenerative braking to compress air and store it in 2 pneumatic cylinders, and release it as needed. The power from this pneumatic unit is also used in the suspension system.

The handling dynamics of the Tomahawk are enhanced by a continuously active aerodynamic system which deploys multiple pneumatically driven elements, including a rear wing and a secondary front splitter. The Tomahawk’s aerodynamic system reacts to inputs provided by a forward scanning laser system that detects surface changes in front of the car. The computer controls anticipate changes in vehicle ride height, pitch and yaw and adjust the splitter accordingly. The exhaust of the V10 engine is routed to the rear diffuser. This accelerates underbody flow at the rear of the car and creates a blown diffuser effect that increases downforce with no negative effect on drag.

 The GTS-R is the most lightweight and race-ready form of the Tomahawk concept. The extreme g-forces resulting from its immense power output, extremely light weight and increased handling grip, are more than the human body can handle unassisted. For this reason, the driver requires a special racing suit that pressurises the entire body to maintain blood flow to the brain. This G-suit uses excess pressurised air from the pneumatic power system, allowing it to quickly react to increasing g-forces.

The Tomahawk GTS-R’s aerodynamics are enhanced with a dual-element version of the active rear wing. The upper element is stored beneath the lower element when not required or when low-drag/high-speed manoeuvres are requested. Each of the four fenders is vented to avoid any high pressure build up in the wheel wells.'

The SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo is a 20-year-forward vision of uncompromising, unrestricted performance. It is the virtual fusion of extreme motoring and stunning design. The Tomahawk is a single seat MR-AWD (mid-rear engine, all-wheel drive) vehicle constructed on a purpose-built composite chassis and designed around an aggressive powertrain.

This system provides the Tomahawk with All-Wheel Drive capability to improve cornering and acceleration when grip at the rear wheels is traction limited.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A85:
The SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo is a near-future supercar created by Dodge's cutting edge special development team SRT. This juggernaut is a vision of next generation automobile technologies, high-tech materials are used throughout the chassis which utilises a road surface sensing active aerodynamics system and houses a 1,000 horsepower V10 engine supported by pneumatic power units.

The SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo (Gr.1) reuses the core concepts and dynamic nature of the Tomahawk and modifies them to create a Gran Turismo Gr.1 category regulation vehicle.

This version is based on the racing spec GTS-R, the lightest model in the series. However, in overhauling the body size, the characteristic active aero parts have been scrapped, replaced by a large fixed rear wing as well as a shark fin to the rear of the cabin. 

In the interest of weight reduction the pneumatic power units have been removed, with the V10 engine now tuned to produce <703ps>. The power train layout has also been changed from all-wheel drive to rear-wheel drive to comply with regulations.

While it is no longer capable of extreme speeds which test the limits of the human body, its superb handling and aerodynamic control remain intact. In long endurance races, this model is sure to be an intimidating presence for its rivals.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A87:
At the 1970 Turin Motor Show, Bertone introduced a concept car called the 'Stratos Zero'. With a completely wedge-like silhouette and a front windscreen that serves as the door, it was simply a design study, but Bertone already talked of this car as being a midship design. After the show development started with Lancia, who at the time were looking for a rally machine to replace the Fulvia.

Marcello Gandini was the one who refined the design for mass production. He utilised the strong wedge shape of the Stratos Zero, and created a sharp exterior befitting the 'Stratosphere' name. This was how the Lancia Stratos was born.

The body of the Stratos consists of a strong welded-steel monocoque frame with fibreglass exterior panels. The engine located behind the seat is the same 2.4 L DOHC V6 as the Ferrari Dino 246 GT.

Its driving performance can be guessed from its wheel base and tread width; with an extremely short wheelbase of <2180mm>, and a wide rear tread of <1457mm>. This produced ultimate turning ability and nightmarish sensitivity. As a result, driving a Stratos requires some serious driving skill, but because of its performance it was nothing short of fantastic in rally racing, and brought a period of glory for Lancia in rallying.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A88:
Vision Gran Turismo is a revolutionary project established for car enthusiasts all over the world. The car provided by Subaru for this dream project, where the world's car manufacturers and brands develop concept cars in the game world, is an ultimate sportscar carrying Subaru's concept car motto 'VIZIV'; Vision for Innovation. The car is called the 'SUBARU VIZIV GT Vision Gran Turismo'.

Inheriting the design language of Subaru's 'SUBARU VIZIV 2 Concept' revealed at the March 2014 Geneva show, the Subaru design team have added dynamic and solid shapes to the model. Its shoulder line extends from the front hexagonal grill all the way to the rear. Its tough-looking body seems as though it was carved from hard, solid metal. And with blister fenders extending its shape three dimensionally outward, it visually expresses Subaru's pursuit of a safe and enjoyable driving experience. Its large diffuser, the roof integrated rear spoiler, and its shooting brake silhouette, which accounts for aerodynamic performance, will surely stand out among others in the game.

Thorough weight reduction was a focus in the design of the body structure, and carbon materials have been utilised everywhere. As a result, the vehicle weight was held down to <1380kg> despite being equipped with heavy batteries and motors. And propelling the lightweight body is Subaru's legendary 2 litre horizontally opposed engine that has been fully tuned with years of motorsports experience. The direct injection turbocharged engine that has been powered up with revised restrictor diameters is combined with one high-power motor in the front and two in the rear, which achieves a total system power output of <600ps> and 800 Nm (<82kgm>) of maximum torque. By independently controlling each of the motor outputs, turning ability while cornering is drastically improved, while the torque vectoring lamps built into the fenders visualise its movement. Thus, as with any other Subaru, the car is made controllable for anyone driving it, regardless of its extremely high performance levels.

Experience the 'SUBARU VIZIV GT Vision Gran Turismo', a car that delivers Subaru's ideals of confidence and driving pleasure through an unprecedented aggressive desngn and extreme levels of performance.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A89:
The Supra is Toyota’s high-performance GT which debuted in February of 1986. It was originally a model that branched out from the Celica XX (known as the Supra in the U.S.), a derivative model of the Celica which debuted in 1981. It had been a long-nosed, hatchback coupé aimed at the North American market, but with the rising sportscar boom in Japan, it was taken to the next step, evolving as a high-performance sports model.

The body size of the Supra, which shared its platform with the Soarer specialty car, was <4620mm> long, <1690mm> wide and <1310mm> tall. The suspension is double wishbone for all 4 wheels, a first in Toyota since the 2000GT. The rear differential utilised a subframe to balance driving performance and comfort.

The initial engine lineup was led by the type 7M, a 3L turbo producing <230ps>. There was also a 2L twin-turbo with <185ps>, a 2L DOHC with <140ps>, and a <105ps> 2L SOHC. Various models were added to the lineup thereafter.

One of the most talked about of these variations was the 3.0 GT Turbo A that appeared in 1988. This was the homologated model that had been released for participation in the Group A All-Japan Touring Car Races, and which boosted the 7M-GTEU engine to <270ps>. It was a model which utilised the same <1745mm> wide body as the North American spec model, with low-profile, size 50 tyres and improved suspension.

In a significant change introduced in 1990, the 3L engine was removed from the lineup, and the top grade became the 2.5GT twin-turbo R, powered by a new 1JZ-GTE engine. This model produced <280ps>, which was at the maximum power limit that was self imposed within the Japanese car manufacturing industry at the time. This made the Supra join the ranks of high-performance sportscars, and it reigned as the king of Toyota Sports models for 7 years running.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8A:
The Toyota Supra ended production in 2002 to the dismay of many fans worldwide, but the car made its comeback in the 2019 North American International Auto Show.

This flagship Toyota model, which carries over the inline 6 cylinder engine and rear wheel drive, is headed by chief engineer Tetsuya Tada, who also brought the Toyota 86 to life. Under the slogan 'Numbers are one thing, feeling is what matters', he proceeded to create a car that speaks to the senses of the driver. Optimally balanced with a 50:50 weight distribution and a low centre of gravity, it provides powerful acceleration with a twin scroll turbo. The quick handling enabled by the wide body and short wheelbase is a result of a pursuit to achieve an ideal sports car, and its glamorous and elegant form and straight six engine sound combines to gives it an aura that is unrivalled by others.

The sportscar was developed for not only real motorsports but also with competition in Gran Turismo Sport in mind. Expectations are high for its glory in both real and virtual racing.
