DescriptionLong.0x00004A8C:
In May 1993, the Supra, Toyota’s GT car, was reborn into a new model.

Going against the original idea of the powerful, American macho-car, the engineers at Toyota wanted to create a new stoic and spartan impression with this new generation model. The long nose design was changed to a glamorous, masculine body, and while the width increased by <120mm>, the total length was reduced by <100mm>, giving the car proportions more ideal for a sportscar.

The interior is arranged simply in black, with 5 independent dashboard instruments, including an analogue clock.

The engine line-up was kept simple, offering a 2JZ model, 3 L DOHC inline-6 in twin-turbo or NA. The twin-turbo produces <280ps>, while the NA produces <225ps>. The twin-turbo 2JZ-GTE engine is often used as a base for tuning, and <500ps> spec engines are common.

The transmission was available in a 5-speed MT, 4-speed AT, and a 6-speed MT. This transmission was developed in co-operation with Getrag of Germany, and was provided together with Bilstein suspension on spartan sports models such as the SZ-R, RZ, and RZ-S.

The suspension is the same 4-wheel double wishbone as in the previous model, but its geometry, as well as other specs, have been completely redesigned. With increased rigidity in various areas, and tuning of the dampers and bushes, controllability has been greatly improved.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8D:
The Suzuki Swift Sport is based on the 2nd generation Swift, a model aimed at the global market. The European model is a 3-door, but in Japan it is also offered in a 5-door variant.

Its development was undertaken mainly in Europe, and was based on the production model rather than a prototype. Though this delayed the release to be later than the model change, this European development was imperative to perfect the level of tuning on the car. For the same reason, it was subjected to numerous tests, under a wide variety of road conditions.

One merit of developing in Europe was that they gained the partnership and support of Teneco. Their know-how, gained from their Monroe brand, helped to perfect the driving performance of the Swift Sport.

The engine is a 1.6 L normally aspirated engine, combined with forged pistons and VVT, and tuned for driving in the high rpm range.

In the minor update of 2007, the maximum power did not change but the rev limit was increased from <7000rpm> to <7500rpm>. By introducing cross-ratio gears for the 5-speed MT, its power can now be more effectively applied and appreciated. It is also equipped with an ESP, a feature which is becoming more common amongst European cars, and the overall quality level of the car has been improved. The interior also used to have many red trim parts, but these have been reduced for a more mature, chic colour scheme.s
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8E:
The Taycan is Porsche’s answer to the question of sustainable mobility, their first fully-electric vehicle.

A sports sedan that combines sports performance with everyday usability, its electric all-wheel drive system uses 2 electric motors mounted on the front and rear axles, with the rear-motor encompassing a revolutionary 2-speed transmission allowing unparallelled acceleration and efficiency at high speeds.

Both the Turbo and the Turbo S models normally output 460 kW (<625ps>), but with the overboost feature engaged the output of the Turbo model is boosted to 500 kW (<680ps>), and the Turbo S cranks out a staggering 560 kW (<761ps>). This incredible power output is enabled by the first 800-volt power unit to be seen in a production car, which successfully achieves greater efficiency while drastically reducing charging time.

And of course no effort has been spared in producing dynamic handling. It features Porsche’s superior active suspension management and torque vectoring technology, controlling these systems in sync to provide the best possible driving experience under all driving conditions. Taycan’s technical advances also extend to its user interface, enabling media and air-conditioning to be operated directly through its intuitive voice control system.

The Taycan carries forward Porsche’s historical lineage while signalling a new era of automobiles. Truly a model in which heritage meets the future.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8F:
The U.S.-based Tesla Motors first announced their Roadster in 2006, an open-top, 2-seater EV. At this time many car companies were still experimenting with how to bring electric cars to market, but Tesla started delivery in 2008, and in 2012 they sold out their initial planned production of 2500 cars, making steady progress in bringing electric cars to the mass market.

The second model for the Tesla lineup, announced in 2009, was a 5-door saloon, the Model S. The body size of the new car is just between a Mercedes S class and E class, and the design, with its sharp nose and short front/rear overhang, was by Franz von Holzhausen, originally of Mazda’s North American Design Centre.

The interior is made of environmentally friendly materials, including 100% recyclable PET plastic and no-lead Italian leather. There is a 17' touch screen on the interior panel that centralises all information features, and a 3G service that allows continuous connection to the internet is available as an option.

The powertrain utilises a newly developed, liquid-cooled 9' motor, with lithium-ion batteries under the floor. The battery is available in 3 capacities according to price, and the highest capacity type allows a total driving distance of 300 miles. It can be charged from a household plug, and is compatible with 110 V, 220 V and 440 V. It can be charged in 4 hours using 220 V, and in as short as 45 minutes with 440 V.

The top grade Signature Performance boasts a maximum output of <416ps> and a maximum torque of <61.2kgm>. More than just adequately sporty, the 0-60 acceleration is a mere 4.4 seconds.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A90:
The 86 GRMN, which started internet-only pre-orders in January 2016, is a completely tuned car built by Toyota based on their popular ‘86’ sports car. The ‘GR’ in GRMN stands for Gazoo Racing, the team who race Toyotas in various motorsports activities. The ‘MN’ stands for ‘Meister of the Nürburgring’.

Gazoo Racing have competed in the Nürburgring 24 hour race since 2012 in the 86, and have won their class twice since. The 86 GRMN is the ultimate 86 containing all the know-how gained from their racing efforts.

The chassis is made stiffer with the addition of reinforcements. In order to lower its centre of gravity, the bonnet and boot lid, as well as the roof, have been changed to carbon, and the rear and rear quarter windows are made of polycarbonate plastic. Aerodynamic parts such as the front spoiler and rear wing are specifically developed parts designed for effectiveness. The car has been made into a full 2 seater, with special Recaro bucket seats and a small diameter steering wheel.

For the engine, intake and exhaust parts have been replaced, and the friction of internal parts has been reduced to improve response and power in the high RPM range. As a result, both power and torque have been improved from the standard model by <19ps>/<1.2kgm>, to reach <219ps>/<7300rpm> and <22.1kgm>/<5200rpm> torque. To fully utilise the new specs a close ratio 6-speed manual transmission is added to the mix.

Of course, the chassis has been tuned as well. Specially developed dampers and springs are utilised for the suspension, and even the tyres are special models developed in conjunction with Bridgestone, with different sizes for the front and rear wheels. The brakes utilise opposed 6 pot monoblock calipers in the front and 4 pot in the rear.

The 86 GRMN is a 100 car limited production model and despite its price tag, which was over double the price of the standard model, it received orders reaching 30 times the number of available cars.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A91:
The Toyota 86 is a sports car released in 2012, combining a relatively compact body with a rear wheel drive layout.

The quick, controllable character of the car is inherited from the popular Corolla/Sprinter AE86 of the 1980s. This character was even more pronounced with the front midship layout and the 2 litre flat 4 engine that provides the car with a low centre of gravity, and was welcomed by car enthusiasts who love to drive.

In 2016, the 86 received its first minor update. Rather than just an update to its looks, it received a number of improvements affecting its driving performance, including an increase in the number of spot welds to increase the rigidity of the body, and a change to the shape of the front spoiler to improve aerodynamics. The power of the 6 speed manual version was raised to <207ps>/<21.6kgm>, and Sachs dampers were also made available as an option on all models.

The GT 'Limited' version is the top grade model of the 86. This is the more 'mature' model of the lineup, with high quality materials such as leather and alcantara used for the interior.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A92:
The FT-86 Concept was announced in 2009 as an exciting compact, front-engine, rear-wheel drive sportscar developed in co-operation by Toyota and Subaru, and it heightened the expectations of car enthusiasts everywhere. In 2011, the commercial model of its Toyota version finally debuted at the Tokyo Motor Show.

The FT (Future Toyota) designation has been removed, making its official name the Toyota 86. This new generation 'Hachi-Roku' (8-6 in Japanese), named after a popular predecessor in the 1980s, has a silhouette close to the FT-86 II Concept shown at the 2011 Geneva Motor Show. It is designed under the 'Aero Handling' concept, in which the car is held to the ground from all directions through superior aerodynamics.

The naturally aspirated <1998cc> 4-cylinder DOHC boxer engine mounted front-midship in the car produces <200ps> @ <7000rpm> and <20.9kgm> @ <6600rpm> torque, which is then transferred to the rear wheels through a short-stroke 6-speed MT or paddle-shifter 6-speed AT.

The front-to-rear weight balance is 53:47, and is designed this way for controllability of the rear end and excellent steering feedback. The centre of gravity of the car is equivalent to that of supercars, at only <460mm> off the ground. The standard grade MT model weighs in at <1230kg>, and there are also grade models that come standard with a limited-slip differential.

Each and every part of the new generation Hachi-Roku is designed specifically for this car to allow quick handling and control, and the result is a sportscar that is like an extension of your own hands and feet. This is a car in which you can enjoy exceptional handling that will make you feel as if you were a part of the car.

There are also plans for a lineup of Modellista and TRD custom parts, and a customisable grade model for competition use. This is a new generation, lightweight sportscar that truly caters to the car enthusiast.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.

The centre of gravity of the car is equivalent to that of supercars, at only <460mm> off the ground. The standard grade MT model weighs in at <1230kg>, and there are also grade models that come standard with a limited-slip differential.

Each and every part of the new generation Hachi-Roku is designed specifically for this car to allow quick handling and control, and the result is a sportscar that is like an extension of your own hands and feet. This is a car in which you can enjoy exceptional handling that will make you feel as if you were a part of the car.

There are also plans for a lineup of Modellista and TRD custom parts, and a customisable grade model for competition use. This is a new generation, lightweight sportscar that truly caters to the car enthusiast.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.B regulations by Gran Turismo.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A94:
Following the excitement of the FT-1 release in the Gran Turismo 6 game, the CALTY design team from Toyota’s North American Design branch have taken their dream one step further in creating the ultimate racing car, the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo.

The designers’ original intention in designing the FT-1 was to unabashedly appeal to the die-hard car enthusiasts. In the same way, the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo is designed for die-hard Gran Turismo fans. The designers focused on keeping the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo authentic for the virtual racetracks of the game, to maximise their driving pleasure.

As the bones and architecture of the FT-1 already lent themselves to cooling and downforce through 'function-sculpting' the vision version just needed to be enhanced as a pure racing car. The designers closely studied racetracks and racing cars, and applied their research into the styling. A deep sense of rawness is evident in the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo, due to its purely function-driven design aesthetics. The fenders and tyres are wider for extreme grip on the track. The enlarged air intakes provide increased cooling, and a larger rear wing and additional front canards have been added for even more downforce. The rear diffuser has been enlarged with multiple vertical fins, and is moved further back for cleaner airflow.

The FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo looks and feels the way it performs, so the driver can speed through the racetracks with the same sensation and thrill of real racing.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.T

DescriptionLong.0x00004A96:
In May 1983, Toyota's mainstream car, the Corolla/Sprinter, underwent a full model change and became an FF vehicle. However, as a special exception, the sport model continued to be an FR; this was the AE86 Corolla Levin/Sprinter Trueno, nicknamed the 'Hachi-Roku', meaning eight-six in Japanese.

The 86 immediately became popular as the last lightweight FR. There were two body types: a 3-door hatchback and a 2-door notchback. The main difference between the Corolla Levin and the Sprinter Trueno was the front end; where the Corolla Levin had a horizontal grille and square headlights, the Sprinter Trueno had no grille and was fitted with retractable headlights.

The engine was the newly developed 1.6 L 4A-GEU, a DOHC inline-4. To make the most of the DOHC, the airflow meter was removed in favour of the EFI-D (Electronic Fuel Injection-Druck) system, which calculates the amount of fuel injection required using a pressure sensor. Additionally, it was equipped with the T-VIS (Toyota Variable Induction System) at the inlet port, reaching a maximum output of <130ps> and maximum torque of <15.2kgm>.

The pickup of the light engine combined with the sharp, responsive steering provided an incredible driving feel, even though engine performance was not all that amazing when actually driving. Its handling was not very stable, either. However, it was possible to use this instability to change the orientation of the car at the driver's will. It was a true FR, where the driver could feel at one with the car.

During its time, there were rival cars with similar specs, but the 86 was loved by many car fans who appreciated the fun of driving and the exhilarating feeling it gave them. There were many cars which came later boasting higher performance, but it is hard to find a car that is loved by as many as the 86.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A97:
The popularity of the AE86 Levin/Trueno platform, known in Japan as the 'Hachi-Roku' (eight-six), has not diminished in the more than 25 years since it first appeared. The car here is a Trueno owned by Shuichi Shigeno, author of 'Initial D', a popular comic book series in which the AE86 plays a main role.

The AE86 platform enjoys a long history of engine tuning, with many different upgrades chosen over the years, from carburettor conversions and superchargers to the addition of turbo kits. The method chosen here was perhaps the most common of all AE86 upgrades: conversion to a 4-barrel throttle body. Further upgrades like high-compression pistons and a high-lift camshaft help bring out the famous 4A-G engine's character even more, making for an exciting power curve, where engine response is sharp and torque delivered generously with increasing revs.

For the engine control unit, a MoTeC full computer was used for superior control, enabling the engine to attain <210ps> maximum output, which is close to the physical limits of the 4A-G under a naturally aspirated tune. The exhaust system employs an HKS manifold and Trust exhaust to extract more performance from the engine and also give a sporty sound.

Rigidity was increased by reinforcing the body panels in key areas. Weight reductions like replacing the stock bonnet with a carbon-composite one knocked about 100 kg off the stock kerb weight.

The suspension saw a classic AE86 upgrade as well with the addition of a TRD suspension kit. When paired with the stiffened chassis and lighter body, the new suspension makes for agile handling and enables high cornering speeds.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A98:
The TS030 Hybrid is a prototype race car that was developed by Toyota to race in the 2012 24 Hours of Le Mans and the WEC (World Endurance Championships).

As can be guessed from its name, it comes from the lineage of machines that raced the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the 1990s, such as the TS010 and TS020. Its major difference however is that it utilises a hybrid system.

The THS-R (Toyota Hybrid System-Racing) powertrain was developed in cooperation between the Toyota production hybrid development team and the motorsports department of the East Fuji Research Lab, utilising a newly designed, naturally aspirated 3.4 litre V8. The power storage unit is not a battery but an electric double-layer capacitor. The Denso motor unit is built into the rear gearbox.

The drivers of this racing machine were Alexander Wurz, Nicolas Lapierre and Kazuki Nakajima. For the 24 Hours of Le Mans a second car was driven by the formidable line-up of Anthony Davidson, Stéphane Sarrazin and Sébastien Buemi.

In its debut run at the 24 Hours of Le Mans it ran in the top ranks, but was forced to retire due to unfortunate accidents and problems. However, they thereafter proved that the speed they exhibited at the Le Mans was for real, consecutively producing outstanding results from the 4th round of the WEC. Of the 6 races they participated in they won 3, with 3 pole positions and 4 fastest laps. Although they did not partake in all the races of the series, they still managed to place 2nd overall in the WEC series.P
DescriptionLong.0x00004A99:
The TS050 Hybrid is a prototype racing car, developed by Toyota in 2016 to compete in the LMP1 class of the FIA World Endurance Championships, which includes the famed Le Mans 24 hour race. Two years prior to this, in 2014, Toyota became the series champion in the TS040 Hybrid. In 2015 they ended the season in 3rd place, and the TS050 was developed from scratch to attempt a return to the top once again.

As with its predecessor, the car was still an all-wheel drive hybrid with a MGU in the front and rear wheels, but the powertrain was greatly changed from the previous naturally aspirated 3.7 litre V8 to a twin turbocharged direct injection 2.4 litre V6. The battery was changed from the super capacitor with fast charge and discharge characteristics to a high power lithium-ion battery developed for racing, with a high power storage capacity. The total system output, including the engine and front/rear motors, is <1000ps>, making it equal to the TS040 in this respect, but the torque had been increased significantly due to the turbocharging.

Also, the MGU of the front wheels was made more compact, which allowed design changes to redirect the airflow under the car, further improving its aerodynamic performance.

Two TS050 Hybrids participated in the World Endurance Championships from the TOYOTA GAZOO Racing team. One was driven by Kazuki Nakajima / Sébastien Buemi / Anthony Davidson, and the other car was driven by Kamui Kobayashi / Stéphane Sarrazin / Mike Conway. In 2016 the Kobayashi team showed great speed and were a contender for the Drivers' Championship, but in the end they finished 3rd in the season rankings, and also placed 3rd in the Manufacturers' rankings.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9A:
Audi was hesitant at first about producing a compact 2+2, but when the TT concept was greeted enthusiastically at the 1995 Frankfurt Motor Show, the company went to work in making the car a reality, and the TT 1998 bowed to a waiting public.

The base engine was a <180ps> 1.8 L DOHC inline-4, the same engine that powered the Audi A3 and Audi A4. The choice for enthusiasts though was a re-tuned version with dual intercoolers that pumped out <225ps>.

Because of the compact size of the TT, it was one of the most nimble cars in the marketplace. Built on the A3’s platform, with wheelbase shortened <9cm>, the TT displayed excellent cornering balance with a slight penchant for understeer. The all-wheel drive version had a more neutral turning character, helped in part by the double wishbone rear suspension.

The TT’s popularity was increased even more by an attractive convertible version in 2000 and the addition of a 3.2 litre DOHC V6 in 2003. With <250ps> on tap and mated to the company’s revolutionary DSG twin-clutch semi-automatic gearbox, the TT became the luxury 2+2 of choice for discerning enthusiasts.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9B:
The TT Cup is a racing car developed by quattro GmbH based on the Audi TT. It is a car made specifically for the one-make races started in 2015, the ‘Audi Sport TT Cup’.

The road version of the TT coupé utilises aluminium for the outer panels and the upper part of the frame, but the TT Cup car uses carbon fibre for some of the body shell. By further removing comfort equipment, it is over <100kg> lighter than the lightest commercial model on the market, at <1125kg>.

The fenders are enlarged in both the front and rear in order to fit 260/660R18 tyres. The front and rear bumpers are special low profile designs for improving aerodynamics, and in the rear is a large adjustable rear wing.

The engine is the 2.0-litre TFSI inline 4 used at home in Germany. Power is unchanged at <310ps>, but in order to make the race more interesting with more overtakes, the car is equipped with a push-to-pass button which temporarily gives an additional <30ps> for a short period of time. The gearbox is the same 6-speed S tronic shared with the road going car.

The front axles are equipped with an electronically controlled Haldex hydraulic limited slip differential, and the driver can adjust the locking ratio from the cockpit.

Though the ‘Audi Sports TT Cup’ is positioned as an entry level race, the race is sometimes held as an opening race for the DTM. The race has been very popular, and in 2016 there were a total of 125 participating drivers.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9C:
The 3rd generation Audi TT debuted at the 2014 Geneva Motor Show. As with its transition from the first to second generation, the concept for the car was kept in the full model change. The silhouette of the rounded two-door coupé was retained, but the front-end was tightened up with an enlarged single frame grille and R8-like headlights.

While many cars become bigger with every model change (the wheelbase was extended by <37mm>) the total length was shortened by <10mm> and the width was reduced by <8mm>, making it slightly smaller than the previous model. The chassis, combining aluminium and steel using the Audi Space Frame Technology, has been made lighter by thoroughly reviewing the application of materials and is <50kg> lighter than the previous model using the same engine.

In the interior it inherits the simple design of the previous generations, while replacing the meter panel with a 12.3 inch TFT screen. The car navigation maps and other information are displayed in the 'virtual cockpit' system.

The TTS sports model is equipped with a 2.0 TFSI inline 4 cylinder turbo, tuned to produce <314ps>/<38.7kgm> in the German domestic model. This is combined with a 6-speed manual transmission and the quattro system, with a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 4.7 seconds and the speed limiter cutting in at <250km/h>. The Audi Magnetic Ride variable damper is equipped as standard and a dual clutch, semi-automatic S Tronic with launch control is offered as an optional feature.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9D:
The Tundra is a full size pickup truck developed and sold for the North American market by Toyota.

The first model was rather small and struggled in sales. Because of this, Toyota expanded both the body size and engine displacement for the 2nd generation model that debuted in 2007. This led to greatly improved sales and made the Tundra a very popular model.

From 2014, it underwent minor changes that give it powerful looks, and in 2015 the 'TRD Pro' version was introduced. This TRD Pro was tuned by Toyota’s motorsport department, TRD. In order to improve its driving performance on rough roads, this model utilises TRD coils and Bilstein dampers in order to improve the stroke characteristics of the suspension.

The TRD Pro was dropped from the lineup for some time afterwards, but returned as a catalogue model again in 2019. Based on the Crewmax 4x4 with a 5.7L V8, the suspension was further tuned with Fox dampers, and its sporting character is further raised with equipment such as the new bonnet scoop and BBS wheels.C
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9E:
The TVR, taking on a part of Trevor Wilkinson’s name as a part of the company name, started business as one of many specialist car manufacturers in the UK. Their first production car, the Grantura, debuted in 1958. Even back then, an FRP body with a characteristic styling was combined with production car components, from cars like VW and Austin Healey, to produce high driving performance in the TVR style.

The Tuscan, sold in 2000, was a revival of a sportscar bloodline of the same name, a model that wreaked havoc on circuits in the 1960s.

The 2-door, 2-seater coupé with unique styling utilises many curved surfaces, and bears little resemblance to the 1st generation model. It is still one of the most aggressive styles in the world.

Because of this seductive styling, the body size seems fairly large, but in reality it is fairly compact at <4235mm> long, <1810mm> wide, and <1200mm> wide. The wheelbase is also short, at <2361mm>.

The engine is a 4 L DOHC 6-cylinder engine, developed in-house. The name 'Speed 6' comes from this 6-cylinder engine. It boasts a dry-sump lubrication system with an oil cooler, and an inline-6 throttle body to control intake air, built to a level on par with racing engines.

Power output is <365ps>, with a maximum torque of <42.86kgm>, and accelerates the lightweight <1100kg> body violently forward.

It is far from being a modern car in many respects, but is a car in which you can enjoy the very fundamental joys of driving a raw, unadulterated sportscar.P
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9F:
The Volkswagen created by Dr. Ferdinand Porsche had a plethora of ideas packed into the small chassis, as well as infinite possibilities. The cars were developed into a range of variants, from off-road cars for battlefields to sportscars like the Porsche 911.

This Sambabus is an example of its transformation into a van with a large luggage space. Because the engine is mounted in the rear in the same manner as the old Volkswagen Beetle, the nose is extremely short. With the flat horizontally opposed engine, the floor of the luggage room is also lowered, and is a classic example of the Volkswagen methodology in attaining the maximum space in a minimum body size.

The actual height of the car is relatively low at less than <1600mm>, and it is said this is because they did not want to raise the air resistance with a high height. Still, because the floor of the car was very low to the ground, it had more space than its rivals, and it was also very high in cost performance. Its small turning radius, thanks to its short wheelbase, and the versatility of its compact size, also gave it a lot of advantages as a commercial van.

The round headlights and the rounded front end design were practical but cute in appearance, and are often used as a motif of other custom cars. Volkswagen is well aware of the important image of the Sambabus, and has already introduced this in taller concept cars of this segment.\
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA0:
Italy’s Carrozzeria Zagato was established in 1919 at Monza, located just outside of Milan. Their particular talent lay in building lightweight car bodyshells utilising technology from aircraft manufacturing. Alfa Romeo (who have been producing sportscars since before World War II) took note of this, and they were very successful in the racing world using these Zagato-built bodyshells. This collaboration continued even after the war, and together they have created many attractive models that have become a notable part of automotive history.

One of the foremost examples of this was the TZ which debuted in 1962. This was a model intended for racing application, and as the name Tubolare Zagato implies, it mounted an aerodynamic aluminium body on a steel tubular space frame. Mounted on this extremely lightweight chassis (weighing only <660kg>) was a DOHC 1.6 L engine from the Giulia series, producing <112ps> @ <6500rpm>.

The TZ2, appearing in 1965, took the TZ one step further and made it even more competitive. It is said that the total production was probably 10 or 12 cars, and there have also been examples of TZs being returned to the factory to be refitted as the TZ2. Unlike the TZ, which was released as a road-going car, the TZ2 was a complete racing spec car from the outset.

The major difference of the TZ2 was that the body was built of FRP to make it <40kg> lighter, with its nose and roof lowered for better aerodynamics. Its engine was also upgraded using the same twin ignition head from the GTA, to produce <172.4ps> @ <7500rpm>, and its top speed significantly increased from <215km/h> to <245km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA1:
The Aston Martin V12 Vantage GT3 is a pure racing machine, participating in GT races from 2012 when it replaced the successful DBR9/DBRS9 models.

The car is based on the top performance model in the Aston Martin catalogue line-up, the V12 Vantage that debuted in 2009. The 5.9 litre V12 engine of the flagship DBS, producing <517ps> and <58.1kgm>, is mounted in the slightly smaller, lighter and agile V8 Vantage body, giving it a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 4.2 seconds and a top speed of <305km/h>; even faster than the DBS. It gained a strong reputation for its well-balanced handling performance befitting the Vantage series.

Based on this road going model, the V12 Vantage GT3 is a racing car developed to match the FIA GT3 regulations. The front and rear fenders are greatly enlarged, a ground scraping front spoiler and a huge rear wing has been added, making the original elegant styling of the car appear much more aggressive. The engine was tuned to <600ps> / <71.4kgm> and the transmission was changed to an XTrac sequential transmission with paddle shifters. The weight of the car was reduced down to <1250kg> and the front-to-rear weight distribution was re-balanced to be roughly 50:50.

The V12 Vantage GT3, delivered to racing teams around the world, showed its great potential from the year of its debut. In 2012 there were 18 wins and 30 podium finishes with the car; in 2013 there were 17 wins and 34 podium finishes. This racing machine has reinforced Aston Martin’s glorious racing history since their full return to motorsports in 2005.z
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA2:
The third generation Vantage came 5 years after the 2nd generation model ended production, debuting in 2005. The Vantage had been positioned as the high-performance model previously, but the new model was placed as the low-end model in the lineup; with a strategic price tag that was set surprisingly low for an Aston Martin.

The 3rd generation Vantage was sometimes referred to as the ‘baby Aston’ for this reason, but its targeted rival was now the Porsche 911. For this reason, this Vantage was developed to truly pursue driving performance of a front engine rear wheel drive sportscar. The basic structure of the flowing coupé body carried over from the DB7 is a unique bonded aluminium space frame called the VH platform, started from the DB9 announced in the previous year. Lighter than the 2nd generation Vantage by almost <400kg>, the car weighs in at <1570kg>.

The power unit is a naturally aspirated V8 based on the model from the Jaguar XK. In actuality it has been so modified that the only thing in common is the shape of the block, producing <385ps> from 4.3 litres. Gradual improvements brought the power up to <406ps> in 2007, and in 2008 the displacement was increased to 4.7 litres with <426ps>. In 2011 it was further increased to <436ps>.

The high-performance Vantage S is the car powered by this <436ps> version of the engine. Not only is it <10ps> more powerful than the standard model, the dampers, springs and bushings are stiffer, with a quicker steering gear ratio that makes it more suited for sports driving overall.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.#

DescriptionLong.0x00004AA4:
The Veneno is a special model of Lamborghini introduced at the Geneva Auto Show in 2013. This is a limited production road car commemorating the 50th anniversary of Lamborghini; only a total of 3 cars were ever sold.

The Veneno is based on Lamborghini's flagship Aventador, with a stunning exterior design and precision aerodynamics that hint at a new generation of Lamborghini. The front section includes an extremely low V shaped front nose and has all the properties of a front wing on a formula car. Combined with the high mounted variable rear wing, gigantic rear diffuser and a shark fin that extends from the roof to the rear wing, massive downforce is created to help increase cornering speed.

The full time four-wheel drive system is combined with a pushrod suspension and powered by a 6.5 litre V12 engine, with a 7-speed 2 pedal MT as in the Aventador. However, for the Veneno the engine power has been raised to <750ps>. Together with additional weight reductions, including a carbon monocoque, the car is <125kg> lighter than the Aventador at <1450kg>. The performance difference is clear: 0-<100km/h> is attained in 2.8 seconds, with a top speed of <355km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA5:
The ultimate high-class supersport. That is the definition of the Bugatti Veyron. Along with the display of the production model at the 2005 Tokyo Motor Show, a limited production of up to 300 vehicles over 5 years was announced.

Bugatti is a legendary sports car manufacturer born in 1909. The Volkswagen group acquired the brand name and manufacturing rights for Bugatti in 1998 and developed the Veyron. It was planned for production at Molsheim in France, where Bugatti was originally founded.

The Veyron attracted attention not just for its looks, but also for its extraordinary £850,000 price tag, <1001ps> power output and unbelievable maximum speed of <407km/h>.

The 8 L, W16 engine is equipped with four turbochargers, producing <1001ps> @ <6000rpm>. The transmission is a twin-clutch, 7-speed DSG developed specifically for the Veyron.

The body, designed at the Volkswagen design centre, was built of carbon fibre and aluminium alloys, in order to achieve speeds of over 250 mph. The vehicle height and rear wing angles change in 3 modes: standard, top speed and handling mode. To enter the top speed mode, enabling speeds of over <375km/h>, it is necessary to insert a special, separate key when parked and stationary.

The 0-<100km/h> acceleration is 2.5 seconds, 0-<300km/h> acceleration is 16.7 seconds and deceleration from <100km/h>-<0km/h> is achieved over a distance of <31.4m>, in 2.3 seconds. To achieve 250 mph it is said to require a straight road approximately <12km> long. Everything about this car, its price, specifications, production quantity and top speed is the ultimate in exclusivity. This is why the Veyron sits at the pinnacle of dream super sportscars.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AA7:
The Dodge Viper evolved into its 3rd generation model at the 2012 New York Motor Show. With the appearance of this iconic American sports car, the development of a GTS-R competition model was also announced, and it became clear that the Viper would return once again to the Le Mans 24 hour race and American Le Mans series after a 10-year hiatus. And the Viper GT3-R is a GT3 machine created for private teams, based on the GTS-R works machine.

In the development of this machine, SRT (the high-performance car development division of Dodge) and Riley Technologies (a major race constructor of the U.S.) worked together to instil the car with their know-how for victory.

The traditional long nosed, short deck body has improved aerodynamics with a flat bottom and the addition of a wing. Weight has also been reduced to <1295kg> (2855 lbs). The 8.4 litre V10 with a dry sump is powered up to <680ps> (507kW) unrestricted, and this power is transferred with an X-Trac 6-speed sequential transmission. It is also equipped with 6 piston front/4 piston rear brake calipers with large diameter discs for stopping power.

The Viper GT3-R was priced at $459,000, with orders received from the latter half of 2013. Its level of performance is already proven in various GT Car races in the US and other parts of the world.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA8:
The Viper debuted as a concept car in 1989, and was released on the market in 1992. Though it sported overwhelmingly high specifications, it was also said to be too retro in taste by some. In 1996, these negative reviews were quelled with the birth of the Viper GTS, a true sportscar with a rigid, closed body. It drew a clear line between it and the roadster.

To truly emphasise the vehicle's sports orientation, a race version, the GTS-R, was also announced at the debut of the GTS. This was a production race car with aims for entering endurance challenges such as the Le Mans and Nürburgring 24-hour races, as well as other GT car races around the globe.

The basic mechanical components of the GTS, including the V10 engine, frame, and suspension, are the same as the RT/10 roadster. However the engine was upgraded from a maximum output of <400ps> to <456ps>.

Though the acceleration of the GTS did not differ much from the RT/10, its maximum speed was greatly improved. The advantage of a coupé body style was significant, raising the top speed of the GTS to <298km/h>, from the <265km/h> top speed of the roadster.

The rigidity of the body was also greatly improved with the closed body, and its timed performance was clearly improved in slaloms and on skid pads. In addition, some of the reinforcements that were necessary on the roadster were possible to omit with the closed body, actually making the car lighter.

The original Viper was a nostalgic and primitive feeling sportscar. However with the release of the GTS, the Viper has joined the ranks of the supercar.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA9:
The achievement made by the Viper in the American automobile industry is significant. For a long time the only choice in the American supersport market was the Corvette, but the Viper challenged and defeated the Corvette when it first appeared in 1991.

This led to an escalated R&D battle between the two and as a result, the performance standards of American sports cars quickly rose to a level that sometimes exceeds that of mainstream European supercars. For this reason there were many disappointed fans when sales of the 2nd generation Viper ended in 2010.

The Viper was far from dead though, as a 3rd generation model debuted in 2012.

The 3rd generation Viper was released by SRT, Chrysler's dedicated sports model brand. Although it basically keeps to its original concepts, its performance has been greatly improved. The platform still uses the square steel space frame as before, but with aluminium cross bracings its rigidity is improved by 50%.

With lightweight materials such as carbon used in various parts, the car is 45 kg lighter. The V10 mounted front mid-ship is still 8.4L, but with changes in pistons, intake, exhaust and engine management, it now produces <649ps> and <83kgm> torque. The upper grade model GTS is also equipped with active suspension.

Its top speed: <330km/h>. Considering the base price of the 2013 model is under $100,000, the bite and venom of the 3rd generation Viper will definitely have an effect on its rivals.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AAB:
The Viper, which debuted in 1992, transformed into its 2nd generation model in 2003, when the Viper SRT10 was announced at the 2003 North American International Auto Show. As with the 1st generation model, it was only available in an open-top model at first, but in 2005 a Viper SRT10 Coupe was released as the 2006 year model. The SRT (Street and Racing Technology) of the name points to a team within Chrysler who handle the development of high-performance models in the company.

The 8.3L displacement V10 OHV engine they prepared for the car produces <517ps>, with a maximum torque of <73.96kgm>, much more powerful than before. Rather than maximum power, the Viper gains its world-class speed from its immense amount of torque.

The car’s weight - which affects handling greatly - is much lighter than the previous model. This is probably due to their aims to target the world’s super sportscar market with this car, rather than just the traditional, more straight-line, American sportscar market. They began development work at the Nürburgring from around this time, and started to compete against the Corvette on the track.

Though its unique exterior tends to grabs everyone’s attention first, the Viper pursues the goals of a real sportscar, to be ever lighter and more powerful, and is a notable presence in the world of supercars.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AAC:
The Volkswagen Type I was a car that was loved by the entire world, given nicknames like the Beetle and the Bug over the years. The people’s car, designed by Dr. Ferdinand Porsche, had a cute rounded silhouette recognised by many, and was powered by an air-cooled four-cylinder engine mounted at the rear, making it a rear-engine, rear-wheel drive car. It holds a record of 21 million cars produced from 1938 to 2003.

The Volkswagen 1200 is the official name of the main line-up, powered by a 1.2 L engine, produced from the mid 1950s to the late 1960s.

Out of these, the 1966 model is of particular interest to many. Until this year's model, the electrical systems of the car used a 6-volt battery, and was nicknamed the 6-Volt in some countries. Due to this feature, the 6-volt is the last model that is considered to be truly vintage by many. From 1967 the electrical system was updated to a 12-volt system, and the headlights were in an upright position, making the car more modern.

Among Beetle enthusiasts, there is a strong affinity for models up to 1966 that have a milder look due to the angled headlights. This has caused these models to command a premium price in recent years, and there are sometimes newer Beetles that have been modified to give it the 6-Volt or Vintage look.

The <1192cc> engine mounted in the 1200 first appeared in 1954. Though a <1285cc> was made available in 1965, and a <1493cc> appeared in 1966, its production continued into the latter half of the '70s as the basic model. Of course improvements were made over the years, boosting the initial <34ps> to <40ps> towards the end of production.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AAD:
The Vulcan is a special model of Aston Martin that was revealed at the 2015 Geneva Motor Show. Though Aston Martin had also released a 77 car limited edition 'One-77' in 2009, that was a road-going car. The Vulcan was developed through experience gained in the One-77, and is a special circuit-only model limited to just 24 cars.

The full carbon fibre monocoque and body, in a front midship/rear wheel drive layout, was designed from scratch specifically for this car. The suspension mounted on this is a push rod type, with variable shock dampers. Brakes use carbon ceramic disks and the ABS system can be adjusted by the driver. The traction control system is also variable, and can be set according to the driver’s preference and the character of the track. Handling and engine output characteristics are also possible to fine tune.

The engine is Aston Martin’s signature V12, increased to 7 litres in displacement and fine tuned to produce <811ps> normally aspirated. The gearbox is an XTrac 6 speed sequential, mounted in a trans-axle layout.

The torque tube is made of magnesium, the propeller shaft is carbon. Every part of the car has been optimised for light weight and strength, keeping the total weight down to <1350kg>. This makes the power to weight ratio an incredible <1.66kg/ps>.2

DescriptionLong.0x00004AAF:
Based on successful GTI DNA, Volkswagen Design has developed a highly distinctive supercar: the 'GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo'.

The design owes much to the successful history of the GTI: style-defining design elements from the various GTI generations illustrate the extraordinary evolution of this vehicle. Boasting a visionary design, the Roadster promises an immediate driving experience – the extreme acceleration can be experienced directly through the low-cut windscreen.

Powered by a 3.0 twin-turbo VR6 TSI engine, the 'GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo' delivers <510ps> with an enormous torque of 665 Nm (<67.8kgm>). The 7-speed dual-clutch transmission with sports programming ensures phenomenal acceleration and fast gear-shifts on the race track.

An aerodynamically optimised front and rear spoiler, together with an integrated diffuser element at the rear, achieve the required downforce for excellent road-holding. Fitted with 20-inch wheels in size 235/35 (front) and 275/30 (rear), the massive torque can be transferred reliably to the track via 4 driven wheels. The supercar features ventilated ceramic brakes, <380mm> in diameter at the front and <356mm> at the rear.

The 'GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo' is presented in a bright, intense Gran Turismo Red, a modern interpretation of the classic GTI red.

The result is a fascinating and exceptionally dynamic extreme sports car with a sophisticated design for the race track in which players can gain a unique impression of what it’s like to drive in the GTI world.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AB1:
The Subaru WRX, announced in the autumn of 2013, is a mid-class saloon that became independent from the Impreza series. The WRX was a grade model that was traditionally given to high performance versions of the Impreza, but the name has now become a new car model. The new model is, of course, a high performance sports sedan that follows in the footsteps of the Impreza WRX.

Its platform is basically the same as the Subaru Levorg, but due to the differences between an estate and a saloon and the expected types of driving conditions, the WRX body is significantly reinforced. The line-up includes a sporty STI model and a grand touring type S4. Both models are 4WD and the power unit is the iconic flat 4 turbo. However, between the STI and the S4, the centre differential and even the power steering mechanism is different. Although they are both equipped with 2 litre flat 4 engines, the engine itself is different. Subaru went out of their way to clarify the differences between the two cars.

The high performance STI is equipped with the EJ20 engine that has been put through some thorough development, producing <308ps> and <43.0kgm>. The transmission is a reinforced 6-speed MT and the driver controlled centre differential combines an electronically controlled LSD and a mechanical LSD. A Helical LSD is equipped for the front wheels, while the rear utilises a Torsen LSD. The power steering is a hydraulic type that places an emphasis on steering feel. The suspension is obviously developed individually for the car. In the end, making the WRX an independent model of its own gave the developers of the car the freedom to really pursue overall performance.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AB5:
In June 2016, a Subaru WRX STI shortened the record for 4 wheeled automobiles in the time trials held as a part of the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy race every year.

The competition, which has been held since 1907, is a race that is well known as one of the most challenging motorcycle competitions in the world. A part of the public road is closed off to create a track with a length of <60.7km> per lap, with over 200 corners with no escape zones, several sections that allow speeds in excess of <200km/h>, and an elevation change of roughly <400m>. Combined with the surface friction which is much less than that of a dedicated race track, this is definitely one of the most gruelling road competitions in the world.

The WRX STI which set the record was prepared by Subaru of America which has been taking part in this event since 2011. In 2011 they set the fastest speed record of 19 minutes 56 seconds in an Impreza WRX STI, and in 2014 they renewed the record with a time of 19 minutes 15 seconds using a VAB series WRX STI which became an independent model separate from the Impreza.

The car for the 2016 challenge was the same VAB WRX STI as the last year. However this year they received engineering support from STI, Subaru’s motorsport division, with the car being designed and built by Prodrive of the UK, the very group who had dominated the World Rally Championships (WRC) for years together with Subaru. The 2 litre flat 4 turbo engine was tuned to produce over <600ps>, with further refinements such as a DRS built into the rear wing.

As a result, with the same former rally driver Mark Higgins at the wheel, they were able to shave down the existing record by nearly 2 minutes, to set a record of 17 minutes 35.139 seconds with an average speed of <207km/h>.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AB7:
The X-BOW is the first sportscar developed by Austrian motorcycle manufacturer KTM, and debuted at the 2007 Geneva Motor Show.

The name is read ‘Crossbow’, and is named because the car evokes the image of the weapon. It is a two-seater with no doors or windows, and absolutely no extras at all. It is, however, street legal.

Its styling was handled by Kiska design, who also design KTM motorcycles, and the chassis inside the motorcycle-like exterior panels is a midship-layout carbon monocoque, designed with the assistance of the racing constructor, Dallara.

A push-rod type double wishbone suspension is mounted in the front and rear, giving it a structure like that of a pure racing car. The vehicle bottom is flat with a large diffuser at the rear end which produces <200kg> of downforce at a speed of <200km/h>. These aerodynamics allow the car to pull 1.5 horizontal Gs while cornering.

There is nothing on the car other than what is required to operate it. In the very simple cockpit there is only a single display panel that serves as the instrument panel. Mounted behind is Audi’s turbocharged direct injection 2.0L TSFI engine, and the standard model produces <240ps> and <31.6kgm> torque and propels the <790kg> body from 0-<100km/h> in 3.9 seconds.

Even in standard trim, it rivals the performance specs of respectable supercars, but the highest grade 'R' model is further boosted to <300ps> and <40.8kgm> torque. With its further upgraded suspension, it can be driven very fast on a circuit with no other modifications.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AB8:
The fan car project that started with the collaboration between Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo continued even after the release of Gran Turismo 5. Adrian Newey, the chief technical officer of Red Bull Racing, and Gran Turismo series producer, Kazunori Yamauchi, further refined the concept of the 'fastest racing car on earth, untouched by any and all regulations', and pursued the optimisation of the design even further. The result was the X2014 series, announced at the end of 2013 in Gran Turismo 6.

This is the entry level model for beginners to the X series: the X2014 Junior. A conventional aerodynamic, compact body is matched to an equally compact, naturally aspirated <2000cc> inline-4-cylinder engine that produces approximately <250ps>. This is an optimal machine for learning the basics of driving a formula car, with high grip and high downforce characteristics.l
DescriptionLong.0x00004AB9:
The fan car project that started with the collaboration between Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo continued even after the release of Gran Turismo 5. Adrian Newey, the chief technical officer of Red Bull Racing, and Gran Turismo series producer, Kazunori Yamauchi, further refined the concept of the 'fastest racing car on earth, untouched by any and all regulations', and pursued the optimisation of the design even further. What came as the result was the X2014 series, announced at the end of 2013 in Gran Turismo 6.

The X2014 Standard, the mid-range model of the X series, is a conventional Venturi car that takes away the axial-flow fan and skirts from the X2014 Fan Car, the top model of the series.

It is equipped with the same front and rear-wheel covers and glass canopy that reduces air resistance, but is given a double plane front wing that produces high downforce. The shape of the rear floor has also been optimised for this configuration. It is governed by the same rules of aerodynamics as a modern day racing car, in that its downforce will increase as the inverse square of vehicle speed. The engine is a <2000cc> turbocharged V6 that is downsized from the X2014 Fan Car, producing <810ps>. When driving this model, the pilot needs to keep in mind that the downforce on the car changes greatly along with vehicle speed.
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABA:
'The fastest racing car on earth, free from any and all regulation': The fan car project of Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo, sparked by this dream of Kazunori Yamauchi, has already produced two ultimate racing machines, the X2010 and X2014. But with the opening of the FIA Gran Turismo Championships, a need arose for a competition vehicle that both the driver and spectators could enjoy. This led to the birth of the X2019 Competition.

The X2019 Competition is based on the X2014 Standard. On the exterior, the front wing and the rear end of the body was altered to reduce downforce, in order to suppress the drastic change in aerodynamics that would occur in close battles with another car. The front and rear wheel covers have also been changed to allow fast tyre changes. The 2 litre turbo is replaced by a 3 litre naturally aspirated engine, and a more conventional throttle system has been introduced in order to give it a more attractive racing sound.

The X2019 Competition will be painted in the national colours of the Nations Cup finalists according to the home nationality of the drivers. This is a racing machine that will be unmatched in its ability to make the championship more exciting.p
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABB:
The R35 Nissan GT-R was announced in the fall of 2007, and started sales in December. In line with its debut, it was announced in January 2008 that the new GT-R would also compete in the 'Super GT' series, the most popular GT race in Japan, from this season.

This GT-R, specially developed for the 2009 vehicle regulations in advance, takes on a structure where the base car roof and pillars are attached to a main chassis built of pipe frames and a part of the existing cabin. Because of this, the front fascia and roof line is reminiscent of a GT-R, but it has a look and feel that is vastly different from a normal GT-R.

The engine was a 4.5 L V8, based on the VK45DE carried over from the Fairlady Z in the Super GT, and it was announced only that the maximum output will be over <500ps>. As when the R34 Skyline had competed in the All Japan Grand Touring Championship, the drivetrain was changed from a 4WD to an FR.

The #23 Xanavi Nismo GT-R, entered by NISMO and driven by Satoshi Motoyama and Benoit Treluyer, showed incredible performance from the opening round of their debut year, immediately winning 2 consecutive races and 3 races over the season, and won the drivers’ title for 2008.

There were 5 GT-Rs competing in the Super GT, and they had achieved a 1-2 finish in the opening round at Suzuka. In the end, the GT-Rs won 7 races out of the 9 races in the year, answering the expectations of their fans. Of these, about half of the wins were by the Xanavi Nismo GT-R./
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABC:
Jaguar is a manufacturer that was originally very active in sportscar racing, and had shown exceptional performance, winning the Le Mans 24 Hours race from 1955 to 1957, 3 years in a row.

Their motorsports activities as a works team ended in 1956, but there were those within the group of Jaguar engineers who still held dear their passion for motorsports. They continued to steadily develop a pure racing machine that would succeed the D-Type that dominated the Le Mans races in those three years.

The car that was finally completed in 1966 was the XJ13, Jaguar’s first mid-engined racing sportscar. Within a low, flowing body that shares its looks with Jaguar’s E-Type production sportcar of the day, was mounted a newly designed <502ps>, 5 L, DOHC V12 unit, that would become the base for 12-cylinder Jaguar engines to come.

The engineers had high hopes for its performance in actual racing, but the management at the time were not very keen on participation in racing, and they also did not want other manufacturers to know about the existence of their V12 engine. In the end, the project was cancelled, and the XJ13 project, said to be the most beautiful car in Jaguar history, ended without ever appearing on the circuit. Only one car was ever produced, and this car was severely damaged once while filming a promotion for the E-Type. Since then the car has been restored and preserved.i
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABD:
Jaguar was very successful in the 24 Hours of Le Mans back in the 1950s, but it did not return to the race until 1986, when they brought in their XJR-6, in Group C.

This machine was designed by famed F1 designer Tony Southgate, and is powered by Jaguar’s pride and joy, a naturally aspirated V12 engine.

Group C at the time allowed any engine format as long as a certain fuel efficiency was maintained. Many rival cars turbocharged a compact engine, but Jaguar held steadily to a normally aspirated engine.

The XJR6 was initially a 6.5 L engine, but it was later enlarged to 7 L producing around <700ps>. As turbocharged competitors started to hit the <800ps> mark, Jaguar improved the machine in other ways to raise its competitiveness. The result of this is the XJR-9 appearing in 1988.

The advantage of the XJR-9 lies in its superior aerodynamic performance and incredible control stability, as well as durability enabled by its simple structure. The XJR-9 faced off with Nissan and Toyota from Japan, Mercedes (who had recently started works activity in full force) and Porsche (who were the champions of the previous year). But Jaguar was also backed by hordes of fans who crossed the Strait of Dover to cheer on their favourite car.

In the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1988, with many Union Jack flags being waved within the crowds all along the course, the XJR-9 continued to charge forward, and the car driven by Jan Lammers, Johnny Dumfries and Andy Wallace successfully completed their 24-hour run, receiving the chequered flag. It was a historic moment, where a normally aspirated engine took the victory in Group C racing, amidst turbocharged opposition.
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABE:
The car which received the ‘Gran Turismo Trophy’ in the 61st Pebble Beach Concours D’Elegance of 2011 was this 1960 Plymouth XNR Ghia Roadster.

The designer was Virgil Exner, the legend who led the golden years of Chrysler in the 1950-1960s, and the XNR is a car that inherits his name. The car itself was built by Carrozzeria Ghia, who had a close relationship with Exner.

Plymouth was a brand that stood as the entry level position in Chrysler, and Exner poured the high-performance image Chrysler built in NASCAR into this car. This concept car was made as the future of sportscars that would rival cars like the Chevrolet Corvette and Ford Thunderbird.

The most striking feature is its asymmetric styling. The air intake in the nose, to the bubble leading to the meter hood, the flow from the headrest to the rear, is an Exner translation of aerodynamic styling of racing sportscars of the '50s. The right side of the cockpit is covered with a tonneau cover which makes it appear to be a single-seater at first glance, but there is a seat under the cover that makes it a fully fledged 2-seater.

The prominent fins on the sides of the body were actually a shared design feature from the Valiant, the car it was based on. Though its overly avant-garde styling prohibited the car from making it to mass production, it made major shockwaves in car designs during its time, and is a car that gives a glimpse into the depth of American Automotive History.)
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABF:
*The Nissan Fairlady Z was sold as the Nissan 300ZX outside Japan.

The Z32 appearing in 1989 was the first complete transformation for the Fairlady Z. Turning 180 degrees from the narrow, long-body designs that lasted 3 generations, it came in a wide, flat body. It was a size for a global sportscar, not restricted by the size classes of the Japanese market.

Its steering characteristics were changed drastically. As soon as the steering wheel is turned, the nose slices into the corner and the wide tread gave it a high level of grip. This Z opened new doors as a cornering machine, while maintaining its performance as a GT. Again, the Z dropped European thoroughbreds into a hole of despair.

At the heart of this car was a compact V6 with a low centre of gravity. Even though it is an FR, it was given a front-midship layout with the engine located as far back as possible, to make the front-to-rear weight distribution close to 50:50. Aiming for the global market, the engine size was fixed at 3 L, and producing <230ps> in the NA, and <280ps> in the twin-turbo, its performance stood tall at the end of the 20th century. Its suspension used advanced designs as well, and even features like an ABS that did not transfer shock to the brake pedal were things that went beyond the usual standards of the time.

In 1992, a convertible model was added to the line-up and was greatly welcomed in its main market of California.J
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC0:
From the very first E85/E86 model BMW Z4s, FIA-GT regulation racing machines developed by BMW motorsports were made available. Private racers all over the world have participated in GT races using these cars.

The 2nd generation, E89-based GT3 machines started racing in 2010. The production Z4, which debuted in 2009, were no longer available as either a roadster or a coupé and only sold as a cabriolet. Correspondingly, for the GT3 machine the roof was fixed in place while omitting the opening and closing mechanism. It was given a large front spoiler and rear wing and widened front and rear fenders. The bonnet, roof, front and rear fenders and the wing were made of CFRP, which succeeded in making the car <300kg> lighter at <1200kg>.

The engine was changed from a straight-6 to the 4 L V8 of the E92 M3, so with a tuned ECU it produced <480ps>. It was then combined with a 6-speed sequential transmission, given a competition ABS and the front axle was newly designed. Even within the existing design, the car underwent a fairly aggressive development process.

In the 2011 model there was another major revolution. The fenders were widened further and the overall body was given more details for improving aerodynamics. At the same time the engine displacement was increased to 4.4 L, meaning the car produced <515ps>. The 6-speed sequential transmission was also updated to a paddle shifter.

This 2011 model Z4 GT3 won 2 races in the FIA-GT3 championships of the same year. In the two 24-hour races of Nürburgring and Spa it placed 2nd overall in both races. It showed superb performance in races with high levels of competition.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC1:
The Z8, announced in 1999, was a luxury open-top sportscar that took its roots from the legendary BMW 507 of the 1950s (of which only 252 cars were ever made). It drew additional attention when its styling was shown for the first time to the world as the Bond car in the 19th 007 movie 'The World is Not Enough'.

While the Z8 is a production car, it was positioned as a very special model in BMW and they spared no expense in its creation. The base structure of the car starts by combining an extruded aluminium space frame with aluminium panelling; an expensive undertaking that requires precision craftsmanship. The long-nose, short deck layout, electric soft top and a retro-modern styling that utilises a variety of classical details, is the work of designer Henrik Fisker who would later work on the Aston Martin DB9, then go on to create his own hybrid car company.

Its design taste is consistent through to its interior, recreating the metallic interior panels of the 507 with composite panels and centre gauges. Meanwhile, fine leather is utilised unsparingly to create an interior fit for a luxury car. Mechanically it takes its engine from the high-performance E39 M5 saloon, a 4941 cc V8 producing <400ps> and <51.0kgm> torque, and also shares the 6-speed manual transmission, front MacPherson strut and rear integral arm aluminium suspension. Because the car is <150kg> lighter than the E39 M5 saloon at <1650kg>, 0-<100km/h> is a brisk 4.7 seconds, making it the fastest BMW in its day."
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC2:
Inspired by the aerodynamic designs of great prototype endurance race cars, the IsoRivolta Zagato Vision Gran Turismo is a contemporary gentleman driver’s sports car designed specifically to compete at the highest international levels. Built virtually using realistic volume and base measurements, the IsoRivolta Zagato Vision Gran Turismo evokes a fierce attitude and raw emotion through its appealing coachwork proportions: low centre-point of gravity, voluptuous fenders and sleek, elegant lines.

Historically, IsoRivolta became famous among sophisticated, international clients in the 1960s and 70s for its innovative approach in marrying Italian design with an American power train, thus producing excellent and reliable performance cars. These classic Iso sports and racing cars participated in some of the world’s greatest sports car competitions, such as the 12 Hours of Sebring, 1000 km of Nurburgring, and 24 Hours of Le Mans. The marque bearing the mythological Griffin logo also joined Formula 1 in the early 1970s through a partnership with Marlboro, competing successfully in the hands of legendary professional drivers Jacky Ickx, Gjis Van Lennep and Arturo Merzario, to name a few.

Zagato, a design atelier and coachbuilder with 98 years of experience has built automobile bodies for most of the world's famous automotive brands and is renowned for creating iconic, competitive sports cars in limited series. Zagato Vice President of Design Nori Harada pays tribute to Iso Rivolta with the creation of the new IsoRivolta Zagato Vision Gran Turismo to honour IsoRivolta’s racing heritage and passion for performance. Once again the Griffin will compete against the Prancing Horse, Raging Bull and other automotive titans of today, this time in the virtual reality of Gran Turismo.Y
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC3:
Pagani Automobili is an Italian supercar manufacturer led by Mr. Horacio Pagani, a former designer at Lamborghini involved in such models as the Countach Anniversary edition.

Pagani is a company that produces limited quantities of dream cars – cars of the type that simply cannot be built using mass-production methods. The Zonda model was first revealed by Pagani at the 1999 Geneva Motor Show.

The unique, spectacular body of the Zonda is reminiscent of a Group C car, or a Le Mans prototype. It is built entirely of carbon, and because of this the first Zonda C12 weighed in at an incredible <1250kg>. With the engine powering this ultra-light supercar being a monstrous <394ps> AMG V12, you can easily imagine the jaw-dropping performance this car is capable of.

After initial release there were a few variations in the model lineup, and this particular Zonda R is a dedicated model for circuit racing, much like the Ferrari FXX. The mid-mounted AMG V12 produces <750ps> and <72.4kgm> torque, and the transmission is a 6-speed sequential. In order to raise stability on the circuit, the wheelbase and tread width have been extended, and for improved aerodynamics a large spoiler is fitted to the front, and a variable wing mounted on the rear. The total length of the car has been extended by nearly <400mm> to streamline the airflow over the car. According to the official manufacturer's specs, its maximum speed is an amazing <350km/h> and the 0-<100km/h> acceleration is just 2.7 seconds.a
DescriptionLong.0x00005137:
While, to many, the 300 SL name calls forth the image of Mercedes' historic and elegant production sports car that debuted in 1954, the name originally comes from a prototype race car made for the factory team.

Also known by its development code W194, the 300 SL race car features an aluminium tube frame and panel body, fitted with improved versions of the engine and suspension from the W186 300. The car weighed just <870kg>, and the inline-6 engine was tuned to produce <172.4ps> for use in the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

This very car, chassis number 194007/52 achieved a stunning debut victory for Mercedes-Benz at the 1952 24 Hours of Le Mans. 2 months later, the car achieved victory at the Nürburgring after the body was modified, cutting off the roof to create a spider style body and reducing the weight by <100kg>.

Its success in racing created much demand for a production model and development started on a road-going version.
DescriptionLong.0x00005138:
The 308 GTB is a midship sports car made by Ferrari which debuted in 1975. The successor to the Dino 246 GT, it is considered to be the origin of the 2-seater midship V8 trend that would become a staple of the Ferrari line-up.

The elegant exterior that encapsulates the tube frame was created by Leonardo Fioravanti of Pininfarina, who was responsible for a number of Ferrari designs from the late 1960s up to the early 1990s.

It used the same 3L V8 DOHC engine as the Dino 308 GT4, producing <255ps> at the beginning of production. In 1980 however, in order to meet new emissions regulations the car changed to fuel injection, becoming the 308 GTBi. In 1982, in order to address power output, which had dropped to <215ps>, the engine head was changed to a 4-valve design to create the <240ps> 308 GTB Quattrovalvole.

From 1977, the targa top GTS was also available. This body style would be continued on the 328 which succeeded it in 1985.~
DescriptionLong.0x00005139:
The Porsche 356 is Porsche’s first mass production model, which debuted in 1949. It underwent a major update for the first time in 1955 and again in 1959, and the model during this period was called the 356A.

The 356A became modernised in many aspects, with a naturally rounded front window, soft pads above the interior panel, and the horn on the centre of the steering wheel, etc. The 356A continued to become more and more high performance from its first year, and led to the limited production of models which has continued to the modern day GT3s: the 1500 GS Carrera and the 1500 GS GT Carrera.

The car is equipped with a 4 cam engine that had been slightly detuned from the 550 Spyder racing sportscar. The 1500 GS Carrera was positioned as a road car and produced <100ps>, and the semi-racing car 1500 GS GT Carrera produced <110ps>. The body was available in a coupé, cabriolet, or speedster.

And the first car to ever don the ‘Carrera’ subname, which has come to represent Porsche over the years, was this 356A 1500 GS/GS GT.~
DescriptionLong.0x0000513A:
Alfa Romeo before World War II was a small production manufacturer focusing on race cars and high end vehicles. The iconic car that crowns the end of this era is the 8C series from 1931.

The letters 8C stand for its 8 cylinder engine. This water cooled inline 8 cylinder designed by the famed engineer Vittorio Jano packed the latest engine technologies of its day, with dual overhead cams (DOHC) and a hemispherical combustion chamber. The last models of the Alfa Romeo 8C 2900B from 1937 had a displacement of 2.9 L and were equipped with twin superchargers, producing <180ps> in their stock state. The chassis was offered in two types with different wheel base lengths, and the body could be selected from a number of different Carrozzerias.

The Alfa Romeo 8C 2900B Touring Berlinetta is a gorgeous coupé created by Carrozzeria Touring, utilising their Superleggera (Superlight) technology. Performance-wise it was within the realm of racing cars, and it was a de facto super sportscar of its day. It is said that only 5 of these cars were ever produced.s
DescriptionLong.0x0000513B:
In 1989, Porsche announced an almost entirely new model of the 911. This was the Type 964, the third generation 911.

As the 911 had managed to retain a high level of popularity, particularly in North America, the overall image of the car followed on from the previous 911 models. The underpinnings, though, had greatly improved, using around 80% new parts. The first announced variant was the Carrera 4 which was equipped with a 4WD system developed on the 959 development prototype to mitigate the unique handling characteristics of the rear-engine layout. The lighter rear-wheel drive Carrera 2 was released a year later in 1990.

Both models were equipped with the air-cooled flat-6 engine that 911s had become known for, though now producing <250ps>/<31.6kgm> with the displacement increased to 3.6L.

The Carrera RS is a performance model based on the Carrera 2, adding body strengthening while reducing overall weight by <120kg>. Engine power has also been increased to <260ps>, greatly improving the car's racing potential. A turbo model was also added to the 964 line-up. The most powerful model, the Turbo S, produced a staggering <381ps>.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513C:
The Porsche 911 series moved into its 4th generation in 1993, becoming the Type 993.

The most prominent change for this new generation model was a much lower nose which flattened the peaks of the front fenders and sloped the headlights back. The rear fenders were also widened among other changes which overall gave the car an entirely new look. The rear suspension was also changed to a multi-link design in the interest of improving handling.

The base power unit is the 3.6L flat 6 from the previous type 964 tuned to <272ps>, and because the next generation 996 was changed to water cooling, the 993 would be the last air cooled flat 6 model.

The most powerful model of the Type 993 911 was the Carrera RS model released in 1995. The engine was upgraded to a <300ps> 3.8L unit along with improvements to body rigidity, and weight was reduced by removing the back seats.

The line up also included the Carrera RS Clubsport which included track oriented modifications such as a large front spoiler and rear wing, as well as a welded roll cage.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513D:
The 911 GT1 Strassenversion is a street spec version of the 911 GT1, a car Porsche originally developed to compete in GT races between 1996 to 1998. The FIA-GT1 regulations of the time required that over 25 street spec cars be produced to pass homologation; so the car was designed as a full race car, then modified to meet regulations for driving on the street.

Debuting in 1996, it used the cabin and floor pan of the 993 combined with a spaceframe, in a midship layout. The engine is a twin turbo 3.2L flat 6 producing <640ps>.

In the same year, Porsche passed the street spec version through road certifications. The model built in 1997 had lights from the 996 to match the model change of the street spec 911, but it is fundamentally a race spec car. While the engine is de-tuned to <544ps> to meet European emissions regulations, its dry weight is only <1100kg>, and accelerates from 0 - <100km/h> in 3.7 seconds, with a top speed of <308km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513E:
The Porsche 917 Living Legend is a hypercar inspired by the legendary Porsche 917 race car, which brought the manufacturer the first overall victory of the 24h of Le Mans back in 1970.

Developed in 2013 by a small team of engineers and designers in Weissach, the 917 Living Legend is simultaneously a tribute and spiritual successor. Inspired by the signature proportions of the original 917, the 917 Living Legend breathes the spirit of Le Mans.

However, there is more to the concept than the puristic design implies. The carbon fibre chassis is packed with state-of-the-art technology. At its heart sits a turbocharged eight-cylinder engine with up to <1014ps>. The front and rear suspension are based on 918 Spyder components, utilising motorsport-developed linkages and pushrods. They guarantee that even at its top speed of over <300km/h>, the 917 Living Legend remains stable. Furthermore, the car utilises adaptive aerodynamics, ensuring an unmatched combination of maximum speed and downforce.

The 917 Living Legend is the embodiment of Porsche's core values, combining innovation and tradition, uniting motor sport history and the highest ambitions on the race tracks of today.w
DescriptionLong.0x0000513F:
The Porsche 917K is a prototype race car developed by Porsche to compete in Group 4 sports car racing. The 917 series debuted in 1969, and in 1970 the standard short tail body came to be called the 917K to differentiate with the long tail 917LH. The letter K stands for ‘Kurz’, which means ‘short’ in German.

The base chassis utilises a space frame made of aluminium alloy pipes, weighing just under <50kg>. The body covering this is made of lightweight FRP, and these are combined with a midship mounted <4494cc> horizontally opposed 12 cylinder engine. Though only weighing roughly <800kg>, the 917 in 1970 produced nearly <600ps> in its high power configuration. Aerodynamic improvements were also added from this year, with additional downforce gained by sloping up the rear edge of the short tail body, and the front tip was also squared off to suppress changes in downforce.

In its 2nd year of competition in 1970, the 917K dominated the international manufacturers' championship, winning 7 out of 10 races, and also successfully brought Porsche their long sought first victory in the Le Mans 24 Hour race.
DescriptionLong.0x00005140:
Debuting in 1971, the A112 Abarth is a sports model that is often considered to be the original hot hatch. It was developed using the ultra compact Autobianchi A112 as a base, a 3-door hatchback measuring just <3230mm> long and <1480mm> wide.
