It was tuned by Abarth who had just been acquired by the FIAT group. The prototype used a highly modified version of the base <903cc> inline-4 OHV engine which increased the displacement to <982cc> to produce <108ps>. This gave the car a top speed of <208km/h>.

The production model used the same <982cc> engine now producing <58ps> for optimum usability, though this was still a 20% power increase over the base engine.

Abarth would continue to make numerous improvements to the A112's sports performance. In 1975 the engine displacement was increased to <1050cc> to produce a maximum <71ps> and in 1979 the transmission was changed from a 4-speed to a 5-speed unit. 

Though production ended in 1985, the car is still loved by enthusiasts to this day for its incomparably energetic character.
DescriptionLong.0x00005141:
Introduced in 1963, the FIAT Abarth 595 was a high performance version of the second generation FIAT 500 tuned by Abarth.

While the base FIAT 500 utilised a <496cc> air-cooled 2-cylinder engine, the Abarth version received improvements across the board, increasing displacement to <594cc> along with improved intake and exhaust flow. This resulted in a huge performance boost, with maximum output increasing from <18ps> to <27ps> and the top speed from <95km/h> to <120km/h>, making it an instant hit with younger enthusiasts who yearned for cars with more power.

Then in 1964, Abarth released a further tuned model of the 595. That car was the 595 Esseesse.

While the engine had the same displacement as before, the compression ratio was increased and a larger diameter carburettor fitted, which along with redesigned manifolds allowed for a new maximum output of <32ps> and a top speed of <130km/h>.

The 595 series as a whole saw great success in under <600cc> class touring car racing across Europe.
DescriptionLong.0x00005142:
Debuting in 1971, the BMW 3.0 CS was a luxury sports coupé model developed from the 2800 CS originally released in 1968.

The series which started with the 2800 CS took the body of the 1965 4-cylinder model 2000 C and added a large front overhang inside which it housed a powerful straight-6 engine, nicknamed the 'Big Six'.

The BMW 3.0 CS was essentially a follow-up to the 2800 CS, increasing the engine to 3L from 2.8 to produce <180ps>/<26.0kgm>. To match this power increase the car was fitted with 4 wheel disc brakes.

BMW decided that this high performance Big Six coupé could be put to use in motorsports. A homologation model was developed reducing component weights across the entire car. 200kg lighter than the base model CS, this version would go on sale as the 3.0 CSL with the 'L' standing for 'leicht' ('lightweight' in German).
DescriptionLong.0x00005143:
The BRZ STI Sport was introduced in 2017 as the highest level model in the BRZ line-up. As the name suggests, this model was developed in conjunction with Subaru Tecnica International (STI), Subaru's motorsports development team.

Both the interior and exterior have been adjusted to meet the expectations of a top of the line model. The exterior has been fitted with a unique front bumper and fender garnishes, while the interior has received a full makeover in Bordeaux Red, a colour exclusive to STI Sport models. In particular, the seats use a mix of leather and alcantara for a mature, chic look.

While the powerplant is the same as the base model, the major sales point is the body is filled with STI performance technology. Flexible V bars and draw stiffeners have been introduced to control body rigidity, improving responsiveness and stability. Handling has been likewise improved using dampers and springs specially developed for this car by Sachs.
DescriptionLong.0x00005144:
The Porsche Carrera GT was a midship engined super sportscar produced from 2003 to 2006, with a total production count of just 1270 cars.

The distinct difference of this car to other production Porsche models like the 911 series, is that it was a fully dedicated design with all the parts specifically designed just for this car.

Structurally, a carbon tub was joined together with a subframe which mounts the engine and suspension, and carbon body panels were mounted on top. Because all the forces applied to the car are designed to be absorbed by the chassis, it made it possible to make this model as a Targa top. And because most of the body is made of light weight materials such as carbon, the vehicle weight is a mere <1380kg>.

The engine was a 5.5 litre V10 which was rumoured to have been developed for LMP endurance racing, respecced as a 5.7 litre to provide torque characteristics better suited for the street. The engine produces <612ps>, with a maximum torque of <60.2kgm>. It was given a 6 speed MT providing a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 3.9 seconds, with an announced top speed of over <330km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00005145:
To compete in the FIA-GT championship that began in 1997, DaimlerChrysler and AMG began a joint project to develop a racing machine in just 128 days. This car was the Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR. The front grille of the car comes from a CLK, but the rest of the car is a pure racing machine. The body skeleton is a carbon-fibre-composite monocoque with a steel roll cage, and a body with a giant air intake on the roof covers this chassis.

Mounted amidship behind the seat is a <5000cc> V12 that produces <600ps>. Even though the CLK GTR was never tested adequately, it had an astonishing debut year winning 6 of 11 races and making Bernd Schneider the series champion.

In the following 1998 season, Porsche developed and introduced the 911 GT1 and thus began a struggle between the two cars. Because of this, in addition to the two works cars that Mercedes entered in the FIA GT, they also provided two CLK GTRs to private teams in order to strengthen their efforts on the track.

For the 24 Hours of Le Mans, They entered the CLK LM, the successor to the CLK GTR. The major difference between the LM and the GTR was the engine; the V12 engine was replaced with a lightweight V8. In addition, the radiator was moved to the side, the body was redesigned, and the suspension was changed to a pushrod system, achieving a more Formula-style control characteristic.

The CLK LM did not finish the Le Mans, but subsequently became the FIA GT championship works machine. As a result, the GTR and LM won 10 out of 10 races, a perfect victory. The team of Klaus Ludwig and Ricardo Zonta produced 5 wins.w
DescriptionLong.0x00005146:
The DB5 is a sports car produced by Aston Martin that debuted in 1963. It was posed as a direct evolution of the DB4 which received widespread critical acclaim as a high performance sports model.

The basic design was created by Italian coachbuilder Carrozzeria Touring with the body made using Touring's patented 'Superleggera' super light construction methods.

The engine is a tuned version of the DB4's inline-6 unit which increases the displacement to 4L and features triple carburettors. The standard model produced <285.9ps>, while the high performance 'Vantage' model produced <318.4ps>.

Putting out higher figures than its Italian V12 equipped rivals, the DB5 is considered to be one of the most representative international supercars of the early 1960s.

The car also gained fame through its numerous movie roles as one of the 'Bond cars' driven by 007 himself in the James Bond film series.
DescriptionLong.0x00005147:
A driving force behind Pontiac in the mid-1960s, and once vice president of GM, John Z. DeLorean made the bold choice of establishing his own car manufacturer towards the end of the 1970s.

DMC ('DeLorean Motor Company') was set up in Ireland in 1975. Its first mass production model was the DMC-12.

DeLorean's objective was to produce a reasonable, stylish sportscar. However, as the recently established DMC did not have the expertise to develop such a car, the design of the DMC-12 had to be outsourced.

As a result, the chassis was handled by Lotus, while the body design was undertaken by Italdesign. Chassis construction consisted of a Lotus-style steel backbone frame, with a PRV SOHC V6 engine capable of <130ps> mounted in the rear. Its rust-proof stainless steel body and gull-wing doors attracted a lot of attention.

DeLorean sold 6,500 units of the DMC-12 in its first year, but a public scandal and other bad headlines forced the company into bankruptcy in 1983. Total production of the DMC-12 until this time was only 8,500.

After this, the entire inventory of DMC-12’s were shipped from Ireland to the U.S. and passed into the hands of a new-born DMC which would service the DeLoreans. This company, responding to the requests and demands of DeLorean owners, announced a tuning menu that increased engine power to <200ps>. DeLoreans equipped with this engine are known as Series 2.@
DescriptionLong.0x00005148:
The F12berlinetta is a flagship model of Ferrari announced in 2012 as the successor to the 599 GTB Fiorano.

The space frame and body shell forming the base structure are a brand new design combining 12 different types of aluminium alloys. The midship mounted engine is a naturally aspirated <6262cc> V12 producing <740ps> of maximum power and <70.5kgm> of maximum torque, the most powerful of Ferrari road cars to date.

However Ferrari focused the most development effort not on the frame and engine output, but on the vehicle layout. The car is <47mm> shorter, <20mm> narrower and <63mm> lower than the 599, and its wheelbase is also <30mm> shorter. The engine is also mounted <30mm> lower than the 599. The dual clutch 7 speed F1-matic gearbox utilises a transaxle layout, and all this combined lowers the centre of gravity by <25mm> with a front to rear weight ratio of 46:54; optimum specs for improving driving performance.

As a result the car achieves incredible levels of performance with a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 3.1 seconds, 0-<200km/h> acceleration is 8.5 seconds, and a top speed of <340km/h>. It also shortened the fastest road car lap time set by the 599 GTO on the Fiorano test track by a full second. This is solid proof that handling and cornering performance has been dramatically improved.

With refined aerodynamics and electronic devices as well as implementing F1 technology in its brake cooling system, this Ferrari lives up to its name as the flagship of their line up..
DescriptionLong.0x00005149:
In 1969, the Nissan Fairlady changed from a traditional open-top roadster to a radical fastback. The top grade model of this new Fairlady 'Z' was the high performance Z 432.

The most notable element of this model was its engine. The base model Z was equipped with the L20 SOHC straight-6 but only the Z 432 was equipped with the DOHC 'S20'. The S20 was a detuned mass production version of the <220ps> GR8 engine used in Nissan's R380 prototype race car. In the Z, it produced <160ps> the same as the previously released Skyline GT-R version. The '432' of the car's name was a direct reference to the engine setup: 4 valves, 3 carburettors, 2 camshafts.

The car was considerably quick for its time, with a 0-<400m> time of 15.8s and a top speed of <210km/h>. Thanks to this performance it began making appearances in motorsports a year after its debut, taking home a number of titles.

There was also a race spec version known as the Z 432 R which was sold in extremely small numbers. This model utilised fibreglass and acrylic components to reduce the body weight by <100kg>.
DescriptionLong.0x0000514A:
While there have been numerous variations of the Ford Focus, the line-up has always included a sports model. The 4th generation continued this trend with its high performance 'RS' model debuting in 2018.

While in previous generations the 'RS' badge had indicated a front-wheel drive model with sporty handling, the 4th generation Focus RS moved to a 4WD layout. The adjustable torque distribution allows for any ratio between 100% front and 100% rear, and the rear axle uses a twin-clutch system that functions as an LSD. In addition to a 'Track' mode the drive mode selector also has a 'Drift' mode. Attention has also been paid to the suspension which features 'Dual Mode' dampers.

The car uses the same 2.3L inline-4 EcoBoost engine as seen on the Mustang but tuned to produce <350ps> and <44.8kgm> through the addition of a new turbocharger and larger intercooler. With a 0-<100km/h> time of just 4.7s and a top speed of <266km/h> the Focus RS goes above and beyond the level of the average 'hot hatch'.
DescriptionLong.0x0000514B:
The second generation of the reborn Ford GT was introduced in 2015, with the new model having a much greater emphasis on speed over its predecessor.

The new body design features extensive aerodynamic effects and is equipped with a compact V6 twin-turbo engine which makes it all possible. With a 0-60 mph time of 3.0s and a top speed of <348km/h> it more than matches the performance of its European counterparts.

Naturally the car also saw use in the world of motorsports. Celebrated American race team Chip Ganassi Racing served as the Ford factory team across several series from 2016 including the FIA World Endurance Championship (WEC) and the IMSA in America.

While the car scored a small number of victories in the WEC starting with the 24 Hours of Le Mans, it was the IMSA where it performed best., winning 3 races in 2016, 2 in 2017, 5 in 2018 and 3 in 2019 which would be the final year the factory-backed team would compete.

Additionally, in the 2018 season, starting with a race win at the season opening 24 Hours of Daytona, the car achieved a number of podium finishes over the season ultimately crowning Ford the Manufacturers' champion in the GT-LM class.
DescriptionLong.0x0000514C:
The FXX K is a track-only supercar released by Ferrari in 2014 with only 32 cars made. It was developed from the limited production LaFerrari model by Corse Clienti, Ferrari's customer oriented racing division.

The 'K' represents 'HY-KERS', Ferrari's own HYbrid Kinetic Energy Recovery system, similar to the KERS systems used on F1 cars.

The 6.3L V12 engine from the LaFerrari has been tuned to produce <860ps> which combined with the <190ps> HY-KERS electric motor adds up to a total power output of <1050ps>.

The aerodynamics of the vehicle have also been extensively improved and, when combined with the EVO kit released in 2017, produce 75% more downforce over the LaFerrari.

Unhindered by homologation or championship rules, no compromises have been made on this vehicle making this the ultimate driver's car.a
DescriptionLong.0x0000514D:
The base model of the Subaru IMPREZA had always been the 4-door saloon, since its 1st generation cars. However, the base model of the 3rd generation IMPREZA that appeared in 2007 was based on a 5-door hatchback. That is why the WRX STI appearing in October of the same year also utilised the 5-door body.

On the other hand, there was still a strong demand for the traditional IMPREZA with a 3-box (engine room, passenger compartment, boot room) silhouette, a legend in its own right. To answer this demand, a much awaited WRX STI 4-door saloon model was introduced in July of 2010.

The engine powering the car was the same 2.0 L flat-4, twin-scroll turbocharged engine, producing a maximum output of <308ps> and a maximum torque of <43.0kgm>. The total length of the car is <165mm> longer than the 5-door, mainly at the rear end, and a large dedicated rear wing has been added. Due to the difference in body shape, it has an advantage over the 5-door in terms of body rigidity and aerodynamics, giving it an extra edge in the high speed range.

The tuning for the STI goes back to pure handling reminiscent of the 2nd generation models, with a very solid feel that has no lag in terms of response. The handling of the car answers directly to the input of the driver. In addition, the rigidity of the body and capacity of the suspension had been greatly improved, and the ride quality is not hard at all. It is well within the realm of a high-performance sports saloon.

Furthermore, its performance was proven at the North loop of the Nürburgring, the testing ground for all Subaru Imprezas over the years. The former WRC Champion Tommi Makinen, who once drove the IMPREZA WR car, recorded an incredible laptime of 7 minutes, 55 seconds in this car in April 2010.
DescriptionLong.0x0000514E:
Just one year after the release of the radical Spec C, in November 2002, a facelift was already being implemented in the Impreza series.

Though loved by many, the previous round headlights proved to be unpopular on the mass market and were abandoned in favour of imposing new teardrop-shaped lights. This time, under joint development with the SWRT (Subaru World Rally Team), new expertise facilitated the creation of better aerodynamic characteristics.

On the performance side, a twin-scroll turbo system was introduced for better spool efficiency along with a modified exhaust system to match. The crankshaft, along with the pistons and conrods were reinforced enabling the engine to produce <40.2kgm>, the highest torque figure in the 2-litre class at the time.

Some manual transmission models were also equipped with a driver controlled centre differential featuring an automatic mode. Depending on the conditions while cornering, the distribution of torque to the front and rear of the central differential was divided automatically, and the car demonstrated tremendous effectiveness on both circuits and winding roads.

In June 2004, a model with larger tyres was introduced. This was in response to demands from the motorsport field, such as in the Super Taikyu Endurance racing. The maximum torque was also increased to <42.0kgm> at this time.

The Impreza found its way to fame as one of Japan's most representative high-performance cars, recognised by enthusiast the world over. From 2003, the exportation of the STi model to America began, and with the Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution also starting exportation, the fierce rivalry reached further outside Japan’s borders.
DescriptionLong.0x0000514F:
The Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo SV is an all-electric virtual race car created by Jaguar Special Vehicle Operations to deliver the extremes of performance needed to dominate endurance races of the future.

Developed from 2019's dramatic Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo Coupé, and fusing inspiration from the iconic C- and D-type with proven race-winning technologies, the Vision Gran Turismo SV is the most radical interpretation yet of what an electric Jaguar of tomorrow could be.

With the sweeping forms and perfectly balanced proportions inherent in all Jaguar cars, the dramatic, streamlined composite body structure is a function of exhaustive aerodynamic optimisation. The prominent front splitter, purposefully-sculpted underbody, rear venturi and large rear wing with deployable elements create the downforce needed for traction and high speed stability while at the same time minimising drag.

The state-of-the-art lithium-ion battery pack is packaged around the cabin to enable near-perfect front and rear weight distribution. The liquid nitrogen cooling system ensures that every cell delivers maximum performance even under the most extreme race conditions, for lap after lap, hour after hour.

Integrating all of the learning gained during development of Jaguar’s I-TYPE 5 Formula E racing car, the Vision Gran Turismo SV’s four powerful, light, compact electric motors enable a maximum speed of more than 255 mph (approximately <410km/h>). Reflecting the increase in power and torque output compared to its precursor’s three-motor powertrain, the Vision Gran Turismo SV generates a sound that is even more distinctive, purposeful and hard-edged, reflecting its true racing DNA.

The pure, sweeping surfaces within the cockpit truly envelop the driver and position the instruments and perfectly-weighted controls exactly where they need to be. Every component is beautifully crafted with absolute precision from advanced, lightweight materials.

Authentically yet futuristically Jaguar, the Vision Gran Turismo SV is designed and engineered to take the performance and dynamics capability of the original Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo Coupé to the next level and deliver an intuitive, immersive and truly electrnfying driving experience.
DescriptionLong.0x00005150:
Automobili Lamborghini joins the world of virtual racing with a visionary project to amaze and touch the very heart of all Vision Gran Turismo racers. The stunning design and concept of the Lambo V12 Vision Gran Turismo was developed with the highest passion and design skills of the Team of Centro Stile Lamborghini in Sant’Agata Bolognese, led by Head of Design Mitja Borkert.

The creation of the design prototype began from initial sketches then led to a digital model realised in a 1:3 scale and approved by Kazunori Yamauchi and Mitja Borkert. The full-size model was subsequently developed by a highly experienced and motivated team from 2018 to 2019.

The Lamborghini Lambo V12 Vision Gran Turismo is a fascinating sculpture that imparts all the iconic Lamborghini Design DNA. It looks futuristic and beautiful, but also boasts a high degree of engineering integrity and state of the art aerodynamics.

From the very first ideation by the design team, the core of this being a dedicated virtual race car led to the subsequent single-seater design. Focused and reduced, the cabin is purely designed for the player of the game. Following our special design philosophy 'to feel like a pilot', the seat is located in the centre as found in formula or endurance racers. The digital cockpit features augmented reality and is fully voice controlled.

The powertrain is derived from the Lamborghini Sián FKP 37 with its V12 mid-engine super capacitor hybrid system. The virtual racer offers up to <830.4ps>, creating a thrilling sound and a unique virtual driving experience. The engine is always in view, aspiring and visible.

The design is dedicated to the design language of Automobili Lamborghini with its typical one/line silhouette. The architecture is clearly following the Lamborghini DNA that began with the iconic Lamborghini Countach in 1971. There is a strong influence of the visionary design language experimented and explored by Marcello Gandini. The side profile is inspired by the groundbreaking concept car Bertone Stratos Zero from 1970. The iconic upsilon and hexagon graphical elements are visible in every detail, with the 'Y' shaped front lights providing a strong link to the future light design oa Lamborghini.
DescriptionLong.0x00005151:
The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution IX MR GSR is the 2006 update of the Lancer Evolution IX GSR which debuted in 2005.

On first glance, the car appears to be almost identical to the previous model, but numerous refinements have been made across the entire car. For example, while the maximum power and torque numbers of the 4G63 engine remain the same, the MIVEC variable valve timing system has been retuned, the standard specification turbine wheel has changed to a titanium-aluminium alloy, and the compressor inlet diameter has been downsized. Along with other minor improvements, this resulted in sharper engine response and faster acceleration.

The suspension has also been upgraded, employing high spring rate Eibach coils combined with Bilstein dampers, and the electronically controlled 'Super AYC' 4WD system has been reprogrammed to focus on cornering ability. There have also been refinements to the aerodynamics with the shape of the front bumper being changed to reduce lift.

The 'MR' of the model name stands for 'Mitsubishi Racing'. Throughout the company's history this designation has been given to the highest performance sports models. For the Lancer Evolution, MR models first appeared in the VIII line-up, making this IX the second MR model in the car's history.

This model is the culmination of the continued development of the 3rd generation Lancer Evolution which had started in 2001 and is also the very last Lancer Evolution to feature the legendary 4G63 engine./
DescriptionLong.0x00005152:
The Mercedes AMG GT R debuted in 2016 as a high performance version of the AMG GT first introduced in 2014. While marketed as a road car, in performance terms the car is much closer to a road legal race car.

The first thing that will catch your eye is the vertical accents on the front grill which evoke the image of the 300SL race car that won the 1952 Carrera Panamericana Mexico. Other notable features of the exterior include the adjustable rear wing and the flared fenders of its wider body.

However, the largest changes from the base model are actually on the inside. Areas like the roof, front fenders and torque tube have been replaced with carbon fibre components to reduce weight, and the 4L V8 twin-turbo engine has been tuned to produce <585ps> and <71.3kgm>. The first Mercedes AMG model to use four-wheel steering, it also features an active aerodynamics system for the front of the car.

It can accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in 3.6 seconds and has a top speed of <318km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00005153:
The BAC Mono is a sports car produced by British manufacturer Briggs Automotive Company since 2009. Having themselves worked in design and development for large scale automotive manufacturers, this car is the realisation of the Briggs brothers' vision of 'a road vehicle that offers the most authentic and pure driving experience possible while implementing the very latest in racing technology.'

The car's most notable aspect is its formula car style single seat design. However, unlike modern formula cars which typically use a carbon monocoque, it uses a more classical tubular frame design with a carbon-fibre body shell. Both the front and rear suspensions implement a double wishbone pushrod design.

The engine situated behind the driver is a Cosworth tuned 2.5L inline-4 Ford Duratec unit producing <309ps> and <31.4kgm>, which is directed through a race specification 6-speed sequential transmission.

Ultralight at only <580kg>, its performance rivals F3 machines with a 0-60 mph time of 2.8s and a top speed of <274km/h>.C
DescriptionLong.0x00005154:
The Polo is one of the main pillars in the Volkswagen line up, a car in a class one size smaller than the Golf. But this car maintains all the high quality virtues as displayed in the higher class Golf, and is a model that is positioned as the world’s benchmark for B segment compact cars.

The Polo was reborn into its 5th generation model at the 2009 Geneva Motor Show. The styling is similar to the 6th generation Golf of the same period, but with its clean, bold lines, it exhibited a strong image that put it above other cars in its class. Thorough considerations were made for environmental performance as well, downsizing the engine and utilising an efficient 7 speed DSG.

The high performance GTI model debuted in 2010 featuring a 1.4L direct injection turbo + supercharger engine setup which, despite being <400cc> smaller in displacement than the previous model,  produced <29ps>/<3.1kgm> more at <179ps>/<25.5kgm>. The 7 speed DSG transmission allows for a top speed of <225km/h>, with a 0 to <100km/h> acceleration of 6.9 seconds. The chassis was also upgraded, featuring sports suspension and electronic devices that perform the same function as a limited-slip differential. This model is also notable for its fantastic handling response.

In 2014, the GTI model received a facelift. One of the most notable changes is the new engine. Now featuring a <400cc> larger 1.8L inline-4 turbo engine the maximum power output has increased to <192ps>. Extra power isn't the only difference, as the fuel efficiency has also been greatly improved, consuming much less fuel than the 1.4L GTI.
DescriptionLong.0x00005155:
The Audi R8 LMS Evo is, as the name implies, an evolution model of the R8 LMS. The R8 LMS is a GT3 regulation race car based on the midship R8 sportscar. Introduced in 2009, it saw great success in racing until 2015 when the road car underwent a full model change from the Type 42 to the Type 4S.

The biggest advancement of the R8 LMS was its improvments in cooling and aerodynamics. The openings of the front grille and rear bumper were enlarged, and air channels were added next to the headlights. The front canard wings were also enlarged, and the drivetrain was improved overall to increase reliablity.

The output of the 5.2L V10 engine has not changed at over <585ps> and <56kgm>, but the base weight of the car has been reduced by <25kg> to <1200kg>, making it easier to balance weight in competition.

The R8 LMS Evo revealed at the 2018 Paris Motor Show competed in and won the Gulf 12 hour race at the end of the year.
DescriptionLong.0x00005156:
Every year at SEMA, the Gran Turismo Awards are given to the best custom car on show at the convention. In 2014, the 12th year of these awards, the award went to the 1970 Chevrolet Camaro SS 'Rampage' built by muscle car chassis specialists 'Roadster Shop' of Illinois, United States.

The car has been given an intensely aggressive visage with oversized fender flares on the front and rear, as well as a large front spoiler and rear wing. What's most surprising about the car though is on the inside. The chassis has been rebuilt, adding a roll cage for strength and numerous parts across the car have been replaced with carbon-fibre and aluminium components, significantly reducing weight.

The 7L LS7 engine has been tuned to produce <750ps> and set back <13cm> to improve the front-to-rear weight ratio. The chassis specialists' piece de resistance though, is the suspension which has been converted to an inboard cantilever design. This car is perhaps the ultimate restomod.
DescriptionLong.0x00005157:
Released in 2011, the Mazda RX-8 Spirit R was the final special edition model of the RX-8 which had originally debuted in 2003.

The RX-8 offered two slightly different experiences. The 6-speed manual model was more sporty, while the 6-speed automatic felt more like a grand tourer. Both the manual and automatic were again available for the Spirit R model, with each based on the highest grade model that matches those characteristics.

The manual model was based on the sporty Type RS, featuring extra aero parts and extra-hard suspension with Bilstein dampers. The automatic model was based on the grand tourer style Type E and had a fully equipped interior with leather seats. The only differences from previous models, though, were the exterior and interior details, engine specs and mechanicals had remained unchanged. Despite this, with the announcement that production of the RX-8 would cease in June 2012, orders for the cars soon exceeded the originally planned 1000 vehicles and 1000 extra were produced to meet demand.
DescriptionLong.0x00005158:
In May 1988, the 5th generation S13 Silvia swept away the market share from the Honda Prelude and gained incredible popularity. It captured fans not just as a 'Dating Car', but also for being a fun to drive, compact FR.

The first and foremost reason for its popularity was its styling. Its refined coupé body was cutting-edge, and had a flamboyance that seemed to epitomise the buoyant economy. Of course its driving performance was another major factor. It was agile and sporty, and the price was affordable. This car met every need of the young generation in its day.

Initially the engine was a 1.8 L CA18, which was replaced with the SR20 series 2.0 L, DOHC inline-4 in later models after a minor change. The premium K's model was turbocharged and produced <205ps> and <28.0kgm> torque, while the Q's and J's were naturally aspirated and produced <140ps> and <18.2kgm> torque. The front suspension utilised MacPherson struts, with multi-link suspension in the rear. A 4-wheel steering system called the Super HICAS was also available as an option.

Acceleration in the <1170kg>, <205ps> turbocharged K's was exhilarating, and due to the amazing balance of the chassis, drivers could truly feel connected to the road. There are many drivers in Japan who first learned what drifting is while driving this car. Another characteristic of the Silvia was that it had a huge following as a tuning base car. The CA18DET engine was very tough, and was able to withstand over <300ps> when tuned. There was even a period of time when almost all cars parked outside tuning shops in Japan were S13 Silvias.
DescriptionLong.0x00005159:
The roots of the Shelby GT350R harken back to 1965, when Ford commissioned Carol Shelby to build a car for competition in the SCCA (Sports Car Club of America) races. While based on the first generation Mustang, the SCCA race regulations only allowed minor modifications such as weight reduction from the stock model, so the GT350R was sold as a road car that could go straight to the track. It saw incredible success in racing and the name quickly became legend.

The Shelby 350R of 2016, based on the 7th generation Mustang, is also a car you could bring straight to the race track to enjoy.

The 5.2L V8 was tuned to produce <533ps> and <59.3kgm> naturally aspirated, and combined with a 6 speed manual transmission. The chassis has also been reinforced to support this engine performance. The suspension incorporates Ford's MagneRide system, which detects road conditions and adjusts damping strength using magnetorheological fluid. Made into a two seater, significant efforts have also been made for weight reduction.

The GT350R was based on the catalogue model GT350, but because of all the special tuning performed on the car, it was sold as a special model available only through a limited number of dealers.
DescriptionLong.0x0000515A:
Radical Sportscars Ltd. is a constructor that manufactures and sells full-fledged racing cars for amateur race enthusiasts. Since their establishment in 1997, the base concept of their machines are midship racing cars powered by high performance superbike engines. They also sell road versions of these cars with looks and performance that resemble Le Mans prototypes.

You can drive from your own home for a day at the track, and drive straight home. Unmatched on winding roads, it gives the owner a feel of what it’s like to drive a racing car in the city. The extreme stimulation the car is able to provide attracted not only race enthusiasts but also those who could no longer be satisfied with just your average sportscar.

The SR3 SL is a model that has a stronger emphasis on its character as a road car. There are no major changes to its design principles and styling, but the car has been redesigned to be powered by an automobile engine in order to clear the variety of emissions regulations around the world.

The power unit is a Ford Ecoboost 2 litre 4 cylinder direct injection turbo, producing <240ps> standard, with an option to go up to <300ps>. The transmission is a 6 speed sequential with paddle shifters, and the car weighs <775kg>.

Accelerating from a standstill to <96km/h> in 3.4 seconds, it can then come to a full stop in just 2.67 seconds. Together with a top speed of <257km/h>, its performance is leaps and bounds beyond the norm. There is no other car more befitting the term 'road-going racer'.
DescriptionLong.0x0000515B:
Introduced in 1984, the Testarossa would become Ferrari's flagship mid-engine model. It also served as the successor to the Berlinetta Boxer series which had continued for 11 years.

The most memorable aspect of this car is its exterior stylings. The rear fenders which jut sharply from the small cabin with the 5 almost sculptural side strakes create a highly artistic and vibrant image which won the car countless fans.

While at a glance it may appear to be just a design flare, they are actually designed to incorporate F1 style side radiators. These solved the problem of excess cabin heat as well as creating front luggage space, overall greatly increasing the car's comfort as a grand tourer.

The engine is a 5L 180-degree V12 unit with a maximum power output of <390ps> and <50.0kgm> maximum torque. It has a 0-<100km/h> time of 5.8s and a top speed of <290km/h>.

Though it was replaced by the 512 TR in 1992, the car is still an extremely popular and historic model.
DescriptionLong.0x0000515C:
If you trace back the roots of the modern SUV category, you will eventually arrive at this compact four-wheel drive car which began development in 1940 by request from the US Army during the Second World War.

The US Army called upon Bantam, Ford and Willys to develop and produce their own prototypes based on a design by Bantam. Each company produced over 1500 such vehicles which were put into military service. The best performing of these prototypes, the Willys MA, was further improved upon to create the MB and officially entered service with over 360,000 units produced.

This model would serve as the inspiration for every Jeep model to come later.

After the war, Willys registered the Jeep trademark and released a civilian model based on the MB. Thanks to the numerous accounts from returning soldiers of the MB's performance and off-road ability, the car was a huge success for Willys.

With a ladder frame and solid axle as its base, this is the car that proved to later generations the superiority of simple, hardy construction when combined with a four-wheel drive system.

One cannot understate the importance of the MB to the history of four-wheel drive cars.D
DescriptionLong.0x0000529D:
Every year at SEMA, the Gran Turismo Awards are given to the best custom car on show at the convention. In 2016, the 14th such award was presented to this car built from a 1951 Ford Custom Club Coupe by a team of customisation specialists for former racing driver Bruce Leven.

Leven's dream had been to build a classic racing Ford which incorporated elements of European style. The car has undergone major bodywork in order to realise this vision, chopping the waistline and lowering the roofline along with it.

The powerplant is a 1956 Lincoln 368 cu in V8 unit tuned by a race engine specialist to produce <380ps>. Additionally, both the front and rear suspension have been carefully constructed to provide competition spec handling.

Almost every single part of this machine has been customised, taking an estimated 10,000 hours of work to complete.
DescriptionLong.0x0000529E:
The Cappuccino, the Kei sportscar released by Suzuki in November 1991, is a car that initiated the huge popularity in 2-seater K-cars in its day, along with cars like the Honda Beat and Mazda Autozam AZ-1.

The major characteristic of the Cappuccino was that it is a 2-seater front-engine rear-wheel drive (FR) convertible, with a unique concept different from the convertible midship Beat, and the midship gull-winged AZ-1. What was interesting is that though K-cars often shared parts, this had an all-original body designed specifically for the car. The main purpose of this was to realize the concept of an 'FR' with excellent handling characteristics, but it also allowed for a near perfect 51:49 front-to-rear weight distribution. Details like this show just how serious they were in development of the Cappuccino.

The design embodies classic FR cars with its long nose and rounded body. Another innovation was the structure of the roof, that allowed it to be removed in 3 pieces. Starting as a hardtop, it can be converted to a T-bar roof, targa-top and, with the rear window lowered, it becomes a fully open top car, enabling the owner to enjoy 4 variations in style.

The power unit is a <657cc>, DOHC 12-valve inline-3-cylinder turbo engine based on the same specification as the <64ps> engine of the Alto Works, the most powerful such engine used in a kei model. The suspension uses newly designed double wishbones in the front and rear, with four-wheel disc brakes employing ventilated discs in the front. 

In 1995, the car received a number of minor improvements including an overhaul of the power unit, which changed to a newly designed all-aluminium block. The engine control unit was also updated allowing for an increase in maximum torque. The line-up originally only offered a 5-speed manual transmission but these changes also saw the introduction of an electronically controlled 3-speed automatic model. This automatic model was also fitted with power steering.

At the end of 1998 it ceased production at 26,500 cars. The Cappuccino was truly a dream Kei sportscar, born from the economic bubble in Japan at the time.
DescriptionLong.0x0000529F:
Since receiving its manufacturing licence from Lotus in 1973, Caterham Cars have continued to produce a very Spartan sportscar called the 'Seven'. And the car that was born in 1996 in the evolution of this Caterham Seven, was the ‘Caterham Seven Superlight’.

Styled like a formula car from the ‘50s, the car has a semi-monocoque chassis built from a tubular frame with aluminium panelling. It retains the basic long front nose and the rear wheel drive layout of the standard Seven, but significant weight reductions were introduced in this model as its name implies.
While depending on the chosen engine, the car is <35kg> - <50kg> lighter than the standard Seven model.

The name R500 comes from 500-horsepower-per-tonne power-to-weight ratio, and was the name of a variant that appeared in 1999 to be the most powerful in the series. Initially it was powered by a Rover type K engine, but later models from 2008 were equipped with a 2 litre Ford Duratec with <266ps> which reigned supreme until the appearance of the supercharged R600 in 2012. Its acceleration performance surpassed that of supercars, with a 0-<100km/h> acceleration time of 2.88 seconds.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A0:
Introduced in the 1964 model year, the Chevelle was Chevrolet's first intermediate model. With an SS sports grade model in the line-up, and an option for a 327 ci high output V8 engine, the Chevelle carried all the hallmarks of a muscle car.

In the following year of 1965, however, the Chevelle SS was transformed into a full-blown high-performance car, with a 396 ci, OHV V8. From then on, the Chevelle SS was only offered with this 396 ci unit, drawing a clear line between it and the previous SS.

In 1970, the Chevelle SS went on to be called the most powerful intermediate model on the market. The engine line-up that was only available in 396 ci was upgraded, offering an enlarged 402 ci model. In addition, the 427 ci engine of the higher grade model was further upgraded to 454 ci.

The option codes for the two types of 454 ci models offered were the LS5 and LS6. The former produced <360ps>, with a compression ratio of 10.25:1. The latter produced approximately <456ps>, with an increased compression ratio of 11.25:1, high cams, and high-flow headers. This was the most powerful catalogue model engine in the history of American cars in its day.

The LS6-equipped Chevelle SS 454 was immediately recognised as a very special model, with its wild power output, which was unlikely for a road-legal car. Equipped with a straight exhaust and carburettor settings, it is said to have easily exceeded <500ps>, and was the big contender in stock class drag racing.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A1:
The Honda Civic is a long-selling model that first appeared in 1972. The mainstream model of the 6th generation EK Civic, appearing in 1995, also called the Miracle Civic, was given a high-fuel-economy, high-output 3-stage VTEC, and was also equipped with a CVT called the Honda Multimatic.

Two years later in August 1997, the Type R of this 6th generation Civic made its first appearance. Based on the 3-door hatchback model, the car attracted much attention as the first Type R Civic.

The engine of the Civic Type R was a B16B, 1.6 L inline-4-cylinder DOHC 16-valve engine, and equipped with VTEC it produced an amazing <185ps> @ <8200rpm> even though it was a normally aspirated engine. The body was lightened, as with the other Type R models, and was equipped with a harder, lower suspension, enlarged four-wheel disc brakes and ABS with a sports setting.

The lightweight, compact and high-performance Civic Type R was very active in racing, invoking one-make Civic races and actively competing in races like the Super Taikyu endurance series, while still captivating many amateur racers.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A2:
A full model change in the autumn of 1967 brought with it the new C3 Corvette Stingray as the 1968 model. It was very reminiscent of the 'Mako Shark II' show model, which was displayed at the New York International Auto Show in April of 1965.

This concept sought to show off the Corvette in a new light, specifically as a grand tourer. Chief designer Bill Mitchell's design ideas were extremely important factors in the achievement of this goal.

Working as Mitchell's right-hand man was a man named Larry Shinoda, a Japanese-American who had worked as a detail designer on the original Stingray. Taking many hints from Mitchell's concepts, Shinoda's image of the next generation GT car materialised as the Mako Shark II.

With a dynamic, curvaceous exterior, and an interior stuffed with the newest electronic gizmos, it was indeed the Corvette of the future. The essence of this idea was thoroughly incorporated into the street model that was to become the C3 Corvette.

In 1969 the standard engine's displacement was brought up from 327 ci to 350 ci, but maximum output remained unchanged at <300ps>. At the same time, the small-block option changed from the 327 ci L79, to the 350 ci L46, with maximum output again unchanged at <355ps>.

Though at the time talk was all about the power of the big-block Corvette, the small-block held the advantage in handling with its lower front-end weight. The epitome of this was the replacement of the top-grade L46 by the <370ps> LT1. Available around 1970, this was acclaimed as the best handling of all the C3 Corvette combinations.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A3:
In the world of customised cars, the U.S. is often number one in terms of quality, volume and genre. The oldest genre of these, now an iconic part of American culture, is the Hot Rod.

This was a movement that originated in the 1930s, where the Ford Model T and the later Model A’s and Model B’s were heavily modified by their owners. Extensive exterior modifications were performed on these cars such as removing wheel arches, bonnets and cutting the body to make chop-top convertibles. More and more powerful engines were then added to the cars as technology improved over the years.

The most popular base car for this was the Ford Model B. This stems from it being the first car to equip the cutting edge V8 engine of the era, and for its rarity – the car was only produced for a single year in 1932.

The car with the number plate 'V-3883' displayed in the Henry Ford Museum is one such car, based on the model B with the ‘Deuce’ nickname. It was built by Richard Smith of Phoenix, Arizona in 1954 to the tune of 2800 dollars - a huge sum at the time, and a massive amount of time and effort.

This is a classic ‘highboy’ style with removed wheelarches, but the engine has been swapped for a <180ps> Chrysler 331 Hemi. The side panels have been cut and modified to fit the wide engine, and the engine covers themselves are now a part of the exterior styling. This is a car that has been worked down to the very last detail, and is a simple, beautiful example of the good ol’ days.W
DescriptionLong.0x000052A4:
Debuting in 2003, the baby Lambo ‘Gallardo’ underwent many improvements over the course of a five-year span, including several high-performance evolutions. Then, at the 2008 Geneva Motor Show, a model debuted that would outshine all of its predecessors. On the surface, the new Gallardo, or ‘LP 560-4’, looked as if it had simply taken stylistic cues from the limited-edition Lamborghini Reventón. But in truth, it had undergone some major modifications.

The most prominent of such modifications was the enlargement of its V10 engine displacement, from <4961cc> to <5204cc>. With additional intake and exhaust upgrades, and increased compression, the engine produced <560ps> and <55.1kgm> of torque, which was a <40ps> and <3.1kgm> improvement from the original Gallardo model.

The drivetrain employed the same full-time 4WD transmission and viscous coupling as its forebearers. As for the car's name, the '560' was taken from its maximum engine output, and the '4' stood for its 4WD system.

The car also inherited a 6MT, or ‘6-speed, 2-pedal manual transmission’, the E-gear in particular being greatly upgraded, its shifting speed shortened by 40% in the sporty 'CORSA' mode. Many thorough weight-reduction efforts were also made, resulting in the vehicle weighing in <20kg> lighter than previous models, at <1410kg>.

Thanks to the combination of these features, the maximum speed of the car was raised to <325km/h>, with a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of 3.7 seconds, making it not just a few steps but leaps and bounds ahead of its rivals. Today, the Gallardo is a model with a strong presence, having confidently outgrown its 'Baby Lambo' nickname.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A5:
The Integra Type R was introduced in 1995. While the name 'Type R' was known to car enthusiasts as the 'racing car on the street' since the introduction of the NSX in '92, this became much more affordable with the launch of the Integra.

The engine was based on the 1.8 L, B18 VTEC equipped in the Si. Redline and engine compression were increased using high-compression piston heads, high-strength connecting rods, and dual-valve springs. Assembly was performed one engine at a time by hand, and it produced <200ps>, which is <111ps> per litre of displacement. The body was reinforced but also made lighter. Despite the use of heavy parts such as performance rods and a helical LSD, weight was offset by reducing battery size, removing soundproofing material, and by using lightweight aluminium wheels, and a 40 kg decrease in weight was achieved. Fundamental suspension settings were revised, and it resulted in handling characteristics that virtually eradicated understeer.

Upon release, this Integra Type R became the symbol of high-performance front-wheel drive cars.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A6:
The Maserati Merak was a mid-engine sports car introduced in 1972. It was developed to be a sister model to the Bora which had debuted a year earlier.

The exterior stylings were very similar to the Bora, both having been designed by Giugiaro. However, while the Bora had been a fastback, the Merak was actually a notchback with a fastback style pillar. This allowed it to retain the same silhouette while making the car feel lighter and improving engine cooling.

Similarly, while the Bora housed a V8, the Merak was equipped with a <190ps> 3L V6 taken from the Citroën SM. With this more compact engine, the seating arrangement changed to a 2+2 layout which allowed for some luggage space.

A high performance model was later released in 1975 as the Merak SS. The compression ratio was increased and other adjustments were made to tune the engine to <220ps>, increasing the top speed from <225km/h> to <250km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x000052A7:
Originally a Le Mans Prototype race car, the name and technology from the 'R8' were carried over to create the R8 road car which debuted in 2006. The car was met with worldwide critical acclaim and a 2nd generation model was introduced in 2016.

While this new model retains the key concepts behind the vehicle, it uses new versions of the lightweight Audi Space Frame made with lightweight materials, and their full-time 4WD 'quattro' system. While aesthetically similar to its predecessor in many ways, almost all of its exterior details are completely different.

Following on from the previous model, the powerplant is a 5.2L naturally aspirated V10. However even the new base model R8 produces <540ps>, which is a <15ps> improvement over its predecessor. The new line-up also features the high performance 'R8 V10 Plus' model which tunes the same engine up to <610ps> and also adds a fixed rear wing and mechanical LSD as standard.

The specifications released indicate that the R8 V10 Plus goes from 0 to <100km/h> in 3.2 seconds, with a top speed of <330km/h>.K
DescriptionLong.0x000052A8:
From the middle of the 1969 season, the Charger 500 Daytona made its appearance in stock car racing. It took full advantage of its aerodynamics, and was performing very well. This in turn raised demand from teams racing Plymouth race cars (which are in the same Chrysler group) for a model that had the same aerodynamics as the Daytona. The answer to those demands was the Superbird.

Plymouth did not produce a vehicle that could be considered the sibling of the Charger, so the Road Runner, which had the same intermediate class chassis, was selected to be its base.

There are slight differences to details such as the shape of the roof, but otherwise it looks very similar to the Daytona, with features like the familiar extended nose and rear wing.

The number of cars required for homologation was doubled in 1970 from 500 cars to 1000, and with the Daytonas performing so well on the circuit, many Superbirds made it to the streets as well as the track.

The base engine for the Superbird was the <375ps> 440 Super Commando, with a 426 Hemi producing over <425ps>, and a <390ps> 440 six-barrel as options. This was more in line with the GTX, which was ranked above the Road Runner.

The Superbird was produced, like the Daytona, during the homologation certification period of only one year.2
DescriptionLong.0x000052A9:
The FD3S, the 3rd generation RX-7, debuted in December 1991. The name 'Savanna' given to the previous versions was dropped, and it was renamed the ɛ̃fini RX-7.

In order to accommodate wider tyres, the FD3S was significantly widened, but its bonnet, spare wheel, jack, and front and rear double wishbone suspension were all made of aluminium, keeping the vehicle weight down to a miraculous <1260kg> despite the size increase.

The engine was a 13B Turbo as in the FC3S. However with its new sequential twin-turbo, power output was raised to <255ps> and <30.0kgm> of torque. The weight-to-power ratio of the lighter Type S reached <4.90kg/ps>, and the car was the fastest RX-7 ever released, with huge potential.

The FD3S continued to evolve. Body rigidity, the computer, and ABS specifications were upgraded year after year. The Type I, created in 1991, evolved to Type II and III, and finally to the Type VI in 2000.

However, the RX-7 was unable to survive the environmental standards of the 21st century. In August 2002, The RX-7 Spirit R was released as an anniversary model as the last of the series, marking an end to 25 years of production.~
DescriptionLong.0x00005550:
The mid-engine Mangusta is De Tomaso's second production sports car, debuting in 1966.

Their previous model, the Vallelunga, proved to be underpowered with its 1.5L inline-4 engine. In response, this model used a modified racing chassis, which had been under development in a separate project, and was fitted with a Ford V8. As standard the car used the <310.2ps> 289 engine, while the American version used the <233.2ps> 302 engine, both paired with a ZF-made 5-speed gearbox.

Weighing only approx. 1.3 tons, the top speed was set at <250km/h>.

The fine balance of the exterior stylings were drawn up by Giorgetto Giugiaro who was working for Carrozzeria Ghia at the time.

Though only 401 such cars were made, the combination of gorgeous Italian mid-engine style and a powerful American V8 would live on in the hugely successful Pantera which debuted in 1970.
DescriptionLong.0x00005551:
The Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3 is an FIA GT3 regulation production race car developed by Nismo based on Nissan's R35 model GT-R.

A GT3 version of the GT-R had been available to customers since 2012, but from 2015 the base model changed to the GT-R Nismo which featured improved body rigidity. The 2018 model changed to a dry sump allowing the engine to be placed approx. <150mm> lower in the engine bay to lower the centre of gravity and <150mm> further back to optimise weight distribution. 

Front body rigidity was also improved and the suspension and members for both the front and rear were redesigned to provide accurate body feedback.

The layout of the engine bay also received improvements with the radiators and intercoolers repositioned to provide better airflow and better cooling as a result. By refining airflow, they also succeeded in improving body stability on high speed sections.
DescriptionLong.0x0000565B:
The Porsche 918 Spyder is a supercar introduced by Porsche in 2011. A successor to the Carrera GT, production was limited to 918 cars.

The most notable aspect of the car is that it is actually a plug-in hybrid. A <608ps> 4.6L V8 engine based on the engine from the RS Spyder prototype race car is mounted in the mid-ship position. The car is also equipped with a motor on the front and one on the rear, resulting in a total system output of <886ps>.

This incredible performance when combined with the optional Weissach Package allows the car to reach <100km/h> in 2.6s, <200km/h> in 7.2s and <300km/h> in just 19.9s. Advertised as having a top speed of <345km/h>, it was able to set a lap time of 6:57 on the Nürburgring Nordschleife.

The Weissach Package reduces the total weight by <40kg>, though the standard model weighs only <1674kg>. Given that the car is a hybrid this is already exceptionally light.
DescriptionLong.0x0000565C:
Debuting in 1971, the BMW 3.0 CS was a luxury sports coupé model developed from the 2800 CS originally released in 1968.

The series which started with the 2800 CS took the body of the 1965 4-cylinder model 2000 C and added a large front overhang inside which it housed a powerful straight-6 engine, nicknamed the 'Big Six'.

The BMW 3.0 CS was essentially a follow-up to the 2800 CS, increasing the engine to 3L from 2.8 to produce <180ps>/<26.0kgm>. To match this power increase the car was fitted with 4 wheel disc brakes.

BMW decided that this high performance Big Six coupé could be put to use in motorsports. A homologation model was developed reducing component weights across the entire car. 200kg lighter than the base model CS, this version would go on sale as the 3.0 CSL with the 'L' standing for 'leicht' ('lightweight' in German).
DescriptionLong.0x0000565D:
In early 1953, there were no cars built in the United States that you could call a ‘true’ sportscar. The American sportscar market then was dominated by European sportscars that were imported after World War II. To change all this, the sportscar that GM released under their Chevrolet brand was the Corvette.

This first Corvette was born in 1953. Combining FRP panels with a steel backbone frame, it was very futuristic and advanced in style, and set its presence as an American-made sportscar. A <152ps>, 3.8 L inline-6 was mounted in the <4249mm> long, <1773mm> wide body. The Corvettes made in this year were almost all hand-made, and only 300 were produced.

After seeing that these initial 300 cars sold out instantly, GM moved its factory from Michigan to Saint Louis in the following year of 1954, and prepared for mass production. In this year they produced 10 times the number of cars they had the previous year, at 3,640 cars.

The specs of the 1954 model are basically the same as the first years, but midway through the model year they changed the cam profile, and the engine output was raised to <155ps>. The front grille and rear design was changed for the ’58 model, and the most dramatic change in its looks involved the newly adopted quadruple headlights.
DescriptionLong.0x0000565F:
The Giulia GTA and GTAm are special editions of the Giulia released to celebrate the 110th anniversary of the founding of Alfa Romeo in 2020. Based on the high-performance Quadrifoglio model, performance has been increased even further for these anniversary editions.

The power output of the 2.9L V6 twin-turbo engine has been increased to <540ps>. Use of lightweight construction materials throughout the car has decreased the weight by <100kg> and the front and rear track width has been increased by <50mm> to shorten the effective wheelbase, all resulting in a significant improvement to handling.

Additionally, the car features enlarged front fenders and arching over fenders on the rear, as well as a number of aerodynamic parts developed in conjunction with Alfa Romeo's F1 partner Sauber.

The GTAm offers a more hardcore setup designed for circuit use. It adds a larger front splitter and carbon fibre rear wing, while replacing the rear seats with a roll-cage.
DescriptionLong.0x00005660:
The first M3 of BMW appeared in 1985. This was a road car developed by BMW M, based on the E30 3 series, as a base car for participation in touring car racing.

Based on the 2 door Sedan, the tread width was widened, and the fenders were flared to match. Together with front and rear spoilers as well as side skirts, even the angle of the C Pillar and rear window was revised, with the rear boot changed to a high deck style. This improved the Cd value of the car from 0.38 to 0.33. The engine was a special 2.3 litre DOHC inline 4 cylinder, with a maximum output of <195ps>, and a maximum torque of <23.4kgm>.

The race spec model was introduced from 1987, and in the DTM it dominated the series by winning 5 races out of 10. While the car gained fame in motorsports around the world, further advancements were made to the Homologation model road car.

In the same year, the M3 Evolution was released with even further improved aerodynamics and a <210ps> engine. In 1988 the engine was further improved to produce <220ps> in the M3 Evolution II, and in 1989 the final model of the E30 type M3 was released. The final model, called the M3 Sports Evolution, had a bigger displacement of 2.5L according to racing regulations, and produced <238ps>/<24.5kgm>. Dedicated front and rear spoilers were also produced.,
DescriptionLong.0x00005661:
The 4th generation Mercedes-Benz C-Class was introduced in 2014, and as with previous models an AMG model was later introduced, coming in 2015.

Though it bears the same C63 badge as its predecessor, the engine itself is all new. The naturally aspirated 6.2L V8 has changed to the 4L V8 twin-turbo M177 engine, which uses the same basic configuration as the M178 in the AMG GT.

In terms of maximum power output and torque, the base C63 offers <476ps> and 650Nm (<66.3kgm>), while the high performance C63 S produces <510ps> and 700Nm (<71.4kgm>). Though both match the equivalent AMG GT models in horsepower, they actually offer greater torque figures and have been tuned to lower the start of the power band, widening its effective rpm range. These changes account for the car's weight which is heavier than a typical sports car and also its usability as an everyday car.

Originally only available as a sedan or station wagon, C63 and C63 S models were introduced for the coupé body in 2016.L
DescriptionLong.0x00005663:
Released in 2017, the Swift Sport is the high-performance model of the 4th generation Suzuki Swift, originally released in 2016.

The body has been redesigned for aerodynamic performance, in particular the nose is slightly lower than the standard swift. The engine has also been downsized from the naturally aspirated 1.6L unit featured in previous models to a 1.4L turbo configuration. Though this engine had previously been seen on other Suzuki models, it was retuned for sports performance allowing it to produce <140ps> and 230Nm (<23.45kgm>) on high-octane petrol.

Another difference from previous Swift Sport models is the suspension setup which is not only tuned specifically for this model but also increases the front and rear track width by <30mm> to improve handling. In addition, the body is both lighter and more rigid than the equivalent base Swift, while also being 70kg lighter than the previous Swift Sport model.
DescriptionLong.0x00005676:
The summer of 2004 saw the unveiling of the Ford GT, a supercar built to commemorate Ford's 100th anniversary. The car was conceived as a re-interpretation of Ford's legendary '60s-era GT40 using the latest in automotive technology. So we created this LM Race Car with the idea of tuning a Ford GT to Le Mans specs just to see what would result.

The original GT40 was developed for the purpose of winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans, a long-cherished dream of Ford's. During the heyday of Le Mans racing in the '60s, as top European makers like Ferrari and Porsche were fighting head-to-head for the title, this unlikely car emerged and showed what Ford was made of by winning the championship four years in a row, starting in 1966. So naturally we felt that the Ford GT, as the 'resurrected' GT40, just had to show up at Le Mans again. With that in mind, this car was created with an eye to now-defunct Le Mans GTS class regulations - this class being the home of such cars as the Corvette C5-R and the Viper GTS-R.

The engine is still Ford's characteristic supercharged 5.4 L DOHC V8, mid-mounted behind the seats and driving only the rear wheels just like in the normal GT, but the <558ps> output of the road model is boosted to a whopping <600ps> in the racing version. The suspension is double wishbone front and rear, and the gearbox is a racing spec 6-speed.[
DescriptionLong.0x000057E8:
The Type 964 that appeared in 1989 was the 3rd generation of the 911 that had evolved through the Type 901 and 930. It was a new generation of the 911, with roughly 80% of the component parts newly designed. Even the exterior that is similar to the 930 at a glance is full of modernism that takes aerodynamics into account.

In terms of its engineering, the displacement of the flat 6 engine was enlarged to 3.6 litres, and the new full-time all-wheel drive that was introduced in the 911 for the ‘Carrera 4’ was a hot topic. In the rear wheel drive model, a Tiptronic Automatic transmission was added to the line up to successfully enlarge their market.

This Type 964 also had a Turbo model for those who desired more power. The engine was initially a 3.3 litre <320ps> unit that was inherited from the 930, but a high power model commemorating the IMSA series participation was released in 1992. This was the 911 Turbo S.

The Turbo S was given high-lift cams and a special turbine to produce <381ps>/<50kgm> torque. Some of the body panels were replaced with carbon and aluminium, greatly reducing its weight in comparison to the standard Turbo model. The intake ducts on the rear tyre housing and the special rear spoiler became the identifying marks of the Turbo S. Only 86 examples of these cars were ever produced, making it one of the rarest 911’s of the series.
DescriptionLong.0x000057E9:
While Alpine's image is deeply tied to rally racing due to their immense success with the A110, they have also had a long history of success on the track, with the development of prototype racing cars in the 1960s.

The M63 developed in 1963, the improved M64 of 1964, and the further improved M65 of 1965 each won several races they competed in. And the even further developed A210 achieved respectable success in competition, even dominating 1st to 3rd place in the energy efficiency index of the Le Mans 24 hour race in 1967, plus two class victories in the same year.

Aiming to take the overall win in the next Le Mans 24 hour race, Alpine introduced the A220 in 1968. A new 3 litre V8 producing over <300ps> was developed, and combined with a newly designed tubular frame that was roughly <80kg> lighter.

Unfortunately the Alpine team faced various issues during the main race and did not achieve the desired result, but as the last hero car of Alpine before becoming a part of the Renault group, this car commands the respect of long time Alpine fans.
DescriptionLong.0x000057EA:
The debut of the 5th generation Honda Civic Type R was in 2017. The biggest difference of this Type R from previous models was that it was no longer a performance boosted model based on the standard Civic, but a car specifically designed to be a Type R from the beginning.

This allowed the car to utilise specialised designs for core technical aspects like the suspension, making it possible to use vastly different designs from the standard models.

The engine is carried over from the previous generation but improved by an additional <10ps> to <320ps> by fine tuning the engine control system. These changes increased the overall speed of the car, reclaiming the fastest time for a production front wheel drive on the Nürburgring Nordschleife at 7 minutes, 43.80 seconds.

The limited edition sold in 2020 is a model that further improves the quality of its driving performance. By equipping special forged wheels and removing soundproofing materials, the car was made <20kg> lighter, and further refined with specialised damper and EPS tuning. The limited world production run of 1000 cars of course sold out immediately.S
DescriptionLong.0x000057EB:
The Ferrari F8 Tributo is a mid-engine V8 model that was introduced in 2019 as the successor to the 488 GTB. This car can be considered a major mid-model change in the same manner as the 328 was to the 308, or the F430 to the 360 Modena.

On the exterior, the car's silhouette is somewhat similar to the 488 though it leaves an entirely different impression. This is mainly due to the been major changes that have been made to the vehicle's aerodynamics, from the flow of air both over and under the car to the convective cooling of the engine bay.

The power unit is the same as that used in the 488 Pista, which has been called the ultimate road-legal version of the 488. This <720ps>/770 Nm (<78.5kgm>) 3.9L V8 twin-turbo engine is as much at home on the circuit as on the street.

This is also their fastest ever V8 model, able to accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in 2.9s, 0.1s faster than the 488 GTB and <10km/h> faster at its top speed of <340km/h>. Thanks to extensive use of the latest in electronic stability systems, the car is also well known for being surprisingly easy to handle.
DescriptionLong.0x000057EC:
The first 'Evo' model of the 3rd generation Lancer was the Evolution VII, introduced in 2001. The most notable aspect of this Lancer 'Evo VII' was of course its Active Center Differential (ACD). Controlled in sync with the AYC system, the ACD raised the already high-traction performance of the VII to the next level. In 2002, the first automatic transmission Lancer Evolution model was introduced. This model brought together the 4G63 engine detuned to <272ps> and an INVECS-II electronically controlled automatic transmission with a manual shift mode.

2 years later, the 8th generation Lancer Evo VIII was released in January of 2003. With this model, the torque of the 4G63 engine was further increased to <40kgm>. Naturally, this model also saw further changes and enhancements to other areas of the drivetrain including the ACD and AYC systems.

And finally in February of 2004, the Lancer Evolution VIII MR was introduced as the final model of the Evo VIII series. This model features various refinements all across the vehicle, including the addition of an aluminium roof panel and the employment of Bilstein dampers for the very first time.L
DescriptionLong.0x000057ED:
McLaren fought the 1988 F1 World Championships season in the MP4/4. This was a low height, low drag machine designed by Gordon Murray and Steve Nichols, powered by the Honda RA168E engine.

This was also the last year for turbocharged machines in Formula racing. With the allowed maximum boost pressures reduced from 4 bars to 2.5 bars, and on board fuel reduced by 45 litres to 150 litres in total, it was supposed to be a very tough season for the turbocharged machines.

But in the end the McLaren Honda MP4/4 totally dominated the season with 15 wins out of 16 races. Of course the chassis was very well developed, but the Honda engine which balanced fuel consumption and effective power extremely well is said to be the major factor in their victory.

The number 12 MP4/4 was the car driven by Ayrton Senna. Senna put on an incredible performance this year with 13 pole positions and 8 wins, and won the drivers’ championship.
DescriptionLong.0x000057EF:
RUF is a company that continues to create unique sports cars based on Porsches, infused with their own philosophy and craftsmanship. One of their continuing model lines include the “RGT”, based on various 911 GT3 models.

At the very core of the RGT is a concept to polish the performance of the GT3 model even further, while miraculously bestowing it the comfort of a road car. And at the 2015 Geneva show, RUF added a new model to this family tree: The RGT 4.2, based on the type 991, 911 GT3.

As the name implies it is powered by a 4.2L flat 6, increasing the displacement from the stock 3.8L of the type 991, 911 GT3 by <400cc>. But the increased displacement is not the only point of note. The RGT 4.2 engine is not just a tuned 911 GT3 engine, but uses the “Mezger engine” with the GT1 crankshaft as a base; an engine that has seen many successes in racing since the air cooled days of the flat 6. The car produces <125ps> per litre, for a maximum power output of <525ps>.

On the exterior it is equipped with aggressive riveted overfenders, and the interior sports the integrated roll cage that the RGT series is known for. Combining competition blood with the grace of a road car, this is another fine example of a RUF, the ultimate car for a gentleman driver who enjoys both the track and daily use.
DescriptionLong.0x000057F0:
The Type S was a car that could be called the first sports car of Mercedes-Benz, produced from 1927 to 1933.

Designed by Dr. Ferdinand Porsche, the chassis exhibited superior driving performance. Compared to the Model K, which can be considered its predecessor, it was better in terms of its centre of gravity and weight balance. The model powered by a supercharged 7 litre inline 6 produced 177.5 BHP, which was very powerful in terms of performance for its day.

This Type S with its signature bodywork which won both the Best of Show as well as the Gran Turismo Trophy at the 2017 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, is the ‘Barker Tourer’.

Its first owner was Earl Howe, a decorated racing driver who had won the Mille Miglia and the 24 Hours of Le Mans, who is also the cofounder of the British Racing Driver’s Club. He commissioned the British coachbuilder ‘Barker’, founded in 1710, to build him a light weight tourer body with a boat-tail design.

This is an extremely rare and valuable one-off model.
DescriptionLong.0x000057F1:
The 550/1500RS is a racing sportscar sold by Porsche from late 1954.

The 550 in its name is derived from the fact that its dry weight is <550kg>. The chassis combining a steel tube frame with an aluminium body was fitted with a 4 cam flat 4 engine producing <135ps>.

The car saw significant success in various races, and won its class at the 1954 Le Mans 24 hour race. In the 1955 race, it achieved 4th overall, with another class victory.

The French Blue 1500RS with Chassis number 550-0067 was a unit originally delivered to a French dealership, and also displayed at the Paris Motor Show.

This is an extremely rare race car that still bears its original livery and paint from its participation in the 1956 Le Mans 24 hour race, and is said to have been owned by famed French racing driver Jean Marie Behra.
DescriptionLong.0x00007F6B:
The Version NISMO Type 380RS is a Z33 Fairlady Z-based complete car built by NISMO. Years of experience from being the factory racing team for Nissan has provided NISMO with cutting-edge racing technology, which in turn has been implemented into this car.

The 300-unit limited edition machine is a works tuned road car, with improved body rigidity, reinforced brakes, tuned suspension, front and rear aerodynamic bumpers and a rear spoiler. The VQ35HR 3.8 L racing engine has been detuned for road use, and produces <350ps> @ <7200rpm> and <40.5kgm> @ <4800rpm>.

Power House Amuse tuned this car even further, to create the Amuse NISMO 380RS Super Leggera. By changing compression ratios and tuning the intake and exhaust systems, the power output was increased to <386ps> @ <7100rpm> and <41.8kgm> @ <4860rpm>.

Furthermore, as the name Super Leggera (literally 'super light' in Italian) implies, weight has been reduced to <1370kg> - <140kg> lighter than the original model. This was achieved by replacing the roof panel and many other body parts with carbon, and utilising titanium for the exhaust system and other metal parts.

These parts are not just for lightweight and looks; they all take into account important functions such as cooling efficiency and aerodynamics.

This car was displayed at the Tokyo Auto Salon in January 2008, and received the Gran Turismo Award as selected by the GT series producer, Kazunori Yamauchi.
DescriptionLong.0x00007F6C:
The Celica received a full model change again in October 1993, and became the 6th generation model. From this version, it starts to stand out as a front-wheel drive sports coupé with futuristic styling.

The major change in the 6th generation was the increase to the Japanese class 3 body size. The <4435mm> length and the height of <1305mm> is almost the same as the previous model, but the <1750mm> width opened doors for new design potential in the Celica. It discarded the rounded look of the previous model, progressing to a design with emphasised indents and protrusions. The headlights were also changed from the previous retractable lights to a set of four round headlights which served to define the face of the car.

Two types of 2.0 L DOHC inline-4 engines were available, a 3S-GE model with <180ps>, and a 3S-FE model with <140ps>. The suspension used traditional front/rear struts, with disc brakes front and rear (ventilated at the front). The 3S-FE equipped model was called the SS-I, and the 3S-GE model was called the SS-II. 4WS was available for the SS-I, and the SS-II could be fitted with the newly developed super strut suspension.

In February 1994, the GT-Four, a familiar base model for the WRC, was released. The GT-Four was equipped as standard with an aluminium bonnet, complete with power bulge, and a rear spoiler, and the output of the 3S-GTE 2.0 L turbo was increased to <255ps>. The convertible model also debuted in this year.
DescriptionLong.0x00007F6D:
The 3rd generation Dodge Challenger was introduced in 2008 as the true successor to the masterpiece muscle car that was the original Challenger. The car is well known for the various performance models that have been released since its debut, but in 2015 the veil was lifted on the most powerful model yet, the SRT Hellcat.

However, the star of the line-up had yet to appear. That was the SRT Demon, produced in a limited run of 3,300 units in 2018.

This car is a monster built for the single purpose of winning drag races. The engine, based on the Hellcat model, has been tuned to produce <852ps> on 100 or higher octane fuel. Subsequently the car is able to achieve such astounding figures as a 0-62 mph (<100km/h>) time of 2.3s and a quarter mile time of just 9.65s. The body is also a full drag strip setup with no passenger or rear seats included as standard, though they are available as an option.
