DescriptionLong.0x0000CB81:
'MAZDA SPIRIT RACING' was an initiative started by Mazda to establish the company's place in motorsports and train new talent through racing. Competing in competitions like the Super Endurance Series with a large crew made up of company employees, it has since developed into a major presence in the sport.

This team would go on to design a car based on all the skills and knowledge it had acquired from its racing experience. The car was unveiled as the 'MAZDA SPIRIT RACING ROADSTER 12R' in early 2025, at the Tokyo Auto Salon.

As the name suggests, it is based on the ND Mazda Roadster. That said, it is packed to the brim with parts worthy of its works team.

The highlight of this is the engine which uses a 2L block not normally available on the domestic soft-top model, and adds a specially tuned head, pistons, and exhaust manifold among other parts, with every unit assembled by hand. The power has been increased to near the limit of what is possible with a production car that also requires longevity, coming in at <200ps>.

The chassis owes much to its makers’ experience in the Super Endurance series. For instance, the suspension uses specially tuned height-adjustable dampers from Bilstein, while the brakes feature 4-piston calipers from Brembo. The forged Rays wheels are the same as those seen on race cars.

There are numerous other special parts as well, such as the Recaro seats and a Fujitsubo exhaust system. Made in a limited run of 200 units, this is quite possibly the ultimate works-tuned roadster.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CB82:
The Toyota Land Cruiser was first pitched as a vehicle for Japan's National Police Reserve, evolving into a world class off-roader thanks to its remarkable all-terrain abilities and reliability. Over 70 years later, the model that still holds a special place in the hearts of Land Cruiser fans is the 3rd generation model '40' that was introduced in 1960.

Land Cruiser exports began with the model '20' in 1955, and the car soon became a contender on the world stage. The model '40' was designed to better meet the expectations of global customers. Besides an exterior design update, the model was notable for building on already lauded off-road capabilities by improving comfort for highway driving.

The 40 was available in short, medium, or long wheelbase variants, each suited to different purposes. The 2-door hardtop model seen here saw extensive use in mountainous regions, where it was able to effectively use its short <2285mm> wheelbase.

The car is relatively compact, measuring in at <3870mm> in length, <1690mm> in width, and <1930mm> in height. It was originally fitted with a 3.9L 'F' petrol engine, but the introduction of the 3L 'B' diesel engine in 1974 only added to the car's popularity. The drivetrain is a part-time four-wheel drive system with a 2-speed transfer case. This model truly embodies the Land Cruiser philosophy of 'go anywhere and come back alive'.

Along with this 2-door hardtop, the model '40' line would prove to be one of the Land Cruiser's bestsellers, staying in production for 24 years, until 1984. It proved to be so popular that in 2006, Toyota introduced the FJ Cruiser, a model which resurrected a number of motifs from the classic 40.

Furthermore, in 2021, Toyota announced the reproduction of model 40 parts through GAZOO Racing, proving that the model 40 Land Cruiser is an evergreen model that will always be worth driving.0
DescriptionLong.0x0000CB83:
When it was introduced in 1994, the Toyota RAV4 pioneered a new market segment known as 'the crossover SUV.' Offering smooth off-road handling in a compact body, the first-generation model was widely acclaimed for its ability to transcend the categories of on-road and off-road vehicles, and continued to evolve thereafter. In 2018, a 5th-generation model with a new platform was released. Based on the Toyota New Global Architecture (TNGA), this model set the standard for driving, safety, and comfort.

The Adventure grade displays the most fundamental characteristics of an SUV. Equipped with a custom front grille, skid-plate bumper and 19-inch tyres, it has a rugged styling that suggests a readiness to take on the great outdoors. Its powertrain combines a 2-litre 4-cylinder Dynamic Force Engine with Direct Shift-CVT, enabling both smooth acceleration and high fuel efficiency.

Of particular note is the application of a newly developed Dynamic Torque Vectoring AWD system, which controls torque distribution to the left and right rear wheels, balancing traction and stability. It also features a disconnect mechanism that allows the driver to cut off the rear-drive system for better fuel economy.

In terms of safety, the Toyota Safety Sense preventative safety package comes standard in all models, and includes such features as a pre-collision safety system, Lane Tracing Assist, and adaptive Radar Cruise Control. The car also comes with other useful features, such as a multimedia system with smartphone integration, and a Panoramic View Monitor that gives the driver a birds-eye view around their car.

The ideal modern SUV, this car easily traverses urban and natural environments, adding a sense of adventure to your daily drives.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD03:
The Polestar 5 is the flagship model of the Scandinavian high-performance electric car brand 'Polestar'. This car is the realisation of the ideas introduced by the 'Precept' concept car unveiled in 2020, embodied through pure Scandinavian design, cutting-edge technology and sustainability.

The stretched form of the <5m> long body takes inspiration from aircraft, while the panel structure and glass roof which stretches towards the rear of the vehicle deliver excellent aerodynamic performance. The body boasts a drag coefficient of just 0.24 and uses bonded aluminium construction to create a lightweight yet rigid structure, with better torsional rigidity than many sports cars.

The power train uses a dual-motor system, based around an in-house developed electric rear motor. The Performance edition is capable of a total system output of 650 kW (<884ps>), and achieving a 0-<100km/h> time of just 3.2s. The 800 V electric architecture can use 350 kW fast charging, allowing the battery to charge from 10% to 80% in just 22 minutes. The maximum range under WLTP testing is <670km> (Dual Motor edition).

The suspension uses a specially designed double wishbone construction. The Performance edition features magnetorheological fluid dampers, which read the road surface up to 1000 times per second, offering both comfort and agility. The car also features extensive driver assistance systems, with automatic lane and speed control up to <150km/h>.

A futuristic design, outstanding electric performance and sustainability, the Polestar 5 offers all of these in the ultimate grand tourer package.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD04:
Ferrari has produced a number of racing machines based on their road-going super sports cars, achieving excellent results in endurance and GT racing championships. The 296 GT3 is one such car to carry on that DNA, developed from the 296 GTB.

As a pure racing car, the 296 GT3 removes the plug-in hybrid system found on the road-car, using only the 600 horsepower V6 twin-turbo engine. This power unit uses a 3L displacement 120-degree V6 design, extensively modified for weight reduction and reliability. The drivetrain and cooling components, as well as the aero parts have all been replaced with special racing versions. 

Unlike classic racing Ferraris, which were constructed by Michelotto, this car was built by legendary racing car constructors, Oreca. From the chassis construction, to assembly, to after-sales services, Oreca provides full end-to-end support. The car was first unveiled at the 2022 24 Hours of Spa, held in July, before making its racing debut at the 2023 24 Hours of Daytona the next year.

The 296 GT3 is not just limited to current international endurance championships; the design is still evolving towards the future. An Evo model with enhanced aerodynamic and endurance performance has already been announced for the 2026 season. 

Combining the sophistication of the road-going model with the pure speed of a racing machine, this car services as the new standard-bearer for Ferrari's motorsports strategy.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD05:
There is a long standing tradition within the Ferrari line-up that their super sports models use a midship mounted V8 configuration. With a lightweight, high-revving engine behind the driver, this layout provides sharp response and high manoeuvrability, and has become emblematic of the brand. The 296 GTB carries on parts of this tradition while opening the door to new possibilities.

To start, the 296 GTB is the first Ferrari to use a V6 twin-turbo engine. It also marks the first time a V6 block had been used in over half a century, having been last used on the 206 and 246 under the Dino brand. With a displacement of <2992cc>, this innovative design uses a 120-degree bank angle with IHI turbochargers placed within the bank space.

One of the major factors behind the move to a V6 powertrain is the addition of a plug-in hybrid (PHEV) system. Combined with a 123 kW electric motor, the system provides a total output of 830 horsepower, allowing for an astoundingly fast 0-<100km/h> acceleration time at just 2.9s. And with a top speed of <330km/h>, this car provides performance befitting the Ferrari name.

The body design is an homage to the classic 250 LM of the 1960s and is also the most compact among the current Ferrari line-up. The tunnel-back style rear window provides both aerodynamic performance and a touch of elegance. The 296 GTB blends the classic midship sports layout with revolutionary technology, making it the epitome of the new generation of Ferraris.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD06:
In 1980, as demand for smaller cars was rising following the oil shock, FIAT released a bold new compact to replace the ageing 126. In a stark change from the 126, this 'Panda' was a front-wheel drive hatchback with a transverse front-mounted engine.

While relatively simple, the design was modern and practical. The packaging of the Panda was conceived by design maestro Giorgetto Giugiaro. In order to reduce costs, the body panels were comprised of flat surfaces and straight lines, while the windows used flat glass. The seats, as well, used a simple hammock design with fabric stretched over a pipe frame, but the overall look of the car was fresh, and the interior was surprisingly roomy.

At its debut, the Panda was available with either a <652cc> 2-cylinder air-cooled engine or a <903cc> 4-cylinder water-cooled engine. At this time, FIAT named their engines according to the power output, with the former known as the '30' and the latter the '45'. In 1983, a part-time four-wheel drive '4x4' model was released. It marked a world first for a vehicle with a transverse-engined, front-wheel-drive layout.

The Panda was an immediate hit on its release, becoming one of the major propelling forces behind FIAT’s success. Giugiaro himself claimed at the time that this gem of compact car design was his greatest work yet.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD07:
Mine's are well known as a long-standing tuner in the Nissan scene, and their most representative work is undoubtedly the 'BNR34 GT-R N1 base' complete tuned car.

Born in 1999, this car is an extensive exploration of the beauty of the R34 model GT-R, while keeping to the tenets of street car style. From the tuning of the RB26DETT, to the low-slung suspension, to the understated exterior, everything has been crafted under the philosophy of Mine's CEO Michizo Niikura, to create 'a first-class street car'.

And yet, the car is also capable of performing well on the closed track. It effortlessly set a lap time under 1-min on Tsukuba Circuit, proving its true ability.

As a result, this particular car, known as the 'Hon-Demo' among enthusiasts, managed the incredible achievement of recording over <10000km> on the odometer with circuit use alone.

However, its legend did not end there. In 2021, the car underwent a full restoration by Garage Yoshida, breathing new life into the beast. The original front GT-R emblem was kept unrestored by Niikura's request. The price of the car within Gran Turismo 7, 3 million Cr., is also a tribute to the passion of the owner, who refused an offer of the same amount.

Thanks to the efforts of Japanese restomod builder 'Built By Legends' the value of the BNR34 GT-R N1 base is being reconsidered across the globe. If you ever have the chance to see one in person, you should consider yourself very lucky.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD08:
The FTO which appeared in October of 1994 is a model that made a comeback 23 years after the debut of the original model. The first Galant coupé FTO was a little brother to the Galant GTO, and the new model was also positioned as a 2-door coupé next in line from the GTO.

The 1st generation model was an FR, but the new model was an FF, since it shared platforms with the Lancer/Mirage. The body was a larger size class 3 in Japanese regulations, a rarity in its time, and its wide body was very characteristic of the model.

Its design, with strong flowing curves, was in line with the GTO and Eclipse of the day. The front fenders were almost at one with the hood, and took on a bold form that flowed continuously all the way to the rear fenders.

It was powered by a 1.8 L SOHC inline-4, 4G93 engine producing <125ps> and <16.5kgm> of torque, or a 2 L DOHC V6, 6A12 engine that produced <170ps> and <19.0kgm> torque (<180ps> and <19.5kgm> in late models), or a highly tuned 6A12 producing <200ps> and <20.4kgm> torque. The <200ps> of the highly tuned engine was achieved through the MIVEC variable valve timing mechanism.

Its transmission was also revolutionary. In addition to the standard 5-speed manual, an INVECS-II 4-speed AT with a sports mode was added to the lineup for the first time in Japanese cars, and led the way for other Sports AT models that came thereafter.

Its unique styling and driving performance was highly regarded, and it won the Japan Car of the Year for 1994. In 1997, the INVECS-II was changed from a 4-speed to a 5-speed. Unfortunately, as the trends shifted gradually from coupés to MPVs and SUVs, the FTO ceased production in 2000.;
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD09:
The Renault Espace debuted in 1984 as Europe's first minivan. 10 years later in 1994, an extraordinary version of the Espace was unveiled at the Paris Motor Show. This beast of a machine carried an F1 engine in the centre of the body, and was dubbed the Espace F1.

The original plans for this machine came from Matra who had initially pitched the Espace to Renault and produced its fibreglass body panels. At the time, Renault had been partnered with Williams in their successful bid for victory in Formula One. Matra proposed that they take the 3.5L V10 'RS4' engine from the 1992 championship winning FW14B car and put it in the Espace as both a celebration of the 10th anniversary of the Espace, and a symbol of Renault's victory.

Constructed in Matra's Romorantin plant in France, the Espace F1 is an entirely unorthodox minivan. It reuses part of the basic chassis from the second generation model, but has replaced most of the materials across the body with aluminium and carbon fibre. The width of the body has been stretched out in order to house the wide tyres, and the roof end adorned with a giant wing to push the body downwards.

The power unit and heart of the beast is mounted midship between the front and rear axles. On the interior, the three rows of seats have been replaced with 4 carbon fibre bucket seats, with the intake funnels of engine proudly on show between the 2 rear seats. It has a maximum power output of <800ps> and a 0-<100km/h> time of 2.8s, eventually accelerating to a top speed of <316km/h>.

F1 drivers like Alain Prost actually drove the Espace F1 on circuit, letting out the characteristic high-pitched whine of the racing engine as it drove past the crowds.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD0A:
'Gran Turismo' features the F3500-A, an original formula machine created as a love letter to early 90s F1. This car is a representation of the speed and technology of that era, serving to bring players a breathtaking formula racing experience.

To carry on that genealogy, we bring you the new F3500-B. The greatest difference between the two models is the power unit. While the F3500-A featured a naturally aspirated V12 engine, the F3500-B uses a lightweight, compact V8.

While there are no high-tech systems like variable intakes or pneumatic valves, it still uses the same electronic fly-by-wire throttle as the F3500-A. The engine is able to rev to <13800rpm>, meaning that even with the shortcomings in power inherent to the V8, it can produce over <710ps>. The transmission is a 6-speed unit mounted transversely for optimum packaging. 

The body shape is the same as the F3500-A, but there have been some modifications to the front end. There are 3 different front wings available for the high-nose, each with a different visual approach to aerodynamics.

The formula car response and direct feel come from the F3500-A design, but we invite you to experience the 'lightness' of this V8.7
DescriptionLong.0x0000CF1F:
Xiaomi has achieved global success in the world of smart devices. Utilizing those same technologies and their innovative spirit, Xiaomi turned their attention to the electric mobility market. Their debut model was the 'SU7' sports saloon which quickly found success, but development on the car did not end there. They would follow it up with a monster variant that would challenge the preconceptions of BEVs. This car was the SU7 Ultra.

The SU7 Ultra uses a 3 motor all-wheel drive system, placing one motor on the front axle, and 2 on the rear. This provides a system total output of up to <1548ps>, with the rear axle 'V8s' type electric motors able to rotate at speeds of up to <27200rpm>, an unprecedented feat for a production model. This translates into sensational performance, able to accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in just 1.98 seconds, and reaching a top speed of <350km/h>.

Xiaomi have not missed any opportunity for innovation in the body either. High rigidity with low weight has been achieved through extensive use of carbon fibre body panels, and 'cell to body' construction which seamlessly integrates the battery and chassis. This presents a whole new era of production car construction.

The exterior has been set up for maximum aerodynamic performance, with the carbon fibre body kit producing up to <285kg> of downforce. Special attention has also been made to stopping power, brakes allow the car to decelerate from <100km/h> to a complete stop in a distance of just <30.8m>.

With its luxurious interior, electronically controlled active suspension, and the latest in ADAS, the SU7 Ultra offers fantastic cost performance as well. This ultimate mobility solution marks a turning point in the history of the BEV.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D167:
The 'ELANTRA N' is a high-performance sedan from Hyundai's N brand. There is also a special edition of this car made specifically for motorsports, the ELANTRA N TC.

The base model ELANTRA N is already an excellent pick for the circuit, featuring a 2.0L direct-injection turbo engine producing <280ps> power and <40.0kgm> torque, and able to accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in 5.3 secs on a front-wheel drive layout. With these solid fundamentals in hand, the TC has been specially modified to fit international touring car regulations, and imbued with the power to win.

The strong downforce provided by its aerodynamic wide body, carbon fibre splitter and large rear wing has greatly improved high speed cornering ability. The drivetrain features a sequential 6-speed gearbox, and special racing suspension and adjustable dampers allow it to instantly adapt to road conditions. The brakes and cooling systems have also been upgraded with endurance race spec parts.

Efforts to reduce weight and increase rigidity have been made throughout, with the cockpit featuring a regulation roll cage and racing seat. The steering and pedal layout also allow for instant response to driver inputs. The ELANTRA N TC has been carefully crafted into a machine with the potential for victory on the track, yet it retains the agility and reliability of the road car.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D18E:
Since the introduction of the original Porsche 911 in 1963 over half a century ago, the 911 has long been seen as the epitome of the sports car on both public roads and racing circuits around the world. With its unique rear-mounted flat-6 engine and highly tuned performance, the 911 series has claimed victory in countless races, cementing its position in automotive history.

This bloodline was continued by the 8th generation '992' model 911, released in 2018. With features like stretched rear fenders on all models, 4-point LED headlights and intricate rear combination lamps, this car is the true embodiment of the modern Porsche design philosophy. Built around the 3.0L flat-6 turbo engine, technological upgrades like improved cooling and the 8-speed PDK transmission allow for peak performance in any task from everyday to sports driving.

The 992 model was also developed into a pure racing model as the 911 GT3 R.

Released in 2022, this machine houses a 4.2L flat-6 engine, producing up to <565ps>. It features carbon fibre and aramid woven components, along with the double wishbone and multi-link suspension from the 911 RSR. The wheelbase has also been lengthened over the previous 991 model from <2459mm> to <2507mm>.

The brakes feature AP Racing discs, while the driver controls have been updated with new steering components and a 10.3-inch user display. The 911 GT3 R is the concentration of all Porsche's racing knowledge and technology, a single car built to dominate the circuit.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D1B5:
Introduced in 1966, the Camaro was created as a pony car to take on Ford's Mustang, with the high performance Z28 model developed for homologation for the SCCA's 'Trans-Am Series'.

The Z28 was released as a hardcore motorsports base model, equipped with a high-revving 302 cubic inch (approx. 4.9L) V8 engine, and no options available for automatic transmissions or air conditioning. One such car under Penske Racing claimed a championship victory in the Trans-Am Series. Such results would create a new trend of small displacement, high-revving American V8s.

Created by Gran Turismo, this 'Camaro 1969 Race-Mod' is modern reinterpretation of the original Camaro Z28. The spirit of classic Trans-Am is carried on in the car's low stance, with a number of elements added from the restomod movement that has seen much popularity at events like SEMA. All the chrome trim has been stripped from the exterior and replaced with carbon black parts. A wide mouth bumper, large ducktail spoiler and a centre exit exhaust have also been added.

The spartan interior features a sequential shifter, roll cage and Alcantara bucket seats. Behind these classical stylings though, lies the true identity of the beast: a supercharged V8 engine producing <667ps>. The ultimate modern Trans-American race car rebuilds tradition through new technologies.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D243:
The Captur is a compact crossover SUV made by Renault. The first model appeared in 2013 and quickly became popular for its urban design and excellent utility. The second generation model was released in 2019, with an updated platform that improved driving performance and ride quality. From here the C-shaped signature light became its identifying character. 

At <4.23m> long, <1.8m> wide and <1.58m> tall, it balances the agility of a compact with the presence of an SUV. The enlarged wheel base and folding rear seat also allows flexible use of its cargo space. 

The powertrain differs according to regions and grade models offered, powered by everything from a 1.0 or 1.3 litre turbocharged petrol engine to diesel and Hybrids. The car was even offered in what is Renault's first plug in hybrid; the E-TECH PHEV utilises hybrid technology garnered by the Renault F1 team, running quietly and efficiently using its electric motor assist.

The agile handling and stable ride, and the quality interior and cutting edge infotainment system provides comfort for the driver as well as all its passengers. Manoeuvring in this car is easy from its high vantage point, allowing the driver to go from daily commute to winding rural roads stress free. This car is a jack of all trades that goes beyond the boundaries of your typical compact SUV.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D314:
In 1990, Renault switched over from the Super 5 to the Clio. The increased body size of the Clio however left a space in the line-up for a smaller model. The car created to fulfil these needs was the Twingo, an A-segment hatchback.

The Twingo is famous for its 3-door monospace body with an almost continuous single flowing from the truncated bonnet, over the roof and to the rear end. This design set it apart from its contemporary rivals, shocking the market on its 1992 debut. The 4 wheels have been placed in the very corners of the body, allowing for an unusual amount of interior space given its compact form at <3433mm> long and <1423mm> tall.

Upon its debut, the Twingo was equipped with a transverse mounted 1.2L inline-4 OHV engine. While this would only provide the minimum of necessary power, it paired well with the lightweight body, providing a jaunty ride about town. The car was also lauded for bringing character to a practical vehicle, with its sliding rear seats providing a number of possible seating arrangements.

The first generation Twingo would receive a number of engine and aesthetic upgrades over the years, remaining in production for 14 years until 2007. Practical, yet loveable, it stands as one of the most revolutionary models in A-segment history.T
DescriptionLong.0x0000D315:
With one electric motor on each of the 4 wheels, the Yangwang U9 is a revolutionary model that challenges the concepts of electric supercars.

Released by Yangwang, BYD's luxury brand, this car uses their proprietary e⁴ platform which features 4 electric motors, producing an incredible total system output of 960kW, or roughly <1305ps>. Hold down the accelerator to go from 0-<100km/h> in 2.36 seconds. This blinding acceleration time could easily make you forget this is a heavyweight EV. 

The value of this model isn't limited to its power either. The 'DiSus-X' suspension system integrates hydraulic and pneumatic systems for complete control over the body balance, sometimes lifting the tires into the air, and sometimes almost dancing. This movement isn't just for show however, serving as the technical core of the Yangwang U9, this 4-wheel independent suspension control system allows for unprecedented ride stability and controllability.

Designed by Wolfgang Egger, the car's scissor door coupe form feels futuristic without losing any of its appeal or impact as a supercar.

In 2025, the U9 Xtreme, a high performance version of the U9, attempted to set a new world speed record, clocking in at an astounding <496.22km/h>. The Yangwang U9 can be seen as an embodiment of power and technology, and the epitome of speed in the electrification era.[
DescriptionLong.0x0000D403:
The BMW M Hybrid V8 is a cutting edge prototype car developed to the 'Le Mans Daytona h' (LMDh) specification. The Dallara made carbon fibre monocoque is outfitted with a DTM derived 'P66/3' 4L V8 twin-turbo engine in a hybrid configuration. This power unit, which produces a total system output of <680ps>, combines the roar of an internal combustion engine with the instantaneous delivery of electric assists, creating competitive performance worthy of the M badge.

The wide 'kidney' grilles of the front fascia create a sense of majesty that lets you know this is a BMW at a single glance. Lined with laser lights, these grilles have been sculpted to represent the brand's traditions and future thinking technologies, while also maximizing aerodynamics and cooling in a form of functional beauty.

In the 2025 season, the BMW M Hybrid V8 entered the IMSA SportsCar Championship and FIA World Endurance Championship sporting a digital mosaic livery. In the 8th round of the IMSA, Road America, the car dominated the field, securing a one-two finish and building a reputation for BMW in the GTP Class. Meanwhile in the WEC, it showed a strong presence with its performance in rounds like Imola, competing at the very peak of endurance racing.

Though it carried over much from celebrated prototypes like the V12 LMR, hybrid technology allowed this car to become a flagship paving the way for a whole new era. Tradition, revolution and the drive to win, this car combines them all.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D404:
The 963 is Porsche's newest generation Le Mans Daytona h (LMDh) category prototype that carries on the concepts embodied by the legendary 962 and 919 Hybrid. The Multimatic carbon fibre monocoque is equipped with a 4.6L V8 twin-turbo engine that has its roots in the 918 Spyder, combined with a standardised hybrid system. It's a package that combines the efficiency, reliability and overwhelming performance demanded by high-level endurance racing.

The 963 had a glorious debut at the 2023 24 Hours of Daytona, and would go on to compete in both the World Endurance Championship (WEC) and the IMSA Championship. Alongside the esteemed Team Penske, it would challenge for the very pinnacle of the world of endurance racing.

The 963 truly blossomed in 2024. It won the opening IMSA race at Daytona, and followed it up with victories at Laguna Seca, Watkins Glen, and Road America—performances that saw it clinch both the drivers' and manufacturers' championships.

Its results at the WEC were also highly impressive. It showed a consistent pace across all races, winning in Qatar, at Spa Francorchamps, and on the Fuji Speedway, clinching the drivers' title in 2024.

Porsche withdrew the 963 from the WEC at the end of 2025, but an updated model continued to compete in the IMSA Championship in 2026. The 963 is something of a masterpiece, and has burnished Porsche's reputation as the kings of endurance racing.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D405:
The 2023 edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans was a very special race, marking the 100th anniversary of the world's premier endurance racing event. Aware of the glory that the winners would enjoy, teams unleashed their most cutting-edge technology, sending their very best cars to the Circuit de la Sarthe.

It was a high-powered showdown, but even among the storied field, most eyes were on Ferrari. They were, after all, returning to the top category for the first time in 50 years, when the 312 P competed in the 1973 edition. The car tasked with replicating this triumph was the prototype 499P. The 499P is a hypercar developed according to Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) regulations in order to compete in the World Endurance Championship (WEC)'s top category. The '499' part of the name refers to the displacement per cylinder, while the 'P' stands for 'prototype'. The hybrid system combines a 3-litre V6 twin turbo with a front-mounted MGU, and is capable of outputting 500 kW.

Its styling was done with more than pure speed in mind. It's futuristic, but also unmistakably Ferrari. That is a large part of the 499P's charm.

The race itself was very closely fought, but in the end car 51 came out on top. The 100th edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans therefore saw Ferrari make a spectacular return to the Circuit de la Sarthe, notching up their first victory in 58 years!
DescriptionLong.0x0000D406:
The Peugeot 9X8 is a Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) developed by the pride of France, Peugeot Sport, to conquer Le Mans. After stepping down from the pinnacle of endurance racing in 2011, Peugeot returned in 2022 under the LMH category and with them came the 9X8. The '9' refers to its lineage in models like the 905 and 908. The 'X' denotes that it is an all-wheel drive hybrid of the electrification era. Finally, the '8' represents its relationship to current models.

Upon its debut, the 9X8 attracted much attention for its revolutionary aerodynamic design that allowed it to forgo a rear wing. The body shape had been crafted from meticulous calculation of downforce and drag, turning the paradigm for prototype cars on its head.

However, the new summer 2022 regulations called for changes to the freedom of aerodynamics and tyre sizes. Complying with the new regulations, the 2024 model features different sized tyres on the front and rear, along with overhauls to the weight distribution and aerodynamic balance. This radical evolution called for a redesign of roughly 90% of the bodywork and the addition of a large rear wing.

The 2025 model further built on these improvements to create this perfected final form. Built around the hybrid powertrain which combines a 2.6L V6 twin-turbo engine with a front-mounted MGU, the car has been tuned for reliability and consistent performance. It would prove its potential in the hotly contested 2025 season of the FIA World Endurance Championship, where Peugeot scored a podium finish in the Fuji round, coming second. Crafted through innovation and iteration, the 9X8 is an excellent representation of Peugeot's racing prowess.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D407:
This 992 model 911 Turbo S is a virtual model created by Gran Turismo, reimagined as a safety car leading the pack in the event of an incident.

The original 992 model 911 Turbo S is the top performance model of the 8th generation Porsche 911. Based on the newly developed MMB platform, the wide body uses a high percentage of aluminium parts in a merging of tradition and innovation. The rear-mounted <3745cc> flat-6 twin-turbo engine produces <650ps> and 800 Nm (<81.6kgm>) torque, which runs through an 8-speed PDK transmission and sophisticated four-wheel drive system before reaching the track surface. It is able to accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in just 2.7s and reach a top speed of <330km/h> but this serves as just a glimpse of its true potential.

Qualities like its excellent traction ability and stability make the 911 Turbo S perfect for the role of leading the field as a safety car. Meanwhile, its ability to effortlessly keep a pack of race cars in line without faltering is in no doubt thanks to its outstanding performance and high level chassis control.Y
DescriptionLong.0x0000D4B5:
The IONIQ 6 N is the second high performance EV from Hyundai’s high-performance ‘N’ brand. It carries on from the brilliant precedent set by the IONIQ 5 N which shook the world on its spectacular debut at the 2023 Goodwood Festival of Speed.

The IONIQ 6 N was named 2026 World Performance Car, marking the second time in three years that Hyundai’s N brand secured the award following the IONIQ 5 N in 2024.

One of its most attractive points is the elegant exterior which embodies the aerodynamic flow of the wind. This uniquely supple silhouette is not just for aesthetics, as it boasts a drag coefficient (Cd) of just 0.27 while also producing downforce for high speed stability.

In terms of performance, N offers a new dynamic standard for the electrification era. With a total system power output of <650ps> and 770 Nm torque, it can accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in just 3.2s. However, the true value of this machine won’t be found in its figures alone. The ‘N Active Sound+’ system recreates different sounds, such as the roar of an internal combustion engine, while ‘N e-Shift’ creates the sensation of gear shifting in EVs, providing the driver with direct feedback.

The car is packed with numerous other features as well, like ‘N Grin Boost’ which unlocks full power for 10 seconds, the proprietary ‘N Drift Optimizer’ which enables slides on demand, and an action camera mount on the ceiling to capture it all.

From driving at the limit on track, to the winding roads of daily life, the IONIQ 6 N sets out to accelerate driving pleasure. Ultimately, this epoch-making model represents the future shape of the sports car.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D4B6:
Originally released in 1968, the Toyota Mark II was Japan's answer to the medium-sized saloon. The Tourer V is a sports trim grade that became available from the 7th generation Mark II onwards. The version shown here is the Tourer V from the 8th generation Mark II, also known as the X100 series. The clean cut long-nose sedan body and wild driving character result in a very attractive car.

Its most notable feature is the power unit. The 2.5L inline-6 1JZ-GTE engine is a further evolved 2nd generation model with variable valve timing and equipped with a single turbocharger, it produces <280ps>/<38.5kgm>. Also available with a 5-speed manual transmission, a push of the throttle pedal would deliver a surge of boost along with the sensuous growl of the inline-6.

While boasting excellent performance, the interior instead focused on luxury and comfort, gently enveloping the driver and passengers.

This dichotomy is what makes the Tourer V attractive. It hides its teeth, portraying the image of a refined gentleman. It's discerning drivability sent many car enthusiasts wild.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D4B7:
The Chaser is a medium-sized saloon that shares the same basic construction as the Mark II but offers different exterior stylings. Of the Mark II, Chaser and Cresta sister cars, the Chaser offered the most sporty character and thus became the favorite of driving enthusiasts. The Tourer V is a sports grade model of the Chaser that features a turbocharged engine. The Tourer V grade was also available on the Mark II.

The version shown here is a 6th generation Chaser Tourer V, also known as the X100 series. The engine is a 2nd generation 1JZ-GTE with variable valve timing, and a single turbine turbocharger system which produces a dramatic driving feel. Pressing the throttle pedal delivers a surge of boost and fierce acceleration, while the front-engine rear-wheel drive (FR) layout delivers predictable control characteristics and responsive handling.

While the engine is obviously powerful, it also has excellent reliability leading the Chaser to be lauded as a tuning base car. The more work you put into it, the more intense the driving experience this exceptional FR sedan provides.
